h: Video recordings and the computer link
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: A video of a session: the screen (or a USB camera) with the master's sound, as one MP4 in the library's videos/ folder ( Paths::videos() , /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/videos on the device), or the sound alone as a WAV among the TRACKS ("Audio only" below). The control center's LIVE REC card starts one; while LIVE REC is on, the device's RECORD key starts a recording and STOP ends it, from any page, as the header's ● and ■ do on the screen. SETTINGS · VIDEO has the QUALITY, the TIMER (a countdown before it starts) and the SOURCE; VIDEO SAVED, when a recording ends, sends it to the COMPUTER set up in SETTINGS or copies it TO USB. Code: src/backend/videorecorder.* ( video ), src/backend/audiotap.* , src/backend/computerlink.* ( computer ), qml/components/ComputerPopup.qml , VideoSavedPopup.qml , the VIDEO card in ControlCenter.qml .

h: The rule it is built on
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The sound comes first: a video may cost the audio nothing it can hear, and the audio in the video must never drop. Everything below follows from that.

h: How a recording is made › The sound is tapped, not recorded through AudioLevels
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The sound is tapped, not recorded through AudioLevels. AudioTap is ravving's own JACK client ( ravving-video , stereo in) connected to the master's last outputs (what the speakers get: the LIVE FX inserts included, which the header's ● WAV recording misses). Its process callback copies each cycle into a ring of 2^20 frames (21.8 s at 48 kHz) and touches nothing else; a plain thread drains the ring into a named pipe ( $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ ravving-video-<stamp>.pipe , 1 MB of kernel buffering) as raw 32-bit float stereo. ffmpeg reads the pipe as -f f32le . Why not libzynthbox's AudioLevels (the WAV recorder's and the exporter's path): it runs one recording at a time, and a video session must leave the header's ● and the samplers' record-to-pad free. Why not ffmpeg's own -f jack input: its ring is 16 periods (85 ms at 256 frames), so an encoder or SD-card stall longer than that drops sound; this ring holds 21 seconds, and what it could not hold is counted ( audioDroppedMs , a warning in the issues center) rather than lost quietly.

h: How a recording is made › The picture is ffmpeg's
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The picture is ffmpeg's. x11grab of the display ( -draw_mouse 0 ), or v4l2 of the camera, encoded with libx264 on two threads at nice -n 10 : the Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder (ffmpeg lists h264_v4l2m2m , but the Pi 5's V4L2 nodes are its ISP and HEVC decoder). The tiers, measured below, all run with 0 xruns.

h: How a recording is made › Sync without a shared clock
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: Sync without a shared clock. ffmpeg stamps every grabbed frame with the wall clock ( -use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1 ; on this ffmpeg x11grab's default stamps are the wall clock too). The tap takes the wall-clock moment of its first sample on the audio thread, from the cycle's own start ( jack_get_cycle_times : the cycle began now − (jack_get_time() − cycle_usecs) ago), and ffmpeg is told it with -itsoffset on the audio input. With -copyts both streams sit on the same absolute clock in the file, to the millisecond.

h: How a recording is made › Matroska first, then one remux
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: Matroska first, then one remux. The recording goes to .recording-<stamp>.mkv : a Matroska is readable even if ravving or ffmpeg dies (an MP4 without its index is not). On STOP the tap closes the pipe (ffmpeg's audio input ends), ffmpeg gets SIGINT and finishes its file, and ffprobe reads the two streams' start times: the audio began while ffmpeg was starting (~0.45 s before the first frame), so ffmpeg -ss <video start − audio start> -i rec.mkv -c copy -movflags +faststart cuts the head to the first video frame, writes the MP4 with its index up front and its title / date tags, and the Matroska is removed. The remux copies packets: a few seconds for a long recording ("SAVING" on the card and the plate). If the remux fails the Matroska is kept under the final name. Checked on milo with tools/video-sync-check.sh (the mechanism alone, with a synthetic audio feeder): video − audio in the Matroska 0.466 s (ffmpeg's launch latency), the cut MP4's video at 0.000 s and its audio at 0.003 s (the AAC frame granularity at -c copy ).

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: tools/video-encode-impact.sh : each tier recording the screen while the transport played the open project, tools/audio-impact.sh 20 playing alongside (frames/s is the UI's own rate, which must not fall; "realtime" is ravving's audio threads' CPU; xruns must be 0). tier ffmpeg CPU (of one core) UI frames/s realtime threads xruns frames delivered none (baseline) — 21.5 18 % 0 — full screen 30 fps, ultrafast 35 % 21.1 23 % 0 991 in 33 s (30.0 fps) HIGH : full screen 30 fps, veryfast crf 21 48 % 20.7 23 % 0 976 in 32 s (30.0) MEDIUM : full screen 15 fps, veryfast crf 23 26 % 21.1 21 % 0 496 in 32 s (15.0) LOW : 640 × 400 30 fps, veryfast crf 26 31 % 21.8 23 % 0 1021 in 34 s (30.0) So every tier records at its full frame rate with the audio graph untouched; the realtime threads cost 3–5 points more of CPU under the encoder's memory traffic, and the UI keeps its rate. MEDIUM is the default (the lightest; the screen's text stays sharp at full size). LOW makes the smallest files, not the lightest load (the scale filter costs what the pixels save). The AAC audio is 192 kb/s. File sizes: ~1 MB per 30 s at MEDIUM with a still screen; a busy screen (the playhead, meters, the SONG page's waves) is several times that.

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: SETTINGS · VIDEO · MIC: the RECORDER's input, as it is set up there (MIC / GUITAR / LINE, the jack in use, its GAIN, its effects), mixed into the video's sound. Nothing of the input is repeated for the video: InputRecorder::setListener(ports) adds the tap's two mic ports ( ravving-video:mic_l / mic_r ) as one more destination at the end of the input chain ( JackWiring::setInputChain 's listeners , beside the monitor lane and the take recorder; a mono input feeds both), the input counts as in use while a listener is set (its effects run), and the audio thread adds the ports to the master's sound as the video hears it. The master itself is untouched: the speakers get the mic only with the RECORDER's MONITOR on, in which case the video hears it twice (louder), so one or the other. tools/video-test.sh records once with MIC on and checks the link; tools/video-mic-check.sh is the listening test: a recording with the music stopped while someone speaks, then the file's audio measured. Measured on milo (2026-10-11, a mic on jack 5, the RECORDER on MIC at 30 dB gain): the chain found jack 5 on its own ( capture_FR → mic_l ), the file's audio peaked at −1.4 dBFS, RMS −21.6 dB, the music stopped: the voice, at the gain set on the RECORDER page.

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: A voice over the playing (a tutorial, a jam with talk) was buried: the master plays some 25 dB above a voice at a normal distance, and a plain sum leaves the voice behind it. With MIC on, the tap mixes the two as a voice over ( AudioTap::setVoiceOver , SETTINGS · VIDEO · VOICE): the mic is made crisp: a 120 Hz high-pass and a +4 dB high shelf from 3 kHz (RBJ biquads on the audio thread), then lifted by VOICE LIFT (+6 dB by default, +12 or flat); its envelope is followed (instant attack, 250 ms release); while it is above the voice threshold the master is turned down to VOICE DUCK (−12 dB by default, −6 or −18; 0 is off) in 20 ms and comes back over 600 ms once the voice stops, so the music sits in the background exactly while someone speaks; the threshold follows the music (since 2026-10-12, in place of a fixed −34 dBFS): it is −34 dBFS at least, and 12 dB over what the speakers are expected to leak into the mic right now, i.e. the master's envelope (as ducked) times a leak ratio the tap learns as the mic's level over the master's: down within a second, up over 8 s, never past −26 dB of the master (0.02, −34 dB, to start; from the moment VIDEO is on, since the mic is wired then). A fixed threshold made the beat duck itself through a mic near the speakers and pump as the duck let go and the leak came back over it; against the expected leak, only a voice counts. The learning is slow upwards on purpose: the first cut learned up fast while no voice was heard, and a steady −20 dBFS tone under the threshold became "leak" within a second and never ducked (tools/video-voice-check.sh caught it). What the cap means: a mic that hears the speakers louder than −26 dB of the master (the mic in front of the speaker) still ducks itself, and a leak between the start value and the cap ducks the beat for a second or two at its start, until the ratio has climbed. The RECORDER's GAIN scales the voice and the leak alike, so the ratio holds when it is turned; the sum goes through a look-ahead peak limiter (1 ms ahead, ceiling −1 dBFS, 150 ms release): the mix runs through a 1 ms delay line, the loudest sample in the line sets the gain, which gets down over a quarter of the line, so a hot mic over a loud beat is turned down before the peak comes out, never clipped, and never with the click of a gain step. The first cut (2026-10-12) clamped the sum instead, and a mic peaking near 0 dBFS lifted 6 dB came out as crackle with runs of samples stuck at the ceiling; a limiter without look-ahead replaced it the same day, the look-ahead the day after. The 1 ms sits inside the measured 3 ms of audio offset; the master without the mic is not delayed. The RECORDER's GAIN still sets how hot the voice comes in, and the recorder watches it: while VIDEO is on with MIC the input is wired into the tap at once (not only while recording) and its peak is metered ten times a second ( micLevel , before the lift). SETTINGS · VIDEO shows it on a LEVEL bar with the −6 dB mark, and the project plate carries it standing in its right corner while VIDEO is on (red while hot, a blue dot at its foot while the music ducks). A peak over −6 dBFS within the last two seconds is micHot : the bar turns red and the settings say MIC TOO HOT, turn the GAIN down; a mic peaking around −12 dBFS leaves the mix room and the limiter idle. The voice over is for a voice: with the RECORDER on GUITAR or LINE the input is summed as it is (through the limiter), nothing ducks under a guitar, and the VOICE rows say so. The settings apply at once, on a recording under way too. With DUCK and LIFT both 0 the mix is the plain sum. tools/video-voice-check.sh measures it: a steady 300 Hz tone at −12 dBFS into the tap's master ports as the music (so the measure does not depend on the project open: a sparse beat swings 30 dB inside a second, which hid the duck on 2026-10-12; MUSIC=project plays the project instead), a 1 kHz tone in bursts (tools/tone.py, −20 dBFS, TONE_DB for another level) into the tap's mic ports as the voice; second by second, the music must be DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, the tone must come out LIFT dB louder, the file must show no clipping (its peak under −0.5 dBFS, no run of samples stuck at the ceiling), and the meter must read the tone ( video.micLevel near −20 dBFS while a burst plays, micHot false; a −3 dBFS burst sets micHot ).

h: The hardware keys and the UI
p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: The LIVE REC card (control center): a tap opens the LIVE REC dialog ( LiveRecPopup.qml ): WHAT, a VIDEO (the screen or a USB camera with the master's sound, an MP4 among the VIDEOS) or AUDIO ONLY (the sound alone, a 24-bit WAV among the TRACKS, see below); MIC, the RECORDER's input in the sound; and START, which switches LIVE REC on and begins after the TIMER (the dialog is the confirmation the card asked for with a second tap until 2026-10-12: a stray tap never starts one; the drawer closes first, so it is not in the picture; the TIMER counts down on an overlay that is not recorded either, since ffmpeg starts after it). ◀ ▶ pick WHAT, ▲ ▼ toggle the MIC, SELECT starts. The card reads LIVE REC · READY / REC IN n / REC mm:ss / LIVE REC · SAVING and is lit while LIVE REC is on; a tap while on ends the recording and switches LIVE REC off. A new project (NEW in the project menu) switches LIVE REC off too, a recording under way saved first ( Projects::created ). While VIDEO is on, RECORD and STOP are the video's before any page sees them ( Ravving::handleCuia → VideoRecorder::takesKey ): RECORD starts when idle (a toast says ■ stops when it is already recording), STOP ends the recording (and stops the music with it: the session is over) or cancels the countdown; STOP with nothing recording is the transport's again. The header's ● and ■ do the same ( Session.toggleRecording / Session.stop ). The project plate shows the video's state while VIDEO is on (VIDEO READY · ● RECORDS, VIDEO IN 3, ● REC 01:23, VIDEO · SAVING); the RECORD LED glows dim red when ready, orange during the countdown, red while recording; STOP lights while there is something to end. While a video records, every device key pressed (ALT combos as "ALT + MODE", knob turns as "KNOB 1 ▲", "BIG KNOB ▼") is named in a short red notice at the screen's bottom ( Ravving::keyShown → Main.qml's second Toast), so the video shows what was played; SETTINGS · VIDEO · KEYS turns it off ( video.showKeys , on by default). An audio recording shows none: there is no picture to explain. VIDEO SAVED / LIVE REC SAVED (when a recording ends): the file, its length, size and picture size; DELETE at the left (a ConfirmButton: the second tap within three seconds removes the file, VideoRecorder::remove ), RENAME and SEND… at the right (SendPopup: a USB stick's ravving/videos or ravving/exports , a computer, the phone); an audio recording also has METADATA… (below). A failure (ffmpeg missing, no space, the encoder giving no frames in 12 s, ffmpeg dying) is a toast, an issues-center entry and video.error ; what ffmpeg wrote before dying is still saved when it has frames.

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: LIVE REC's AUDIO ONLY ( video.mode "audio", VideoRecorder::audioOnly ) is the same recorder without the picture: the tap feeds ffmpeg as before, but the command has no video input and no encoder, only -c:a pcm_s24le -f wav into .recording-<name>.wav in the exports folder ( Paths::exports() , the TRACKS the music player and FILES list), so nothing is encoded and nothing has to be lined up (no -copyts , no -itsoffset ). The first bytes out (ffmpeg's out_time_us in the progress report) stand for the first frame; stopping renames the WAV to <project> - <date>.wav (no remux, nothing to cut: the sound begins where it began). The MIC, the voice over and the limiter apply as to a video. The key notices are not shown. When it ends, LIVE REC SAVED offers, besides DELETE, RENAME and SEND…, METADATA…: the export dialog over the file ( ExportPopup.openForFile , the same form without WHAT and the lengths; SAVE WITH TAGS), which calls Exporter::finishRecording(rawFile, metadata) : the WAV is written whole in the FORMAT chosen (WAV 24-bit, FLAC, OGG, MP3) under the NAME given in the exports folder, tagged with the TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, GENRE, COMPOSER and COMMENT, its cover drawn and saved beside it, its sidecar JSON written, the raw WAV removed, and the files copied to the stick or sent to the computer picked. That is the track export's own finishing ( Exporter::writeAndTag , shared since 2026-10-12: one path for both), so a live recording and an exported track are the same kind of file afterwards. The tagged track then stands for the recording in LIVE REC SAVED ( VideoRecorder::adopt ), so RENAME and SEND… act on it. Without METADATA… the plain WAV stays, playable and listed as any track. tools/video-test.sh has the audio checks: a recording in AUDIO ONLY mode lands as a WAV among the TRACKS, ffprobe sees one audio stream of the right length, finishRecording over the fifo writes the FLAC with its cover and sidecar and takes the WAV away.

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: SETTINGS · COMPUTERS holds the laptops or PCs exports and videos can be sent to over SSH: any number ( Computers , computers , a list of ComputerLink s, each its own group computers/<id> of the settings file; a set-up from before the list is moved into c1 ). ADD A COMPUTER asks for the host name or address, the user there, and that user's password; a computer already in the list as the same user@host is set up again rather than added twice. The password is used once: it opens the first connection so the device's own key ( ~/.config/ravving/ssh/id_ed25519 , made on the first CONNECT) can be installed with ssh-copy-id ; it is never written to the settings. The password reaches ssh through SSH_ASKPASS (a helper script of ravving's printing a file readable by root alone, made for the set-up's seconds and removed after, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force so no terminal is involved). The computer's host key is kept in ravving's own known_hosts (accepted on the first connection, refused if it changes; FORGET removes that computer's entry with ssh-keygen -R , the others stay). The Downloads folder is asked of the computer ( xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD , else ~/Downloads ); files go there with scp , one at a time ( busy / phase / progress ), and sent(ok, count, label) ends it with a toast. Statuses: unset, setting-up, ready, unreachable, refused (the key no longer accepted: CONNECT AGAIN with the password), failed ( error says why: a wrong password, a name that does not resolve, SSH refused or no answer, a changed host key). Where it is used: one standard SEND… button ( SendPopup , the destinations there are: every writable USB stick's ravving/ folder through RemovableDrives::copyFiles , each computer, and a phone by QR code: see "Sending to a phone" in README.md) in the FILES browser (every kind: a project is bundled for the destination by Exporter::exportProjectFile , a preset written out as one JSON file by FileBrowser::presetFile ), on VIDEO SAVED, on each track in the music player, in the pattern presets dialog and the sound picker; and the export dialog's COMPUTER row (a chip per computer, one lit), which sends a new track or bundle as soon as it is written ( Exporter::sendToComputer , the metadata's computer = the computer's id). The computer needs an SSH server: Linux openssh-server (Arch: systemctl enable --now sshd ), macOS "Remote Login"; Windows' OpenSSH server has no $HOME/Downloads in its default shell and is not supported.

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: Tool What it does tools/video-test.sh the feature suite on the device (41 checks, all PASS on milo 2026-10-11): a recording over the fifo while playing, the MP4's streams, starts, length and frame rate, the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the device keys (the music goes on), the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off, the computer link's state tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (21 checks, all PASS on milo 2026-10-11): a throwaway local user stands in for the computer (set up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent and compared, the key removed → refused); the user is removed and the previous computer put back tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share from the laptop (31 checks, all PASS on milo 2026-10-11): the newest video offered over the fifo, fetched with curl and compared (size, md5), a Range → 206, HEAD, 404s, the deliveries counted, stop → connection refused tools/video-mic-check.sh [SECONDS] a recording with the mic while the music is stopped, its audio measured (speak when told) tools/video-sync-check.sh the sync mechanism alone (a synthetic audio feeder + x11grab + the remux), PASS when both streams start together tools/video-encode-impact.sh [SECONDS] the tiers' cost while playing (the table above); mirror any change to the encoder arguments here and re-measure Scripts: set video countdown 0 , call video start , get video state , call video stop , get video lastFile , get video lastInfo , call video toggle , set video quality high , set video source camera , get video cameras ; call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , call computer check , call computer send /path/file , call computer forget .

p: Video recordings and the computer link
t: No probing on the pipe input ( -probesize 32 -analyzeduration 0 before its -i ): with ffmpeg's defaults, avformat_find_stream_info reads 5 s of the raw audio before the output is opened, so the first progress report (and ravving's "recording" state) came 6 s after the launch, while 75 raw frames (4 MB each) piled up in the video input's queue meanwhile. Measured: the first frame= report at 5.1 s with the defaults, 1.8 s without probing; the picture itself starts 0.5 s after the launch either way (the x264 lookahead and the stats period account for the rest). The video input's queue is 64 frames for the same reason. -t and -copyts do not mix: ffmpeg's -t compares against the absolute timestamps, so a recording limited with -t ends at once. Recordings are ended with SIGINT (once; a second signal makes ffmpeg quit without its trailer: -nostdin , and never timeout -s INT in a non-interactive shell, which sent two). The wall clock: a step of the system clock during a recording (the Pi has no RTC; timesyncd steps it on the first network sync after boot) puts a jump in the video's timestamps (a freeze for a forward step; dropped frames for a backward one). Start recording once the device has been online for a moment. A test that pkill -f s a script by name over ssh kills the ssh command line itself when it carries that name (every command after it is lost without a word): pkill -x ffmpeg , and patterns that cannot match the caller. ffprobe on a Matroska written with -copyts reports the absolute starts (epoch seconds); avg_frame_rate is right, nb_frames is N/A (count with -count_frames ). The AAC encoder's priming frame puts the audio stream's start 21 ms before the first sample; the remux reads the stream starts from the file, so the cut is consistent with it. The screen recording shows exactly what is on the display: a dialog opened during the recording is in the picture; the countdown overlay and the drawer are not (both are gone before ffmpeg starts). Camera: USB cameras are found in /sys/class/video4linux (the node with index 0 on a USB device); the capture size follows the tier (640 × 480 for LOW, 1280 × 720 otherwise). Not tested yet: no camera was at hand (2026-10-11). Streaming later: the same tap, encoder, tiers, keys and UI would feed -f flv rtmp://… (YouTube, Twitch, an OBS on the computer) instead of the Matroska; what is new there is the network sink and a bitrate budget for Wi-Fi, not the capture.

Ravving has one undo history for the project, History ( src/backend/history.* ), published to QML as studio.history . Everything that can be undone goes through it; nothing keeps an undo stack of its own.

Today the patterns : every machine's notes, steps, chords, slots, accents, slides, lengths, automation, live timing and its preset's name ( Machine::historyState() ). Not the sound (source, factory sound, MODS), the mix (level, pan, mute), the effects or the project's settings (tempo, swing, key): those were left out on purpose (2026-10-09). Anything can join later by becoming a participant (below). And the arrangement ( Sections::historyState() , "SECTIONS", 2026-10-10): which sections there are, in which order, their names, colours and lengths, and the song. A section removed is put aside with its content ( Sections::m_removed ), so undoing the removal brings it back whole, in its place and in the song; redoing it hands over to the neighbour as REMOVE did. What is not in it: the section on screen (a pick is no step, so an undo never switches what plays; a section added and then undone is the one exception, the first section takes over) and the machines' content (theirs). The removed sections are forgotten when a project is opened.

What it undoes Where The timeline the project's last step, whichever machines it touched the header's ↶ ↷, ALT + ◀ ▶ on the machine pages; a toast names it ("UNDO · CHORDS + BASS") One machine that machine's last change only, wherever it is in the timeline the pattern toolbar's ↶ ↷ ( machine.undo() / redo() , machine.canUndo / canRedo ) A machine can go back on its own because the participants' states are independent of each other: putting back the bass's last pattern cannot break the chords'.

h: What becomes one step › One turn of the event loop
t: One turn of the event loop. Everything recorded before control goes back to the event loop is one step. An action that changes several machines at once is undone in one go without any call: CLEAR (every machine), a key change that snaps the bass and the lead into the new key.

h: What becomes one step › Quick changes of one participant
t: Quick changes of one participant. A change within History::MergeMs (500 ms) of the same participant's last one joins its step: a knob turning, a handle dragged, a SELECT move repeated.

h: What becomes one step › A group
t: A group. Everything between begin(label) and end() (they nest), for an action spread over several turns. Machines also have their own groups for a recorded take ( Machine::beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() ): the take is recorded once, at its end. A step stores, for each participant it touched, the state before and after; nothing else. The history keeps History::Depth (100) steps.

forget(participant) : its state was replaced wholesale, so its steps go (a section picked: undoing into a section that is not on screen would be a surprise; an engine attached again). clear() : a project opened or NEW ( Studio::applyProjectState() ).

C++ ( History ): add(p) / remove(p) register a participant (its state now is where it starts) / take it out record(p) after each change: a step, or part of the open one, when its state differs forget(p) , clear() see above undo() , redo() , canUndo , canRedo , undoText , redoText the timeline undoIn(key) , redoIn(key) , canUndoIn(key) , canRedoIn(key) one participant begin(label) , end() a group signals changed() , undone(what) , redone(what) QML: studio.history.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo , .undoText , .redoText , .begin() , .end() , .clear() ; a machine's own: machine.undo() , .redo() , .canUndo , .canRedo .

Implement HistoryParticipant (four functions): - historyKey() : a name unique among the participants ("bass", "song"); - historyLabel() : how the user reads a step of it ("BASS", "SONG"); - historyState() : its state as plain data, equal when nothing that matters changed (leave out what only says what is on screen: a bar shown, a tab); - applyHistoryState(state) : become that state (it may emit its change signals as usual: the history does not record what it puts back). Register it: studio.history → history->add(this) once it exists (Studio does it for the machines, Machine::setHistory() ). Call history->record(this) after each change the user makes (a machine does it on its edited() signal). Changes that are not the user's (a state restored, a project loaded) call forget(this) instead. Its own ↶ ↷, if it has any, call history->undoIn(key) / redoIn(key) ; their enabled state is canUndoIn(key) / canRedoIn(key) , refreshed on changed() . Nothing else: the timeline, the grouping, the toasts and the header's buttons come with it.

historyState() is computed after every change, so keep it cheap (a map of the content); the machines' is their contentState() less the sound and the view. One machine's undo clears the timeline's redo (what it would redo no longer matches what is there); the timeline's undo of a step a machine was part of is redone by that machine's ↷ too (it falls back to the timeline's redo).

Ravving's Bluetooth does what a phone's does: pair, connect, send a file, play through a speaker or headphones, receive a file. This page records what a Zynthbox needs for that to work at all (a stock image cannot even start the Bluetooth service), how the pieces fit, how to test them, and what to look at when something fails.

h: What the stock image lacks, and the fix
t: Found on milo (Zynthbox on a Raspberry Pi 5, Debian 13, BlueZ 5.82, PipeWire 1.4.2, WirePlumber 0.5.8), 2026-10-08: Problem Cause Fix (shipped by ravving) bluetooth.service fails at boot (status 203/EXEC), the adapter stays DOWN, the control center says "its service is not running" zynthian-sys's drop-in /etc/systemd/system/bluetooth.service.d/01-disable-sap-plugin.conf starts /usr/lib/bluetooth/bluetoothd , which Debian 13 moved to /usr/libexec/bluetooth/ data/systemd/50-ravving-bluetoothd-path.conf , installed to the same drop-in folder: the same flags ( --compat --experimental --noplugin=sap ) with the path that exists a speaker or headphones pair but will not connect: org.bluez.Error.Failed br-connection-profile-unavailable ; the adapter's UUIDs ( bluetoothctl show ) list no Audio Source / Audio Sink WirePlumber's Bluetooth monitor ( monitors/bluez.lua ) waits for a logind "active" seat before creating the BlueZ handle that registers the A2DP endpoints; the root startx session never reports one, so the monitor never starts and BlueZ has nothing to connect the device to data/wireplumber/50-ravving-bluetooth.conf , installed to /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ : wireplumber.profiles.main.monitor.bluez.seat-monitoring = disabled no audio over Bluetooth at all libspa-0.2-bluetooth (PipeWire's A2DP / HFP plugin with the SBC, aptX, FastStream, LDAC codecs) is not installed apt install libspa-0.2-bluetooth , then a WirePlumber restart (it loads the plugin at start) no file transfer bluez-obexd (the OBEX daemon, obex.service in the user session, D-Bus activated as org.bluez.obex ) is not installed apt install bluez-obexd the Qt side ravving links KDE's BluezQt ( libkf6bluezqt6 , present on the image; libkf6bluezqt-dev to build) — tools/bluetooth-setup.sh does all of it on a device and checks every step ( --check only checks); cmake --install puts the two drop-ins in place as well. After the setup bluetoothctl show lists Audio Source, Audio Sink, Handsfree and Handsfree Audio Gateway.

Backend Bluetooth ( src/backend/bluetooth.* , QML bluetooth ), on BluezQt: the adapter (power, discovery, discoverable for three minutes), the devices (connected first, then paired, then by signal; private-address phones without a name hidden until paired), a pairing Agent (DisplayYesNo: a passkey to confirm or a PIN to type lands in pairing , answered with answerPairing ), pair → trust → connect, forget, OBEX Object Push sending ( sendFile , progress in transfer ), an ObexAgent accepting pushes into the library's incoming/ folder, and the audio switch ( useAsOutput ).

Audio. When an audio device connects, WirePlumber makes a sink node bluez_output.<address>.1 (and an input / capture node for HFP). useAsOutput hands it to AudioOutputs ( outputs , also the control center's AUDIO OUTPUT card), which does not make it the default sink: that would clock the whole JACK graph by the Bluetooth transport in 256-frame chunks (glitches, measured on milo with the Sony WH-CH720N) and leave the master's links to the jacks in place (sound from both). Instead the jacks keep the clock, a pw-loopback of ravving's own ( ravving-out , a virtual sink whose playback stream targets the Bluetooth sink with a 2048-frame buffer) is started, the master's two output ports are linked to it with pw-link (its inputs have no JACK name, so libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler cannot) and the jack links are dropped. Measured: the Bluetooth node runs at 48 kHz SBC, the HiFiBerry node goes idle, the sound is clean and the jacks silent. Off, on disconnect, forget or exit, the loopback stops and the jack links come back.

Files. Sending opens an OBEX session ( Target: opp ) and pushes the file; receiving needs milo VISIBLE (discoverable + pairable, three minutes) and lands under library/incoming/ , which PROJECT ▾ → IMPORT lists as "received" and the music library as the album "Received".
UI. BluetoothPopup from the control center's BLUETOOTH card.

The basic checks: sh tools/bluetooth-setup.sh --check . With a device at hand, over the fifo ( docs/testing.md ): tools/device.sh call bluetooth startDiscovery; sleep 10; tools/device.sh get bluetooth devices tools/device.sh call bluetooth pair 84:D3:52:35:80:99 # a speaker pairs without a prompt tools/device.sh get bluetooth pairing # a phone: {kind confirm, passkey} → answerPairing true tools/device.sh call bluetooth useAsOutput 84:D3:52:35:80:99 true tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED # heard on the speaker tools/device.sh call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF "/zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/exports/Lo-fi Say It.wav" What to measure (the user's QA notes, 2026-10-08): Metric How, on the device signal (RSSI, dBm: −30 excellent, −67…−70 good, below −80 drops) bluetoothctl info ADDR (RSSI while scanning), hcitool rssi ADDR once connected link quality / packet loss hcitool lq ADDR (255 = best); btmon -w /tmp/bt.snoop during playback and count retransmissions A2DP codec and latency pw-cli info <bluez sink id> ( api.bluez5.codec : SBC by default, aptX / LDAC when both sides have it); pw-top for the sink node's quantum and the graph's (the studio stays at 256 / 48000; the Bluetooth node runs its own) OBEX throughput transfer.transferred over time ( get bluetooth transfer ) what BlueZ sees btmon (HCI trace), busctl --system tree org.bluez , journalctl -u bluetooth what WirePlumber does journalctl --user -u wireplumber , with systemctl --user set-environment WIREPLUMBER_DEBUG=3 and a restart for the monitor's own lines

Sony WH-CH720N (84:D3:52:35:80:99), paired and connected, playing through the loopback route; the adapter is the Pi's own ( hci0 , UART, BCM43455 class 0x6c0000). The tools are hcitool , l2ping , busctl (BlueZ's D-Bus objects) and pw-dump , all on the image. What Command Result link quality hcitool lq <addr> 255 / 255 (the best the firmware reports) RSSI hcitool rssi <addr> 0 (the firmware reports "in the golden range", not dBm) transmit power hcitool tpl <addr> 12 dBm adaptive hopping hcitool afh <addr> 30 of 79 channels in use (the Wi-Fi band is cut out) round trip l2ping -c 5 <addr> 18.7 ms, 0 % loss codec negotiated pw-dump → api.bluez5.codec sbc ; busctl … MediaTransport1 Configuration = 17 21 2 53 : 48 kHz joint stereo, 16 blocks, 8 subbands, loudness, bitpool 2–53 (SBC "high quality", ~345 kb/s) codecs the device offers the device's sep* endpoints ( MediaEndpoint1 Codec ) 0 = SBC, 2 = AAC; the image has no AAC plugin (Debian ships none), it has aptX, LDAC, LC3, Opus, FastStream for devices with those SBC-XQ ravving's WirePlumber drop-in sets bluez5.enable-sbc-xq a second profile a2dp-sink-sbc_xq appears ( wpctl set-profile <dev> <index> to use it, bitpool up to 76, ~550 kb/s); WirePlumber still picks plain a2dp-sink by default transport delay MediaTransport1 Delay 14 (1/10 ms; what the headphones claim, a nominal value) playback buffer the loopback's node.latency 2048 / 48000 = 43 ms before the codec; the headphones add their own (SBC devices are typically 150–250 ms end to end) xruns over 20 s of a full project pw-top ERR on the bluez sink before / after 19 / 19 (none new); the HiFiBerry node idle, the graph's quantum stays 256 battery bluetoothctl info → Battery Percentage reported (70 %) Not measured yet: OBEX throughput (needs a phone), end-to-end audio latency (needs a microphone at the headphones: play a click through the route and record it). Two traps found while testing: - A scan starves the audio link. The Pi has one radio for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi; a discovery (inquiry) while headphones play makes the sound break up, and a long one gets the headphones dropped. The dialog therefore scans for 12 s only ( DiscoverySeconds ) and does not scan on its own while an audio device is connected: SCAN is the user's call then. - A dual-mode speaker found by its LE advertisement pairs the wrong side. The LG S20A advertises LE Audio (Audio Stream Control, Published Audio Capabilities, Telephony and Media Audio) as well as classic A2DP; paired from the LE advertisement it had no Audio Sink UUID, PipeWire made no sink for it, and ravving offered no PLAY THROUGH. BlueZ can play LE Audio only with its experimental features on and a kernel with ISO sockets, and the Pi's firmware has none, so ravving scans classic (BR/EDR) only ( setDiscoveryFilter {Transport: bredr} ), where the A2DP side pairs. By hand: bluetoothctl remove <addr> , bluetoothctl scan bredr , pair again. - A WirePlumber restart leaves a connected device on the headset profile only (the A2DP endpoints are registered after the device reconnected): bluetoothctl disconnect then connect , and the a2dp-sink profile is back. Also seen at connect time (2026-10-11, the WH-CH720N): bluetoothd logs a2dp_select_capabilities() Unable to select SEP and the device offers only headset-head-unit (mono, 16 kHz): the sink is playback_MONO . ravving's output loopback mixes down to it (it once linked only the left channel: a track panned fully to one side went silent); disconnect and connect for stereo. - SBC-XQ is offered, not chosen. With bluez5.enable-sbc-xq = true the WH-CH720N lists a2dp-sink-sbc_xq beside a2dp-sink (plain SBC), but WirePlumber connects with plain SBC. ravving switches it: SETTINGS · BLUETOOTH · SBC-XQ (on by default, AudioOutputs.preferSbcXq) sets the output in use to SBC-XQ when it offers it, or back to plain SBC when off, once per connection ( wpctl set-profile <device id> <index> ; WirePlumber kept no profile for it). The switch replaces the sink node under the same name; ravving routes to it again (AudioOutputs notices the node id changing). Measured: the WH-CH720N plays SBC-XQ cleanly (2026-10-11).

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10)
t: The user's report: the Sony WH-CH720N headphones connect every time; the LG speaker is "flaky", and after a night idle it reconnects at once from a phone but not from milo. Read with tools/device.sh bt (journals of 2026-10-08 to 10-10; milo: BlueZ 5.82, PipeWire 1.4.2, WirePlumber 0.5.8).

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › The two devices
t: The two devices. LG SJ1(D8) 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 Sony WH-CH720N 84:D3:52:35:80:99 radio BR/EDR only (not the dual-mode LG S20A of the trap above) BR/EDR + LE profiles A2DP sink, AVRCP (no HFP) A2DP sink, AVRCP, HFP, HSP, Sony's own codecs (BlueZ's endpoint cache) 01=01:00:00:3fff0241 : one sink endpoint, SBC only SBC, AAC (no AAC plugin on Debian: plays SBC ) record paired, bonded, trusted paired, bonded, trusted who connects milo must page it the headphones page milo themselves at power-on

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › What happened
t: What happened. Every one of the LG's 11 tries failed; none opened an A2DP transport. Nine went like this, with the Sony connected and playing (since 01:39) the whole time: 03:48:03 ravving: bluetooth: BLUETOOTH CONNECTED · LG SJ1(D8) 03:48:03 bluetoothd: profiles/audio/a2dp.c:a2dp_select_capabilities() Unable to select SEP 03:48:03 kf.bluezqt: PendingCall Error: "br-connection-create-socket" 03:48:03 ravving: bluetooth: COULD NOT CONNECT · LG SJ1(D8) · br-connection-create-socket 03:48:04 ravving: bluetooth: BLUETOOTH DISCONNECTED · LG SJ1(D8) 03:48:20 ravving: bluetooth: NO AUDIO FROM · LG SJ1(D8) (03:48:03, 03:48:08, 03:48:44, 03:49:18, 03:49:21, 03:49:38, 03:49:43, 03:49:55, 03:58:09.) The link comes up, so the speaker answered, but its audio is refused. The other two were page timeouts, where the speaker never answered (off, in standby, or held by the phone): 2026-10-08 16:00:49 bluetoothd: avdtp_connect_cb() connect to 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8: Host is down (112) 2026-10-08 16:00:49 ravving: bluetooth: COULD NOT CONNECT · LG SJ1(D8) · br-connection-page-timeout 2026-10-10 03:51:40 (the same) ravving tried once each time and gave up. WirePlumber logged nothing for the LG: it never got a transport to make a sink from.

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › Why
t: Why. BlueZ keeps its local A2DP stream endpoints (SEPs) per adapter, shared by every device ( a2dp.c : server->seps ), and a local SEP carries one stream at a time ( avdtp.c : lsep->info.inuse is set by avdtp_set_configuration and cleared only in stream_free ; avdtp_find_remote_sep skips an in-use SEP). PipeWire registers one endpoint per codec, and SBC-XQ reuses the SBC one ( a2dp-codec-sbc.c : .endpoint_name = "sbc" ), so milo has exactly one SBC source endpoint ( /MediaEndpoint/A2DPSource/sbc ). The Sony streams SBC through it. The LG takes nothing but SBC. So while the Sony plays, BlueZ finds no free SEP for the LG ("Unable to select SEP"), the connection fails with create-socket, and retrying cannot help. The Sony looked reliable because it was the device already holding the endpoint, and because headphones page their last host themselves. A phone has no such conflict because it plays to one audio device at a time and lets the previous one go. The "after a night" case also needs milo to page: a speaker that wakes up pages its last host only, and that was the phone. Configuration cannot give a second SBC endpoint. An AAC plugin would let the Sony use AAC and free SBC, but Debian ships none ( libfdk-aac is non-free). What ravving does now ( src/backend/bluetooth.cpp ):

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › Hand-over
t: Hand-over. When a device answered but could not connect while another audio device is connected, ravving lets the other device go. It shows SWITCHING FROM · the other , disconnects it, waits 1 s for BlueZ to free the endpoint and connects again. The sound falls back to the jacks in between, and PLAY THROUGH then routes to the new device. Only a connection the user asked for does this; ravving's own reconnect never takes the link from a playing device.

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › Pages retried
t: Pages retried. A page timeout ( Host is down ) is retried after 2, 5 and 10 s. That is about 37 s with BlueZ's 5.12 s page, and the row reads "waking…". Disconnecting or forgetting the device stops it. Only then does COULD NOT CONNECT appear, with a hint: NOT ANSWERING: OFF, ASLEEP OR WITH A PHONE?

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › PLAY THROUGH waits for the connection
t: PLAY THROUGH waits for the connection. It used to start its 15 s sink poll at the same moment as the connect, so a slow connection ended in NO AUDIO FROM. Now the poll starts once the connection is made.

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › The kept output comes back
t: The kept output comes back. AudioOutputs keeps the Bluetooth address of the output picked. When Bluetooth comes on (a start, the switch), that device is connected once, 3 s later, if it is paired and nothing else plays. ravving never repeats this in a loop: paging a speaker in standby wakes it up (LG's Bluetooth standby), so a loop would keep switching on a speaker that went to sleep. Device settings proposed (not applied; they need a bluetoothd / WirePlumber restart, which drops the audio). In order of value: Applied on milo (2026-10-10): FastConnectable = true in /etc/bluetooth/main.conf ( btmgmt info lists fast-connectable ), and bluetooth.autoswitch-to-headset-profile = false , now part of data/wireplumber/50-ravving-bluetooth.conf (installed with ravving). The main.conf line is a device setting (BlueZ reads no drop-in folder): set it by hand on a new image. /etc/bluetooth/main.conf , under [General] : FastConnectable = true . milo then scans for pages more often, so a speaker or headphones paging milo (their last host, waking up) connect within a fraction of a second instead of waiting up to the default 1.28 s scan window. The cost is power, which does not matter on a Pi. /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/51-ravving-a2dp-only.conf : wireplumber.settings = { bluetooth.autoswitch-to-headset-profile = false } Today it is true , and WirePlumber exposes bluez_input.<addr> for the Sony: anything that records from it switches the headphones to HFP (mono, 16 kHz) and their A2DP sink goes away. This does nothing for the LG, which has no HFP. It belongs in data/wireplumber/50-ravving-bluetooth.conf once tested. 3. /etc/bluetooth/main.conf , under [BR] : PageTimeout = 16384 (10.24 s against the default 8192 = 5.12 s). Do this only if a capture ( device.sh bt capture ) shows the speaker answering just after 5.12 s. Each page holds the shared radio for that long. 4. Leave [Policy] ReconnectAttempts / ReconnectIntervals at their defaults (7; 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 s). They act on a link lost by timeout only, not on a speaker that went to standby and disconnected cleanly. JustWorksRepairing does not matter for a bonded device.

h: One audio device at a time (the LG speaker against the Sony, 2026-10-10) › To confirm on milo
t: To confirm on milo. With the Sony connected and playing, open BLUETOOTH, tap the LG and press PLAY THROUGH (or device.sh call bluetooth useAsOutput 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 true ). Expected: SWITCHING FROM · WH-CH720N, the Sony disconnects, then BLUETOOTH CONNECTED · LG, PLAYING THROUGH · LG SJ1(D8), and the journal shows a sep…/fd… ready for dev_6C_5A_B5_49_35_D8 . device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 -1h should tally an A2DP transport opened. Then switch the LG off (or let it sleep), press PLAY THROUGH again, and switch it on during the "waking…" phase: it should connect on a later page. Finally, with the LG as the output, restart ravving with the Sony off: the LG should come back on its own about 3 s after the start.

Symptom Look at Likely control center: "its service is not running" / bluetooth.state unavailable systemctl status bluetooth → 203/EXEC the bluetoothd path drop-in missing (run the setup) the adapter shows but Powered: no after a power on rfkill list (soft blocked), bluetoothctl power on rfkill: rfkill unblock bluetooth the link comes up, then COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-create-socket and DISCONNECTED a second later journalctl -u bluetooth : Unable to select SEP ; device.sh bt ADDR another audio device streams the same codec (SBC): one local endpoint per codec. Disconnect it; ravving hands the link over itself when you connect from the dialog COULD NOT CONNECT · br-connection-page-timeout (bluetoothd: Host is down ) is the device on, in Bluetooth mode, not connected to a phone? device.sh bt capture while connecting it did not answer the page; ravving pages it again for about 37 s ("waking…"). Everything a finger does on the device, a script can do through the remote-control fifo ( docs/testing.md ): load samples, write patterns, pick sounds, set the key and the tempo, save the result as a project. tools/examples/five-am/ (the 5AM demo: sections and the song by script, build.py writing the lines, run.sh sending them) and tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh are complete ones (a third, "Autumn Leaves", is kept outside the repo in ~/Coding/ravving-projects/autumn-leaves/ : its theme is transcribed from the user's own sheet, a generator in Python writing the fifo lines), the lo-fi hip hop project built on the changes of "Say It (Over and Over Again)"; copy it for the next one. This page is the recipe and what we learned writing it.

FIFO=/tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo send() { timeout 2 sh -c "echo \"$1\" > $FIFO"; sleep 0.2; } call() { local line="call"; for a in "$@"; do line="$line|$a"; done; send "$line"; } setp() { send "set|$1|$2|$3"; } get() { send "get|$1|$2"; journalctl --user -u ravving --since '-5s' --no-pager | grep 'fifo get' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*= //'; } A script runs on the device (copy it there, as the example does with itself); every call is one line on the fifo and takes about a fifth of a second, so a full project is a few hundred lines and a couple of minutes. tools/device.sh call|set|get do the same one at a time from the laptop.

Step Calls keep what is there, start clean get studio.projects dirty , call studio.projects saveAs NAME ; call studio.projects newProject tempo, swing, key set studio bpm 74 , set studio swing 0.58 (and set studio swingEighths true for jazz: the off-beat 8ths swing, not the 16ths; the header's SWING 8 / 16, tapped), call header setKey ROOT SCALE (root 0–11 from C, scale an index into Rave.scales: 0 natural minor, 1 major, 2 Dorian…). NEW resets the key to C minor : set it before writing anything in a key drums call drumsN clear , call drumsN toggleStep ROW STEP , toggleAccent STEP ; rows by get drumsN rows ; call drumsN saveAsPreset keeps the beat as "My Beat N" chords set chords bars 8 (the most a pattern holds), set chords viewBar B , then per step call chords setStepNotes STEP "48,52,55,58" (MIDI notes; a note outside the key makes the voicing chromatic). A run of the same voicing on consecutive steps is one held chord ; an empty step ends it. Diatonic shortcuts: setChord STEP DEGREE , or SLOTS: assignSlot SLOT DEGREE + cycleSlotBars SLOT . saveAsPreset keeps a chart as "My Progression N" (a longer form = several presets to switch between) bass, lead set bass bars 8 , set bass viewBar B , call bass setNote STEP NOTE (MIDI; C2 = 36 for the bass, C4 = 60 for the lead, see kits.json baseNote ), setNoteLength STEP STEPS (a note lasts one step unless set: a half note is 8, up to 64, into the next bars), toggleAccent STEP , toggleSlide STEP ; any note is accepted, in the key or not, and a preset keeps it exactly (the chart's ALTER and HOLD lanes) drum kits call drums1 loadKit PATH : a kit file, or a preset inside a soundfont with chosen rows ( …/FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3#128:32?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 , the Jazz kit with its ride and hi-hat foot; docs/engines.md); call drumsN setRowLevel ROW 0..1 sounds call bass chooseSoundSource Upright (names from get bass soundSources ), call chords loadSoundPreset NAME for TAL's factory sounds, call bass.sound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 for the synth's own SOUND MODIFIERS pads call pads clearPad N , call pads loadSample N PATH [start length] , call pads chopRegions N COUNT FIRSTPAD , set pads selectedPad N + call pads setValue MIX VOLUME 0.95 , set pads bars 8 , set pads viewBar B + toggleStep PAD STEP ; a long one-shot (a 16 s intro) needs a loop long enough not to retrigger it: 8 bars at 74 BPM is 26 s SAMPLE KING call sampler loadSample SLOT PATH ; set ravving samplerMachine 1 puts the pads on key 5 save call studio.projects saveAs NAME (a name typed in the dialog would do the same); get studio.projects current to check sections and the song the section on screen is what the calls above edit; call studio.sections rename s1 DROP , duplicate s1 (a copy, placed after the section ON SCREEN, which it becomes), setBars ID 1–8 , set MACHINE paused true (it rests in this section), move FROM TO (the list), removeFromSong 0 / appendToSong ID / setRepeats INDEX N (the song), set studio.sections mode 1 (SONG), pick ID (the one on screen when saved)

A loop in the shell that reads a file line by line and calls tools/device.sh loses all but the first line: the ssh inside reads the loop's stdin. Send the lines from one script on the device (run.sh) or use ssh -n . Soundfont programs: a soundfont's presets are not always at program 0. ACBass.sf3 has its one bass at bank 0 program 3; read the phdr chunk (a few lines of Python) before trusting a number. General MIDI sets ( FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 ) follow the GM numbers. Solos survive: a machine stays silent while another is soloed, by script too. Check the header before concluding an engine is broken. Hearing it from the laptop: tools/meter.py on TrackPassthrough:Channel<track+1>-lane1-dryOutLeft gives RMS and brightness per machine; compare before and after a change. Jazz swings the 8ths: PatternModel's swing moves the odd 16ths only, so ravving swings 8ths itself through each note's delay ( Machine::setEighthSwing ). Measured on milo at 100 BPM, full swing: the ride's off-beat 448–453 ms after the beat, 149 ms before the next (75 / 25), against 300 / 300 straight. A melody needs lengths: a bass or lead note is one step unless setNoteLength says more (a sax's whole note held over the bar line is 19 steps); the roll draws the tail and a long press on a cell stretches the row's note before it up to there. The melody of a published tune is someone else's: chord changes are fine to use, the written melody is not something to copy into a project.

Seventeen genre packs plus the jazz pack: classical, hip-hop, pop, rock, trap, reggaeton, punk, tropical, cumbia, folk, heavy metal, black metal, post-punk, Gregorian (old gothic), vuelo (Flight Facilities' nu-disco), solos (six ballad solos after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker) and bebop (six fast horn solos after Parker, Coltrane and Baker: the first Solos pack). Each has five pattern presets for each of the drums, the bass, the lead and the chords (solos and bebop six). A smaller style pack, piig, has three of each. They are not installed with ravving. To play one, copy a pack's ravving folder to the root of a USB stick: the presets dialog's SOURCE · USB plays them straight from there ( PresetExchange::stickPatterns / loadStickPattern ), and the USB page can import them. data/secret/<genre>-presets/build.py the generator (python3 build.py) data/secret/<genre>-presets/ravving/presets/<drums|bass|lead|chords>/patterns/<Genre> · <Name>.json data/secret/patternkit.py shared by the genre build.py files (not the jazz one) data/secret/validate.py checks every pack against ravving's parsers Each file is {"ravving": "preset", "type": "pattern", "library": "<x>-presets.json", "preset": {"name", "genre", "chart", "sound"}} . The chart is the shipped libraries' format. sound is the sound the pattern was written for: {"soundSource": …} for the bass, lead and chords, {"kit": …} for the drums (a subset of Machine::soundState() ).

h: The genre packs › The notes are scale degrees
t: The notes are scale degrees. They follow the session's root and scale. Each genre is written for one scale, so its four instruments play together: Natural Minor: hip-hop, trap, reggaeton, piig, heavy metal, black metal, post-punk, vuelo. Major: classical, pop, rock, punk, tropical, cumbia, folk, solos, bebop. Dorian: Gregorian. Tropical's minor styles (salsa, bachata) and cumbia's (villera, chicha) sit on degree 6, the relative minor, so each pack stays in one key. In C major they play in A minor. Notes from outside the scale use ALTER (for example rock's ♭3/♭7, trap's ♭2 and raised 7th). Chords from outside the key use chromatic c voicings. Tempo and swing are not stored in a pattern. The tables give each preset's tempo, in quarter-note BPM on the 16-step grid. Every preset plays straight (SWING 50) except these: Preset SWING Hip-Hop · Golden Era Swing 58–62 Hip-Hop · Boom Bap, Lo-Fi Lazy and their bass, lead and chords 54–60 if wanted; straight works Hip-Hop · Jazz Rap, Jazz Rap Walk 60–66 Rock · Half-Time Shuffle about 66, the triplet shuffle Piig · every preset 56–60, the lazy MPC swing Solos · every preset 54–58 with SWING on the EIGHTHS (the templates set it), a ballad's lilt; straight works Bebop · every preset 58–64 with SWING on the EIGHTHS (the templates set it); Trane Countdown and Trane Drive straight to 54, their sixteenths are the swing Set the same swing on every machine playing along. Each pack ships a template, or more ( pack.template(…) , patternkit.write_template() ; the projects dialog's TEMPLATES, ravving/presets/templates/<genre>.json on the stick, a second one under its own name= ): the tempo, swing, key and LIVE FX its presets are best played with. Choosing one starts a new project with them. The tempo is the middle of the pack's preset tempos; the key is the one a pack was made for where it says so, else a usual key of the style. Pack Tempo Key Swing PHASER · ECHO · HEAVY Classical 100 C major 50 0 · 0.2 · 0 Hip-Hop 90 C minor 56 0 · 0.15 · 0.35 Pop 116 C major 50 0 · 0.15 · 0.25 Rock 122 E major 50 0 · 0.05 · 0.35 Trap 140 F minor 50 0 · 0.15 · 0.45 Reggaeton 93 A minor 50 0 · 0.1 · 0.4 Punk 170 A major 50 0 · 0 · 0.5 Tropical 130 C major 50 0 · 0.1 · 0.2 Cumbia 95 G major 50 0.15 · 0.3 · 0.2 Piig 79 D minor 58 0.15 · 0.25 · 0.3 Folk 110 G major 50 0 · 0.1 · 0 Metal 150 E minor 50 0 · 0.05 · 0.6 Black Metal 170 E minor 50 0 · 0.25 · 0.55 Post-Punk 142 A minor 50 0.3 · 0.3 · 0.3 Gregorian 70 D Dorian 50 0 · 0.5 · 0 Jazz 120 C minor 62 0 · 0.1 · 0 Vuelo 120 A minor 50 0.1 · 0.15 · 0.3 Vuelo · Crave 120 C# minor 52 0 · 0.25 · 0.25 Solos 64 Eb major 56 (eighths) 0 · 0.35 · 0 Solos · Late Night 58 Eb major 54 (eighths) 0 · 0.45 · 0 Bebop 160 Bb major 62 (eighths) 0 · 0.15 · 0 Bebop · Ballad 64 Bb major 58 (eighths) 0 · 0.3 · 0 The notes may carry their own velocity and nudge (SELECT's knobs 2 and 3, the chart's VELOCITY and NUDGE lanes by step): patternkit writes them from a note token's @64 and <10 / >10 (10 % of a step early / late). The packs made since use them: palm-muted chugs, tremolo down- and up-strokes, a fiddle's bow, grace notes snapped in early, a dub bass behind the beat, a chant's swell. A note's LENGTH is its _ steps (HOLD), as before. 6/8 and 3/4 in the new packs work as the waltz trio does (below): three 16-step bars hold four 12-step bars, and the tempo counts a quarter of four steps (a jig at a dotted quarter of 110 is "165").

h: The genre packs › The waltz trio is in 3/4
t: The waltz trio is in 3/4. Classical · Waltz, Waltz Oom and Waltz Pah-Pah are three 16-step bars long, which hold four 12-step waltz bars, so the three loop together.

Every sound named is a source in data/kits.json (or a kit path), and validate.py checks this. I added two kinds of entries to kits.json , all from the FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 already on the device ( /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts/SF2 Instruments/ ): Chords sources: Harpsichord 0:6, Guitar · Clean 0:27, Guitar · Overdrive 0:29, Guitar · Distortion 0:30, Marimba 0:12, Steel drums 0:114, Accordion 0:21, Brass section 0:61, Pizzicato strings 0:45. Bass sources: Picked bass 0:34, Slap bass 0:36, Sine sub 8:80, Contrabass 0:43, Cello 0:42. Lead sources: Violin 0:40, Harpsichord 0:6, Trumpet 0:56, Guitar · Overdrive 0:29, Marimba 0:12, Steel drums 0:114, Pan flute 0:75, Accordion 0:21, Music box 0:10, Guitar · Clean 0:27 (champeta's soukous lead). Bass source "808 · Monosynth": a jalv source on Calf Monosynth, the lead machine's own engine (a second instance on the bass track). Its controls are real port values, checked against the plugin's lv2info dump in engine-mods/calf_monosynth_mod/docs/engine-symbols.txt : Sound: osc 1 Sine ( o1_wave 3), plus 15 % of a triangle an octave up ( o2_wave 4, o2_xpose 12, o12_mix 0.15) for the harmonics an 808's saturation gives. Filter: 12 dB low-pass at 400 Hz that follows the key, opened by a 60 ms filter envelope ( env2cutoff 2400 cents): the click of the attack. Amp envelope: 1 ms attack, 1.8 s decay to 0.3, 250 ms release. Glide: legato 3 (Fingered Legato) with portamento 80 ms, so only overlapping notes (a SLIDE) glide. Off: LFO-to-pitch, LFO-to-filter, the mod wheel; master 0.5. What it cannot do:
No pitch drop. The Monosynth's modulation matrix is LV2 state, not ports (the mod's RESEARCH.md), so kits.json can't set a pitch envelope.

No drive port. Turn on the bass machine's DRIVE for the saturation. The bass page's knobs (Nekobi's) don't apply to it. presetKits: Power #128:16 Orchestra #128:48?TOM=48&HAT=43&OPEN=81&CYMBAL=57&PERC=54 . The rows land on: Row Sound KICK concert bass drum SNARE concert (field) snare CLAP castanets TOM timpani on C (key 48) HAT timpani on G below (key 43) OPEN triangle CYMBAL concert crash (clash cymbals) PERC tambourine The timpani suit a key of C: drum kits don't follow the session's key. - Cumbia · timbal #128:0?PERC=73&TOM=65&CYMBAL=56&CLAP=63 : PERC the güiro, TOM the high timbale, CYMBAL the cowbell (campana), CLAP the high conga (llamador). - Cumbia · room #128:8?PERC=74&TOM=66&CYMBAL=56&CLAP=63 : the room kit, with the long güiro and the low timbale. - Latin · congas #128:0?SNARE=63&CLAP=62&TOM=64&HAT=75&OPEN=70&CYMBAL=56&PERC=73 , for salsa: SNARE open conga, CLAP conga slap, TOM tumba, HAT claves, OPEN maracas, CYMBAL cowbell (campana), PERC güiro; KICK stays the kick. - Latin · güira #128:0?SNARE=60&TOM=61&CLAP=62&OPEN=64&HAT=70&CYMBAL=56&PERC=69 , for merengue and bachata: SNARE high bongo, TOM low bongo, CLAP conga slap, OPEN tumba (the tambora's low stroke), HAT maracas, CYMBAL cowbell, PERC cabasa (the metal güira). - All the Latin keys were named from the font and rendered; every one sounds.

h: Sounds › Nothing needs installing on the device
t: Nothing needs installing on the device. The device's font is MuseScore 2.3.2's FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3. It matches by sha256 cfcd66d89e8386823400eca64934b14fbea7bf48ba1f00d21189af1262794ec2 , the hash in zynthbox-qml's config/soundfonts.json , entry SF_00022. A byte-identical copy is in ~/Downloads/ravving-soundfonts/fluidr3mono/ , from https://github.com/musescore/MuseScore/raw/v2.3.2/share/sound/FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 . Its licence is MIT (Frank Wen 2000–2002, mono version Michael Cowgill 2014–16; see LICENSE-FluidR3Mono.md there).

h: Sounds › How the new sounds were checked
t: How the new sounds were checked. Every new preset was rendered offline from that copy with tools/soundfont.py render . All of them sound, with peak levels from 0.02 to 0.20 and none silent. The kit rows were also worked out with a port of DrumKit::fromSoundfont . validate.py checks that every FluidR3Mono bank:program in kits.json exists, whenever the copy is present. Limits of these sounds: FluidSynth sources don't glide; a SLIDE only overlaps the notes. The 808 lines therefore use "808 · Monosynth", which does glide. "Sine sub" (8:80) stays registered, but no preset uses it any more.

h: Piig: Natural Minor, with the Dorian IV and the harmonic V

t: Made for A minor . The progressions are the bands' (Ultimate Guitar), each on its degrees of a minor key: The Cure's A Forest (Am C F D: i III VI IV, the Dorian major IV), Lullaby (i VI) and Boys Don't Cry (A Bm C♯m D in F♯ minor: III iv v VI); Joy Division's Love Will Tear Us Apart (D A Bm Em in B minor: III VII i iv), Disorder and She's Lost Control; Siouxsie and the Banshees' Spellbound (D Dorian: i7 VII IV); The Sisters of Mercy's Temple of Love (i III IV) and Lucretia My Reflection (i III iv); Bauhaus's Bela Lugosi's Dead. Made for D Dorian (SCALE Dorian, ROOT D), the chant's first mode. The Dies Irae (13th century, public domain) is the three phrases of the mfiles.co.uk MIDI: F E F D E C D D | F F G F E D C E | F E D A C D D. Organum Above (lead) and Organum Below (bass) sing it a perfect fifth over and a perfect fourth under, note for note, in its rhythm (organum's parallel fifths and fourths, after the Musica enchiriadis): any two of the three loop together. Dead Can Dance's i v VII IV (In Power We Entrust the Love Advocated: Am Em G D), a saltarello in 6/8, the drone under the chant, and a breakbeat under it the 90s way. The chant's notes swell to the phrase's middle (80–98) and lean a hair early or late. h: Solos: Major (ballads after Coltrane's Ballads and Chet Baker)
t: Made for Eb major (a tenor's ballad key; the lead's degree 1 is Eb4, so the tenor sings "5-".."1+" and cries up to "2+", the soprano floats "5".."3+", the trumpet stays "7-".."6"). The minor moods sit on degree 6 (C minor), and Devotion vamps on degree 2 (F Dorian). Six original ballad solos for the LEAD, each with the brushes, the bass and the chords it is heard over. They are moody, prolonged and passionate, with no fast passages. The model is the John Coltrane Quartet's Ballads (Impulse!, 1962/63: Tyner, Garrison, Jones), plus Baker's slow trumpet. Nothing is quoted: the album's standards and the recorded solos are copyrighted. The style was studied ( tools/genre-research/solos.md ), and every line, progression and rhythm is new. The playing: Tempo 56–70. Long held notes, 6–12 steps, with a beat or half a bar of air between phrases. A swell written across each phrase in velocities: @60 rising to @100–110 and falling back. The MODS soften each note's attack (ATTACK +2400 timecents on the sax, +3600 on the trumpet) and lengthen the release. Every long note sits 8–16 % of a step late, the rubato lean. Flurries only as ornaments: three or four sixteenths pushed early and climbing into a long note. A scoop or slur (~) into a long tone. The chords are Tyner-style: rootless 9ths and 13ths, the So What fourths, fourths planed over a pedal, Lydian clusters, the minor iv (Abm6) and the backdoor Db9, each held a bar or half a bar and then re-voiced. The bass is Garrison's two-feel, whole notes and pedal. The drums are brushes only, darkened with TONE/CUTOFF, with a crash rolled up into the downbeat for the cymbal swell. h: Bebop: Major (horn solos after Parker, Coltrane and Baker)
t: The first Solos pack, kept under its own name when Solos became ballads (2026-10-12): the same presets, renamed Bebop · … , in their own group. Made for Bb major (the horn key; the lead's degree 1 is Bb4, so the alto plays "1-".."7", the tenor "5-".."4", the soprano "1".."4+", the trumpet "6-".."7"). Six original solos for the LEAD, each with the chords, the bass and the drums it is heard over: nothing is quoted (the players' recorded solos and tunes are copyrighted), the vocabulary was studied ( tools/genre-research/bebop.md ) and every line, progression and rhythm is new. The progressions are generic schemes: a rhythm-changes-type A section (I VI7 | ii7 V7 | I VI7 | ii7 V7 | I I7 | IV7 ♯iv°7 | iii7 VI7 | ii7 V7), an 8-bar bop blues (I7 | IV7 | I7 | v7 I7 | IV7 | ♯iv°7 | I7 vi7 | ii7 V7), the Countdown reharm of a ii–V–I (ii7 ♭II7 | ♭VImaj7 VII7 | IIImaj7 V7 | Imaj7, chromatic voicings), a modal vamp on the ii7 with two bars of V7sus (quartal "So What"-type voicings), a ballad's I vi ii V | iii VI ii V, and a cool medium's I | ii V | iii vi | ii V | IV | iv ♭VII | iii VI | ii V. The chords are rootless A and B forms. SWING swings the EIGHTHS here (the templates set it): the ride's "ding ding-a" and the bebop eighths sit on the 16-step grid two steps apart. The playing: Parker's lines run in eighths on the chord tones with chromatic approach notes and enclosures, the off-beats a touch louder (@ +8), the approach notes snapped in early (<8), the blue ♭3 scooped into the 3 (~), a breath between phrases, a motif stated then displaced a beat. Coltrane's sheets of sound are sixteenth 1-2-3-5 cells up and their mirror down on every chord, each run swelling to its top; the modal solo is pentatonic cells, stacked fourths up to the Eb6 and a high note cried four times, on the soprano. Baker's lines are few notes, long and soft (@62–88), every one behind the beat (>8–14), a scoop, and air: the trumpet with its cutoff down a little and a longer release.
