A song is more than one loop. A section is every machine's pattern at once (the intro, the verse, the bridge); the song is the sections in order, each played a number of times. This page is the design, decided before the code (TODO 9b), and the phases it is built in, each closed by its review.

h: What easyrave does, and what ravving does better
t: easyrave's SECTIONS (+) (site/index.html, "SONG SECTIONS") is a row of numbered chips: ＋ saves the whole song (every machine with its sounds, tempo, swing, key, the live FX, mutes, master) as a section; a click recalls it at once, a double click renames, × deletes, a drag reorders. Three things it does not do, which ravving should: easyrave ravving a recall lands at once , wherever the bar is it lands on the next bar line , sample-accurately, as Zynthbox launches clips sections are snapshots : edits after a recall are lost unless saved again as a new section sections are live : what you edit is the section on screen, kept when you move on no song: switching is by hand a song : the sections in order with repeats, played through (SONG) or one looped (LOOP), exported in one take

A section holds the patterns and what plays (not sounds, kits, MODS, effects or levels); sections are live (edits stay in the section on screen); a section picked while playing takes over on the next bar; the sections live on the header's plate and a SONG page (no strip taking height from every page).

The patterns and what plays, per machine: the steps, lines and chords, the bars, accents, slides, note lengths, live timing, automation lanes, the drums' row mix (levels, mutes, solos) and ❚❚ (a machine resting in the intro). That is Machine::contentState() , what undo already keeps, less what changes the engine : the kit and the sound source. Sounds, MODS, effects, levels, tempo, swing and key stay the project's . A kit or a source change restarts FluidSynth or jalv (0.3 s and more of silence): at a section change it would be a gap in the music, which "audio first" rules out.

h: Switching on the bar line: two clips per track
t: Every sketchpad track has five clips; ravving plays clip a only. Each machine gets a second, clip b, and the two take turns: Cue : the section to come is written into the clip that is not playing (the machine's model takes the new content and renders it there, applyContent() ); the playing clip is not touched, so nothing in it can drop or double. Switch : PlayfieldManager is told, for the next bar, to start that clip and stop the other ( setClipPlaystate(…, NextBarPosition) ), which libzynthbox does on the audio thread at the bar's first tick, the way Zynthbox launches clips. A machine whose content is the same in both sections is not switched : it keeps playing (a five-bar brush pattern carries on across the change instead of restarting). When: a section picked by hand while playing is cued at once and switches at the next bar (the grids show it at once, the chip blinks until it plays); in SONG, the next section is cued as the last bar of the current one begins (a whole bar of margin for the main thread). Stopped, a pick is immediate (nothing plays). The bar count comes from SyncTimer's 16th beats since the start (Studio already follows them); Sketchpad's start launches, per track, the clip that holds the section, not always clip a.

LOOP (the default, today's behaviour): the current section loops; picking another switches at the next bar. SONG : the song plays from its first entry (or the one picked) to its end, each entry its section × repeats; at the end it stops, or loops the song (a switch). A section's length is its longest pattern (8 bars at most), shown and changeable (1–8). A song entry: a section and repeats (×1…×8). A section may appear more than once (A A B A).

The section on screen is the one edited; its content is kept in the section when another is picked (and with the project). New sections start as a copy of the current one (DUPLICATE) or empty (NEW): a song is mostly variations. Undo stays per machine and starts over on a section change (it would otherwise undo another section's edit unseen).

The project gets sections: {list: [{id, name, colour, bars, machines: {key: content}}], song: [{section, repeats}], current, mode} . A project without it opens as one section, "A", holding what it has: nothing changes for the projects saved so far. The .ravv bundle carries it unchanged. Presets are untouched: a machine's preset still loads into the section on screen.
EXPORT → TRACK gains SONG (the default when the song has more than one entry): the whole song in one take, its length from the song, plus the tail. LOOP keeps today's BARS × LOOPS.

Header : the project plate reads the section too ("Autumn Leaves · B 3/4"); a tap opens the SONG page. While a section is cued its name blinks there. SONG page (full screen, like the music player): the sections as cards (name, colour, length, which machines play, ⧉ duplicate, rename, delete) with ＋; the song as a strip of blocks, each as wide as its bars × repeats, the playing one with a moving playhead, tap to play from there, drag to reorder, the repeats on a stepper; LOOP / SONG; a tap on a card picks that section. Hardware : ALT + step key N picks section N (the step keys light in the sections' colours while ALT is held, the playing one bright, a cued one blinking); on the SONG page the knobs and arrows walk the cards and the strip. Each section has a colour (from a fixed palette, in order), the same on the plate, the cards, the strip and the LEDs.

Phase 1, the model: done (2026-10-09). Sections (src/backend/sections.h) with its Host, the studio; Machine::sectionContent() / applySectionContent() and the samplers' SamplerBanks ; saved in the project, old projects open as section "A"; 18 unit tests (tests/tst_sections.cpp, they found a name cut leaving a trailing space). On milo: Autumn Leaves rebuilt as A1 A2 B C SOLO from its presets, the song A1 A2 B C SOLO A1 A2 B C (72 bars), each pick bringing back its own lines (A2's held E♭5, C's E♭ E♭ C C, the solo), no sample loaded by a switch, saved and opened again unchanged (not dirty). A capture takes 2–3 ms, a switch (every machine's pattern rewritten) about 60 ms, on the main thread. Startup: restoring the sections takes 19 ms; an A/B against the build before today (6fda638) showed the same 7.9–8.1 s to wired on the same project and page, so nothing measurable is added (the gap to the 5.1 s of quality.md §2 is the device's state, not this code). Review: clang-tidy at the baseline, clazy's three new range-loop detaches and the Qt linters' two findings in the new files fixed. Until phase 2 a pick applies at once, wherever the bar is.

h: Status › Phase 2, on the bar line: done (2026-10-09)
t: Phase 2, on the bar line: done (2026-10-09). Read in libzynthbox first: each tick PlayGridManager advances the playfield (a bar's clip changes, all on its first tick) before the patterns schedule that tick, with no look-ahead ( sequenceProgressionLength 0), so a clip started and one stopped on the same bar meet exactly. Each machine has its track's clips a and b ( Machine::attachSpare() , the PAD SAMPLER's second track too); a pick while playing writes the section into the clip not playing ( cueSectionContent() ), or into the one already waiting when picked again, and Sketchpad::cueTrackClip() has them change places on the next bar; a machine whose part does not change is left playing; ❚❚ in a section goes with the bar too (no note cut at the pick). Sections shows switching until the studio sees, at a bar's start, the clips changed (asked of the playfield, not counted). Measured on milo ( tools/sections-test.sh ): 146 eighths through 24 random picks, none missing or doubled, 10 changes, every one on a bar line, rests in whole bars; tools/audio-impact.sh playing, with a pick every 1.5 s against none: 0 xruns both, realtime CPU 15 % both, GUI 10 % against 9 %. The one edge: a hit recorded early (Q off) on the first step of the section to come cannot sound, its clip not playing yet when it is due.

Phase 3, the interface: done (2026-10-09). Two changes to the plan above, with the user: the SONG page sits under the header, as the MIXER does, rather than over the whole screen (the transport, the tempo and the plate stay at hand while arranging), and the sections follow easyrave's SECTIONS shelf (the user's reference: square keys wearing their number, the name under, ＋ saving the one on screen again, tap / double tap / × / drag), at a finger's size since the header has no room for easyrave's 19–28 px keys; ALT + step keys 9–16 pick sections 1–8 (ALT + 1–8 are the LIVE FX already). A copy now takes its own colour (COLOUR changes it), the song's blocks being told apart by it. Checked on milo by touch: the plate opens it, a tap picks, a double tap renames, ＋ copies, × × deletes, a drag moves (5 before 2 and back), ALT + step 11 picks B, a pick while playing blinks until its bar ( switching true, then false with the section playing); idle it draws 0 frames/s. Review: the Qt QML linter (one clip on the strip's ListView, which scrolls), qmllint, static-analysis.sh handlers , clang-tidy on the C++ (none); 21 unit tests.

h: Status › Phase 4, SONG mode and the song's export: done (2026-10-09)
t: Phase 4, SONG mode and the song's export: done (2026-10-09). Sections follows the song bar by bar ( barStarted() , the bars since the start counted by the studio: libzynthbox's 16th beat counts within the bar): as an entry's last bar begins, the next entry's section is cued through phase 2's path (the same section: it plays on, nothing is touched); as the song's last bar begins the studio stops every clip on the next bar ( Sketchpad:: stopAllAtNextBar() ) and then the transport. PLAY in SONG mode puts the first entry's section in place before the first note ( songStarting() ); PLAY FROM HERE starts any entry (from the next bar while playing); a section picked by hand jumps to its first entry (none: LOOP); song edits while it plays keep the entry playing (removing it: LOOP). The SONG page's LOOP | SONG, the block playing with its progress, "PLAYING PART 6, BAR 44"; the plate's "6/9". EXPORT → WHAT: SONG (its length, once; up to 2048 bars) or LOOP (BARS × LOOPS); the export puts SONG mode on and back. Measured on milo: from part 9 the song stopped on the bar after its 8th; C → SOLO → A1 cued on each 8th bar (27 and 9 ms); Autumn Leaves exported in one take, 72 bars + 4 s tail = 122.36 s, its sections' levels within 0.4 dB of the hand-joined WAV, silent after the tail; audio-impact playing in SONG against LOOP on the same project: the same CPU, 0 xruns. 28 unit tests (the song through, the same section twice, a pick and PLAY FROM while playing, SONG taking over, edits while playing, a missed bar). Sections is a QML type now (its enum by name; uncreatable). zb note: libzynthbox's metronomeBeat16th counts within the bar.

h: Phases, each closed by a review
t: The model (C++ Sections , no audio yet): sections, song, current, mode; capture and apply through Machine::contentState() / applyContent() minus the engine keys; saving and the migration; unit tests (tests/, QAbstractItemModelTester, the song's bar math, old projects). Review: qt-cpp-review, clang-tidy / clazy clean, the API documented. On the bar line : clip b per track, cue and switch through PlayfieldManager, Sketchpad launching the right clip, unchanged machines left alone. Measured on milo: a click on every 16th of section A and a different pitch in B, recorded across a hundred switches (by hand and in SONG): no note missing, none doubled, none late (onsets against the grid); tools/audio-impact.sh while switching: no xruns, no realtime page faults added. The interface : the plate, the SONG page, ALT + step keys and LEDs. Review: qt-qml-review and qmllint, the screenshot tour at 1280×800, the delegates on KeyedListModel, device.sh animations : nothing drawing while idle. SONG and export : playing the song through, the export of the whole song, the Autumn Leaves project rebuilt as A1 A2 B C + the solo chorus and exported in one take (against the hand-joined WAV). Docs and the quality pass : architecture.md, scripting-projects.md (the fifo calls), the user-facing help; the full static-analysis run, QML profiler on the SONG page, boot timing unchanged. Each phase is deployed on milo, tested there, committed on its own.

libzynthbox's NextBarPosition with two clips of one track : Zynthbox uses it per clip; that a stop and a start on one track land on the same tick is to be measured in phase 2 before anything is built on it (a click track recorded across the switch). The fallback, if it slips: both clips change on the bar through one setClipPlaystate pair at CurrentPosition with the bar's tick as the offset. The PAD SAMPLER has a second track (pads 11–16) and SAMPLE KING plays samples: their sections hold the hits, not the samples (loading samples is not for the bar line). Picking a section marked the project changed (fixed 2026-10-09). Projects::comparable leaves out sections.current and, on every machine, the keys the section on screen holds of it (its patterns and rest, repeated at the machine's top level). Nothing real hides: the sections' list captures the section on screen live, so an edit to it (a step, a sample in a pad) still changes the list. Checked on milo: the song played across a section change, a section picked by hand → unchanged; a step added → changed; taken out again → unchanged. Automation recorded in one section stays in it; a live knob sweep across a switch keeps going (it is the knob, not the section).

The sampler page (page 5), and live voice / guitar effects while recording. Research 2026-10-05 from easyrave's source, libzynthbox's source and the device (milo). Status (2026-10-05): phases 1 (playback) and 2 (recording) are built and running on milo; phase 3 (live FX: InputEffects , data/input-fx.json ) is built, waiting for the presets to be tuned with a mic and the guitar; phase 4 is next. The decisions below were taken as proposed: 4 banks × 8 slots, takes in /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples/my-samples/ravving/ (raw takes kept in ~/.local/share/ravving/takes-raw/ ), record wet (+ dry later), TAME first. What the build found is in engines.md (SamplerSynth, the audio input) and architecture.md ( SamplerMachine , InputRecorder , AudioFile ).

Banks A–D , each with 8 sample slots and its own pattern (a step grid, a row per slot). Switching bank switches kit and pattern. Machine knobs on every slot: LEVEL, CUTOFF, BIT CRUSHER, AUTOTUNE (re-tunes autotuned samples to the song's key when the key changes). Slot editor : a waveform screen with trim handles (start, length), PITCH ±12, REVERSE, ▶ preview, ● record; a LAYER : a second sample in the same slot, fired by the same hit. Playback : a hit plays the trimmed window one-shot ; each slot chokes itself (a new hit fades the previous one out in 8 ms instead of stacking). Levels by loudness : each sample is matched by its loudness while it sounds (BS.1770 K-weighting, 100 ms blocks, gated), not by its peak (a vocal and a kick with the same peak were 8 LU apart). A mic take is processed before it becomes a sample : DC removed, 6:1 compression (fast attack, musical release), normalised to just under full scale; the trim defaults to the last burst when a take holds several. KEYS (keys 1–8 play the slots live) and REC (a take of the pattern, count-in first).

h: What the device gives us › libzynthbox's sampler is the engine
t: libzynthbox's sampler is the engine. SamplerSynth plays ClipAudioSources in real time (JUCE, in the audio thread). Each slot is one ClipAudioSource; its root slice has what every slot feature needs: Slot feature ClipAudioSource / slice which note plays it keyZoneStart = keyZoneEnd = the slot's note, rootNote = the same (no transposition) trim startPositionSamples , lengthSamples PITCH pitch (semitones) one-shot playbackStyle = OneshotPlaybackStyle choke exclusivityGroup (−1 none; a slot in its own group cuts itself) level, pan gainHandler , pan (loudness matching sets the gain) envelope adsrAttack/Decay/Sustain/Release (a short release = easyrave's 8 ms fade) LAYER a second ClipAudioSource on the same key zone: SamplerSynth plays every clip that matches the note (later) granular modes, slices, velocity zones, loops A ClipAudioSource is built through its exported constructor, the way ravving already makes the metronome clips ( ClipAudioSource(path, track, slot, row, registerForPolyphonicPlayback, muted, parent) ).

h: What the device gives us › Routing is already in place
t: Routing is already in place. SketchpadTrack (ravving's zlChannel ) with trackType "sample-trig" makes the track's PatternModel send its notes to SamplerSynth ( SampleTriggerDestination ), and its samples list (10 entries, each an object with cppObjId = the clip's id) is how PatternModel registers the clips ( updateSamples() → setClipIds() ). So a bank = 8 clips in that list + its own pattern ; switching bank swaps the list and the pattern. LIVE keys reach SamplerSynth the same way the synths' do. REVERSE is not a one-shot option (only granular and loop styles run backwards), so a reversed slot plays a reversed copy of its file , rendered once. Waveforms : libzynthbox ships WaveFormItem (QML), which draws a ClipAudioSource's waveform with its own peak cache: no drawing in JS. Recording : AudioLevels records any JACK ports to a WAV ( addRecordPort(port, channel) , setShouldRecordPorts , scheduleStartRecording(delay) sample-accurately on SyncTimer's clock, stopRecording , recordingFilenames ): a take can start exactly on the bar after a count-in. AudioLevels also meters the input ( captureA/B ). Files : libsndfile 1.2.2 is installed on the device and the laptop: reading, writing, reversing, the take processing and the loudness measurement run in C++ in a worker thread (QtConcurrent), never on the UI thread.

h: The input (milo: HiFiBerry DAC+ADC Pro, PCM186x ADC)
t: JACK ports Built-in Audio Stereo:capture_FL / capture_FR , 48 kHz. PGA gain −12 … +40 dB per channel ( amixer -c 3 "PGA Gain Left/Right", 0.5 dB steps), plus the ADC digital volume; input select (VINL1/VINL2, differential) and mic bias (on). So the page can offer input modes : MIC (bias on, PGA ~+20…30 dB), GUITAR (bias off, PGA ~+20 dB, mono), LINE (PGA 0 dB, stereo), with a level meter and a gain knob. (The exact gains are to be set with the user's guitar and mic.)

h: Live voice / guitar effects: yes › Feasible and cheap
t: Feasible and cheap. The device has every block, and a whole chain costs little: eight effects running on the input (compressor, saturator, multi chorus, phaser, vintage delay, plate reverb, SwankyAmp, pitch shifter) measured under 1 % CPU each on the Pi 5 (4 cores). Latency : JACK runs 256 frames at 48 kHz (5.3 ms a period), so input → effects → speakers is about 11–16 ms: playable for monitoring a voice or a guitar. (The period could go to 128 if needed, at more CPU.) The design: an input chain of jalv effects (ravving's JalvPlugin , wired by JackWiring like DRIVE and the master inserts): capture → chain → monitor (to the master, with its own level) and → the recorder . A take records the wet sound (what you hear), plus optionally the dry input next to it, so the effect can be changed afterwards. "Like Tame Impala" : Kevin Parker's vocal sound is a known recipe, all on the device: heavy compression (Calf Compressor) → a little saturation (Calf Saturator) → doubling / swirl (Calf Multi Chorus, Phaser or Flanger; the Rotary Speaker for the Leslie wobble) → tape echo (Calf Vintage Delay, slapback + long tail) → a big plate (Dragonfly Plate). Other presets on the same chain: FUZZ VOICE (a guitarix fuzz), ROBOT (Calf Vocoder / TAL Vocoder), TELEPHONE (band-pass), OCTAVE (pitch shift), and for the guitar: AMP (SwankyAmp → guitarix UltraCab → delay → plate). Each preset is data (like kits.json: plugins, fixed controls, and 3–6 knobs for the device knobs: AMOUNT, WOBBLE, ECHO, SPACE…).

Playback (done): a SamplerMachine (a Machine, track 6, "sample-trig"): 4 banks × 8 slots of ClipAudioSources, each bank with its own pattern (the step grid, a row per slot, reusing StepGrid ); trim, PITCH, REVERSE, choke; a sample browser (ChoicePopup over /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples and Zynthbox's sample library); LIVE pads 1–8; all in the session and projects. Verify on the device: choke through exclusivityGroup , layering, live triggering, CPU with 32 loaded clips. Recording (done: guitar tested on jack 4; the monitor runs through its own track with a LEVEL, ready for the chain): input mode (MIC / GUITAR / LINE), gain and meter; ● on a slot records a take (count-in on the transport, or free while stopped), processed (DC, compression, normalise, trim to the last burst) in a worker thread, then loaded into the slot. Live FX (built): the input chain with presets (TAME, FUZZ VOICE, ROBOT, TELEPHONE, OCTAVE, AMP), monitor on/off, record wet (+ dry). Polish : loudness matching (BS.1770), LAYER, the machine knobs (CUTOFF, BIT CRUSHER on the track lane), and later AUTOTUNE (pitch detection + correction: the heaviest part; a separate study).

Banks: 4 × 8 slots, as easyrave (a bank fits SketchpadTrack's 10 sample slots). Takes go to /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples/my-samples/ravving/ , which the browser lists. Record the effect's sound (wet); the clean input next to it is a later option. TAME is the first FX preset.

A second sampler for page 5, next to SAMPLE KING, modelled on the Akai MPC: 16 pads on the device's 16 step keys, the MPC's pad layout on screen, the MPC Sample's parameter set as the first scope, and the MPC Standalone OS's drum tracks as the horizon to scale up to. The two samplers are mutually exclusive : the one on screen plays, the other is silent, as a first rule; later they may play together. Written 2026-10-07 from a cross-reading of three Akai sources, the ravving code, libzynthbox and the plugins on the device. Section 7 is the plan; sections 1–6 are what it rests on.

Source What it gave MPC Sample User Guide v1.3.0 (67 pages) The small device this is based on: one 4 × 4 pad bank at a time (A–H), three knobs K1–K3 that always drive the three parameters of the current tab, three function buttons B1–B3 cycling the tabs, a fader, an encoder, SHIFT. Sample Mode (per-pad parameters), Pad Play (Chop, Note On, Loop, Reverse, Mute, 16 Levels), Sample Record, Sequence Mode (record, overdub, step edit, half/double), Song Mode, Pad FX / Flex Beat / Knob FX. Read in full (pp. 15–45 as images: the screens matter). MPC Standalone OS v3.4 User Guide (451 pages) The full drum track: 4 layers per pad, mute groups (32), pad polyphony, simultaneous play, mute targets, layer play (cycle / velocity / random), sample play (one shot / note off / note on), envelopes, LFO, modulations, insert effects; 16 Level types (velocity, tune, filter, layer, attack, decay, probability, ratchet); Chop Mode (threshold / regions / BPM / manual) and converting slices to pads; the Sampler (record, auto sampler, resample); Note Repeat; pad banks A–H. Read: 16 Level, Note Repeat, Samples (layers, link slices, loop lock, zero snap), Track Edit > Drum Tracks (Global, Mute group, Layer play, Sample play, Polyphony, Simultaneous play, Mute targets). akaipro.com MPC Sample > Features The control list with every SHIFT function (pads 1–16: FULL LEVEL, HALF SEQ, DOUBLE SEQ, COUNT-IN, COMPRESSOR, HALF/DOUBLE SPEED, MIDI CONFIG, FADER, REC QUANTIZE, RESAMPLE, SONG, TRIM SAMPLE, TIME CORRECT, WARP, PROJECT), the knobs' absolute-position pick-up (the same problem the Z2_V5B pots gave us), ERASE / COPY, PAD BANK, SAMPLE SELECT, TAP TEMPO / METRO. The MPC Sample is the model for the first versions: it is a 16-pad sampler with exactly our knob count, and its whole feature set fits one screen. The OS guide tells where each feature grows when scaled up.

Pads. 4 × 4, numbered from the bottom left: row 4 = 13 14 15 16, row 3 = 9 10 11 12, row 2 = 5 6 7 8, row 1 = 1 2 3 4. Banks A–H, one on screen; PAD BANK cycles them. A pad holds one sample (MPC Sample) or up to four layers (OS). Pads light: loaded, playing, selected, muted (red), 16 Levels (velocity ramp). Sample Mode: the per-pad parameters , three per tab, one knob each: Tab (button) K1 K2 K3 Trim (B1) Start 0–100 % End 0–100 % Loop point 0–100 % Mix (B1) Volume −∞…+6 dB (SHIFT: kit volume) Pan 50L–C–50R Amp Env (B1) Attack 0–127 Decay (one shot) / Release (note on) 0–127; SHIFT: decay from Start or End Vel Sens 0–127 Tune (B2) Semi −24…+24 Fine −90…+90 cents Warp (off / 50–200 % / Seq), time-stretch or pitch Play (B2) Polyphony Mono / Poly Mute group Off, 1–16; SHIFT: Pad Link Trigger offset 0–100 % Filter (B3) Cutoff 0–127 Reso 0–127 Type Off, Classic, LPF2/4, HPF2/4, BPF2/4 Filt Env (B3) Attack Decay / Release Depth Pad Play (toggles on the selected pad): Chop (threshold / regions 4-8-16 / manual slices, each slice on a pad; extract, split, merge), Note On (plays while held; else One Shot), Loop (loop point → end; Loop Lock ties it to Start), Reverse , Mute (pads mute instead of trigger; unmute all), 16 Levels (the selected pad on all 16 with velocity, filter or tune ramping; original tune on pad 4).

h: 2. The MPC model, distilled › Sample Record
t: Sample Record. Source (mic, line L/R, resample, USB), monitor off/auto/on, threshold, length free or the sequence; tap a pad to arm it, record, tap again to stop; the take lands on that pad trimmed; RECALL grabs the last 25 s of input.

h: 2. The MPC model, distilled › Sequence Mode
t: Sequence Mode. Sequences on pads (light green when holding events), 1–128 bars, Q (record quantize), RT Swing, count-in, metronome off/on/record, BPM per sequence or global, record then overdub, SHIFT + undo, erase a pad's events, RECALL the last loop's playing; Step Edit lists events per step with velocity and timing nudge; half/double length and speed; resample a sequence to a pad; Song Mode strings sequences. Not for us (yet or ever): Pad FX / Flex Beat / Knob FX (ravving has its LIVE FX), compressor menu (ravving's SOUND EFFECTS), MIDI/CV config, project pages, USB audio.

Everything below exists and is on the device, tested: MPC feature ravving piece A sampler machine with slots, trim, pitch, reverse, step grid, presets, takes SamplerMachine (4 banks × 8 slots on SamplerSynth: one ClipAudioSource per slot, root slice = key zone/root note/one-shot/pitch/trim, reversed copies rendered once), SamplerMachinePanel , SampleScreen (WaveFormItem + trim handles), sampler-presets.json Pattern, bars, playhead, Q, STEP entry, LIVE play, take with count-in, overdub punch-in, undo/redo, presets, automation Machine (one sketchpad track + PatternModel), TakeRecorder (count-in, loop punch-in), PresetLibrary Sample record to a pad InputRecorder ( studio.input : MIC / GUITAR / LINE, gain, bias, monitor, live effects, take processed off-thread: DC, 6:1, normalised, last burst = trim) Swing, tempo, metronome, count-in, play/stop/record keys Studio , the header, Session Pads on the 16 step keys, LEDs per pad, held pads lit RavePage.stepLeds / stepKeysArePads , MachinePanel.heldPads Three knobs on three parameters with pick-up for fixed pots KnobGroup (targets, pick-up, badges), ParamCard / ParamCardRow Mute / solo / level per row StepGrid rows, velocities Browser for samples, hold to hear ChoicePopup ( previewable ), Studio.sampleFiles() / previewSample() A page hosting several machines, one on screen, key again / ◀ ▶ / header chips switching DrumsPage ( ravving.drumMachine , DrumMachineCount ) Screenshot tour, trace logs, profiling, static analysis docs/quality.md , tools/device.sh , QT_LOGGING_RULES=ravving.cuia.debug=true

h: 4. What libzynthbox gives, per MPC parameter
t: ClipAudioSourceSliceSettings (the root slice, and up to 1024 slices per clip) carries: MPC libzynthbox Note Start, End startPositionSamples , lengthSamples as SAMPLE KING's trim Loop, loop point playbackStyle = LoopingPlaybackStyle , loopDeltaSamples (loop start past the slice start), loopCrossfadeAmount loop lock = delta 0 One Shot / Note On OneshotPlaybackStyle (ignores note off) / NonLoopingPlaybackStyle (stops at note off, release applies) Reverse no backward one-shot: a reversed copy of the file ( AudioFile::writeReversed , cached) as SAMPLE KING does granular/loop styles can run backwards; not for one-shots Volume, Pan gainHandler (dB), pan −1…1 Semi, Fine pitch (semitones, fractional: fine = cents / 100) Attack, Decay/Release, (Sustain) adsrAttack/Decay/Sustain/Release one shot: sustain 0 and decay; note on: sustain 1 and release Vel Sens velocity scaling in the machine ( liveVelocity ) + velocityMinimum/Maximum Mono / Mute group exclusivityGroup (−1 none; same group = last played silences the rest) mono = a pad in its own group cuts itself; mute group 1–16 = shared group ids Pad Link (two pads from one) the machine sends both notes ( liveNotes(key) returns two) as ChordMachine plays a chord Trigger offset not native: start position moved forward is a different thing; no Classic model Filter envelope none defer; could ride on automation later Warp / time stretch timeStretchStyle , speedRatio , bpm , autoSynchroniseSpeedRatio phase 4 16 Levels 16 virtual pads: the same clip at 16 velocities, or 16 slices with different pitch the machine builds the map; clips stay one Chop slices: sliceCount , insertSlice , each slice its own key zone → a slice per pad the OS's "convert slices to pads" is native here Layers (4 per pad, velocity/cycle/random) several clips on one key zone with velocityMinimum/Maximum ranges; cycle/random in the machine phase 4 Record, Recall InputRecorder ; AudioLevels' port recorder ( scheduleStartRecording ); a 25 s ring buffer is not there recall = phase 4, needs a continuous recorder Resample MixRecorder (master to WAV) → load onto a pad phase 3 Note Repeat SyncTimer-timed retrigger from the machine while a pad is held phase 3 Other engines on the device were checked and ruled out : the Fabla LV2 (16-pad sampler) runs 1.4 on the device, which cannot load samples; sfizz, samplv1, drumkv1 and LinuxSampler are not installed. libzynthbox's SamplerSynth is the engine, as for SAMPLE KING.

h: 5. The one constraint: samples per track
t: SamplerSynth gives each sketchpad track 10 sample sub-channels (5 slots × 2 rows, each with its own JACK ports), and SketchpadTrack.samples is a list of 10 in zynthbox-qml's model. SAMPLE KING's banks are 8 slots for that reason. 16 pads exceed it. Two ways, decided by a spike at the start of phase 2:

h: 5. The one constraint: samples per track › A. One track, 16 clips (preferred)
t: A. One track, 16 clips (preferred). PatternModel::setClipIds accepts any list length, and SamplerSynth plays every registered clip whose key zone holds the note; a clip's slot/row only chooses which sub-channel's ports it renders to. Pads 11–16 would share sub-channels with pads 1–6, which only means they share output ports, and all of them go to the same track lane anyway. To verify: 16 clips on track 7 with slots i % 5 , rows (i / 5) % 2 , every pad audible on its own note, no voice stealing between pads sharing a sub-channel, and JackWiring::setSampleOutputs wiring the 10 ports.

h: 5. The one constraint: samples per track › B. Two tracks (fallback)
t: B. Two tracks (fallback). Pads 1–8 on track 7, 9–16 on track 8, each with its own PatternModel; the machine mirrors bars, Q and the playhead onto the second pattern and routes a pad's hits to its track. More code in Machine (which is one-track by design). Tracks 7 and 8 are free (0–2 drums, 3 bass, 4 chords, 5 lead, 6 SAMPLE KING, 9 the input monitor).

As DRUMS hosts three machines: SamplerPage gets a Repeater over the two panels, ravving.samplerMachine (0 SAMPLE KING, 1 PAD SAMPLER) picks the one on screen, key 5 again cycles, the header's INSTRUMENTS strip gets a second chip (SAMPLER · PADS), ◀ ▶ keep their panel meaning (SAMPLE KING's banks, the PAD SAMPLER's tabs), so the switch is key 5, the chips, or the nameplate. Session.liveMachine , stepLeds , the big-knob volume and MODE follow the panel on screen, as on DRUMS. Mutually exclusive: Studio.activeSampler names the one that plays; the other is paused (its pattern silent) and muted (its lane down), its clips stay loaded so switching back is instant. Switching the panel on screen switches the active one. Later both can play when the rule is lifted (nothing else depends on it).

h: 6.2 The PAD SAMPLER on screen (the dummy UI, phase 1)
t: Inside the usual MachineModule (strip with nameplate, PAN, VOL, REC, ❚❚, LIVE, S, M; SOUND MODIFIERS collapsed; SOUND EFFECTS chain), the editor is: ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ● PRESET ‹ 1/1 › Q + − AUTO ↶ ↷ CLEAR BANK A B C D ERASE COPY │ toolbar ├──────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 13 14 15 16 │ A03 Kick-808 ♩ ← ⟲ 16 ▁▂▃▅▇▅▃▂▁ waveform ▁▂▃ │ screen │ 9 10 11 12 │ [start]──────────[loop]──────────[end] │ │ 5 6 7 8 │ TRIM · MIX · AMP ENV | TUNE · PLAY | FILTER │ tabs │ 1 2 3 4 │ (K1) START (K2) END (K3) LOOP ⟨3-knob card⟩ │ ├──────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ PAD 3 · Kick-808 ▢▢▢▢ ▢▢▢▢ ▢▢▢▢ ▢▢▢▢ the selected pad's 16 steps │ lane │ 1 ····x···x····· 2 ··x···x···x··· … 16 ················ (overview, tap = select) │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ PadGrid (new): 4 × 4 in MPC order, each pad: number, name (elided), a 16-dot mini step row (its hits in the bar on screen), colour = pad colour when loaded, dim when empty, red when muted, accent outline when selected, white flash while held or hit. Tap selects and auditions (hold to hear, as the MPC), ERASE + pad clears it, COPY + pad copies. SampleScreen (reused): the selected pad's waveform with START / END / LOOP handles, the pad's icons (note on ♩, reverse ←, loop ⟲, 16 levels), the take's time and meter while recording into it. Tabs : three ParamCard s in a ParamCardRow (TRIM, MIX, AMP ENV | TUNE, PLAY | FILTER, FILT ENV), one visible group of three at a time; ◀ ▶ with the editor focused cycle the tabs (B1/B2/B3), the three knobs drive the card (K1–K3), with pick-up on the Z2_V5B pots exactly as the MPC describes for its own absolute knobs. Switch-type values (filter type, polyphony, mute group) use WaveCycler -style choice knobs. Pad Play chips on the screen's edge: NOTE ON, LOOP, REVERSE, MUTE, 16 LEVELS, CHOP (CHOP real since phase 5). Lane : the selected pad's 16 steps as a drum row (tap to write; the 16 step keys write it with LIVE off, as every machine), with the accent key, plus the overview of all pads. This is the MPC's Step Edit shown as a grid; a per-step event list is not needed. Hardware : step keys = pads 1–16 while LIVE ( stepKeysArePads ), else steps of the selected pad; knobs 1–3 = the tab's K1–K3; big knob = volume (page) or the pad selection when the pad grid has the focus; ◀ ▶ tabs; ▲ ▼ walk lane → pad grid → screen → strip → header (and the SOUND sections when open), ALT + ▲ the header; MODE = LIVE; RECORD = a take into the selected pad; SELECT on a pad = audition; BACK = the editor. LEDs : the 16 step keys show the pads' colours while LIVE (held = white), the lane's steps otherwise; ◀ ▶ lit (tabs).

PadSamplerMachine : Machine ( src/backend/padsamplermachine.{h,cpp} ), kind "pads" in kits.json (track 7, baseNote 36 so pad 1 = C1 = GM kick, pads up chromatically; an external keyboard or pad controller plays them as any MPC does over MIDI), pads-presets.json (charts "1"–"16", as the sampler's). struct Pad { // one pad of one bank, everything the MPC Sample keeps QString path; QString name; // the sample (empty = none) qreal level{0.8}; qreal pan{0}; int semi{0}; int fine{0}; // tune qreal start{0}, end{1}, loop{0}; // fractions of the file; loop lock = loop == start bool looping{false}, reverse{false}, noteOn{false}; bool mono{false}; int muteGroup{0}; int link{0}; int attack{0}, decayRelease{0}, velSens{127}; int filterType{0}; int cutoff{127}; int reso{0}; bool muted{false}; QColor color; // the pad's colour, from a palette of 16 }; struct Bank { QList<Pad> pads /*16*/; QHash<int, QSet<int>> hits; QSet<int> accents; int bars{1}; }; Machine gives the pattern, bars, Q, playhead, presets, LIVE, takes, undo/redo, level, pan, effects, mute, ❚❚. The machine adds: pads (QVariantList for QML), bank , the selected pad, loadSample(pad, path) , clearPad , copyPad , setPad<Param> for each parameter, audition(pad) , erasePad(pad) (its hits), halveSequence() , doubleSequence() , sixteenLevels(type) on/off, noteRepeat(division) (phase 3). Clips : one ClipAudioSource per loaded pad (option A: all on the machine's track; option B: track 7/8 by pad), configured from the Pad on every change: key zone and root note = the pad's note, playback style (one shot / note on / loop), start / length / loop delta, pitch = semi + fine / 100, gain / pan, ADSR (one shot: A, D, S 0, R short; note on: A, S 1, R), exclusivity group (mono: 100 + pad; mute group: the group; none: −1), the EQ bands for the filter. Reversed files rendered once in a worker, cached by path hash (SAMPLE KING's code, moved into a shared helper so both samplers use it). Velocity : liveVelocity(pad, accented) = level × (vel sens applied to the pad's measured force where a controller gives one; the step keys give full level) × accent, −1 when muted; revoice() rewrites the pattern as the drums do. Hits : placeHit(position, pad, accented) writes the pad's note; liveNotes(pad) returns the pad's note, plus its linked pad's; the take records live hits through the existing TakeRecorder (count-in, punch-in, overdub). Takes into a pad : studio.input.record() as SAMPLE KING, the processed take loaded on the armed pad with the last burst as its trim. State : state() carries bank, banks (pads, steps, accents, bars); restoreContent reloads it; projects, presets and undo come with Machine . Exclusivity : Studio::setActiveSampler(key) : pause + mute the other, publish activeSampler ; saved with the session.

From docs/quality.md and the ravving-quality skill: clang-tidy / clazy clean on the new files; startup time unchanged (the second sampler loads its clips lazily, after the first frame, like the pages); the QML profiler on the pad grid (16 pads × 16 dots must not bind per frame: one hits list, repainted on stepsChanged ); the screenshot tour gets the PAD SAMPLER screens ( src/main.cpp steps); ravving.cuia.debug traces for the ▲ ▼ walk; the local build loop ( tools/device.sh deploy ), never the AppImage, until a release.
Seven points, in the user's words, that set the order of the phases: Record onto each pad quickly from whatever is on the jack: guitar, a turntable, a mic.

h: 7. What the user wants first (2026-10-07) › Loop the recorded sound on its pad, or not
t: Loop the recorded sound on its pad, or not. The pads in a sequence , looping like the other instruments' views. Live effects on the playing pad : a scratch, an echo, reverse, skip forward, other common ones (the MPC's Pad FX / Flex Beat, which this plan had left out: back in). Loop all of them, or live mode : while the other views play, a long press on a pad leaves it looping, a single tap plays it once. A wave editor shared by both samplers to chop audio.

h: 7. What the user wants first (2026-10-07) › Per-pad sound parameters, effects and filters
t: Per-pad sound parameters, effects and filters. Smart recording : a take that stops by itself when the sound stops (strum a chord on the guitar, the pad has it), so a pad is recorded with one press. Auto-chop a music snippet across the 16 pads , each pad then playing like a note. So the first backend delivers 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8; the next 7 and 9; then 4 and 6. Reference implementations the user pointed at (cloned under ~/Coding/refs/ ): vmpc-juce (an MPC2000XL emulator in C++/JUCE: the sequencer, 16 Levels, chop and pad logic as the original did them), giada (a C++ loop machine: sample channels with loop / one-shot modes and an action recorder, close to point 5), MPC-Sample-Toolkit (Python, the MPC Sample's file formats and kits; anything used from it is ported to C++).

Phase 0 — this document. Decisions to take (defaults in bold if not answered): 1. Clips: option A, one track after the spike; B if it fails. 2. Name on the plate: PAD\nSAMPLER (role PADS; "MPC" stays in the docs, not on screen). 3. Default on key 5: SAMPLE KING stays first (0), the PAD SAMPLER is 1. 4. The lane: selected pad's 16 steps + the 16-row overview (not a 16-row StepGrid: rows would be 24 px). 5. Pad colours: a fixed 16-colour palette by pad number (as MPC pad colour mode), the selected pad's colour lighting its step key. Phase 1 — the dummy UI (QML only, no backend; PadState.qml in memory like PatternState / EffectsState ): 1. SamplerPage hosting the two panels, ravving.samplerMachine , the header chip, key 5 cycling, the exclusivity rule stubbed in Session . 2. PadSamplerPanel.qml (MachinePanel) with PadGrid.qml , the reused SampleScreen , the tab cards, the Pad Play chips, the lane and overview. 3. The hardware walk (pads, tabs, knobs with pick-up, ▲ ▼ chain, LEDs) verified with the trace and screenshots on the device; the screenshot tour step. 4. Docs: architecture.md components table, this plan's status.

h: 8. Plan › Phase 2 — the backend: the user's points 1, 2, 3 and 5
t: Phase 2 — the backend: the user's points 1, 2, 3 and 5. 1. The spike (§5), then PadSamplerMachine with bank A: load / clear / copy a pad, and record to a pad from the input: select a pad, ● REC (or hold RECORD and tap a pad), ● again to stop; MIC / GUITAR / LINE come from InputRecorder 's set-up (INPUT button), the take lands on the pad trimmed to its last burst. Trim (start, end, loop point) and Mix (level, pan) so a take is usable at once. Smart stop (point 8) : the take arms on ● REC and starts when the input crosses the threshold (the MPC's Threshold), then ends by itself once the input has stayed under the threshold for a hold time (0.5 s by default, the SMART chip; the MPC's "Free" length is ● again, "Seq" the sequence's length): InputRecorder already meters the input ( level ), so this is a state machine on it (armed → recording → done) plus the processing it does today (last burst = trim). 2. Loop or one-shot per pad (LOOP chip: LoopingPlaybackStyle from the loop point; NOTE ON: plays while held) and Reverse . 3. The sequence : everything Machine has (the lane, bars, Q, presets, undo, the take with count-in and overdub), plus erase pad, half / double sequence. 4. Live play : while LIVE, a tap plays a pad once (its one-shot, or one pass of its loop), a long press (> 400 ms) latches it looping until it is tapped again, lit while it loops, over whatever the other machines play; a looping pad that is not in the pattern keeps looping across bars (a clip started looping on SamplerSynth, as ClipAudioSource::play(forceLooping) does), and STOP ends them all. 5. kits.json entry, presets file, Studio factory branch, wiring ( setSampleOutputs ), exclusivity with SAMPLE KING, state save/restore, projects. 6. Quality pass: clang-tidy / clazy, startup time, QML profile of the pad grid, the full screenshot tour, the sound verified by pw-record on GlobalPlayback as the drums were. Phase 3 — point 7, the per-pad sound: Amp Env (attack, decay/release, vel sens), Tune (semi, fine), Play (mono/poly, mute group, pad link), Filter (type, cutoff, reso via the clip's EQ bands), per-pad effects (the clip's compressor and EQ as the pad's insert; the track's SOUND EFFECTS stay the kit's), Mute / unmute all, 16 Levels (velocity, tune, filter), kit volume and tune. Point 9, first form : 16 LVL · TUNE spreads one sample over the 16 pads as 16 pitches (the MPC: the original on pad 4, a semitone per pad), which is "each pad a note" without chopping; with CHROMATIC the pads follow the header's ROOT / SCALE instead of semitones, as the chord keys do. Phase 4 — point 4, live pad FX (the MPC's Pad FX / Flex Beat, on the playing pad): ECHO (the track's echo throw, as LIVE FX ECHO), REVERSE (switch the playing pad to its reversed copy from the current position), SKIP (jump forward by a division: restart the voice at position + 1/8 or 1/4 bar), STUTTER (retrigger at 1/16 … 1/64: the Note Repeat engine on the pad), SCRATCH (a speed ramp on the clip, speedRatio with time stretch off, swept down and back as a turntable would; needs a measurement of what SamplerSynth can do live), TAPE STOP (speed to 0), FILTER sweep (the clip's EQ as LIVE FX LO/HI PASS does on the master), GATE (velocity on/off at a division). Held pads (the step keys with ALT, or an FX row of chips on screen) engage them while held, as the MPC's. Phase 5 — point 6, the wave editor shared by both samplers: one WaveEditor (a popup over the page, or the screen enlarged) on libzynthbox's WaveFormItem with zoom, start / end / loop handles, zero-snap, normalise, trim (destructive, to a new file), and Chop : threshold / regions 4-8-16 / manual slices (libzynthbox slices, extract / split / merge), then slices onto the pads (the PAD SAMPLER) or the slots of a bank (SAMPLE KING). CHOP on both panels opens it on the selected pad / slot. Point 9, second form : AUTO CHOP takes a snippet (a take, a loaded song excerpt) and cuts it into 16 slices onto the 16 pads in one press: regions (16 equal parts, beat-aligned when the snippet's BPM is guessed: ClipAudioSource::guessBPM ) or transients (threshold), each pad then a one-shot of its slice, playable as notes from the step keys or a keyboard. Later — towards the OS drum track: banks B–H, layers (up to 4 clips per pad, velocity / cycle / random), warp (time stretch), filter envelope, RECALL (a continuous input ring buffer: a libzynthbox addition), resample the mix to a pad, simultaneous play and mute targets, velocity from MIDI controllers, both samplers playing at once.

h: 9. libzynthbox gaps: patches, then PRs (or a fork)
t: What the sampler needs and libzynthbox does not do today. The rule (the user's, 2026-10-07): fill each gap as a patch against libzynthbox, send it upstream as a PR; if it is declined, keep it in a fork that tracks upstream. Until a patch lands, ravving works around it. Gap Where Work-around in ravving Patch A track's pattern reads exactly ten sample slots ( PatternModel::updateSamples , slotIndices {0..9} ; zynthbox-qml's channel has ten) PatternModel.cpp pads 11–16 on a second track (§5) read as many slots as the channel publishes (or 16) A sample-trigger pattern plays a note whatever its velocity: the drums' silent velocity (−1) does not silence it (to confirm against zynthbox-qml's own sample tracks) PatternModel / SamplerSynth silenced pads are left out of the pattern honour velocity ≤ 0 as "do not play" for SampleTriggerDestination No backward playback for a one-shot (only granular / loop styles run backwards) ClipAudioSource a reversed copy of the file, rendered once ( AudioFile::writeReversed ) a reverse flag on the slice for every style No input ring buffer for the MPC's RECALL (the last 25 s) AudioLevels / the port recorder none (phase 5+) a continuous recorder with a "keep the last N seconds" file No per-slice filter with resonance, no filter envelope ClipAudioSourceSliceSettings the clip's EQ bands for cutoff / type (phase 3), no envelope a per-slice SVF (LP / HP / BP, cutoff, Q) with an ADSR on the cutoff A slice's playback style change is not applied to a sounding voice (a loop turned one-shot ignores the note-off that follows) SamplerSynth voices the unlatch keeps the loop style for 150 ms voices read the style at note-off A non-root slice's own pitch is ignored: a voice transposes by the key's distance to the slice's root note and by the clip's (root) pitch only ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp 552, 780) SamplerSynthVoice 16 LEVELS slices transpose through their root note (whole semitones) apply the slice's pitch in the voice's ratio Deleting a ClipAudioSource under a playing voice crashes the audio thread (bug report 15) ClipAudioSource / SamplerSynth ZynthboxBridge::retireClip() free after the audio thread drops the voices

Next: phase 2, starting with the §5 spike. 2026-10-07: phase 2 in progress. FLT ENV stays stored (no filter envelope in libzynthbox). Pad link and per-pad insert effects left for later; the live listening and the lo-fi jam are the user's. 2026-10-07: phase 4 done (point 4, the live PAD FX on the playing pad, heldFx / fxPad ): ECHO (the kit's echo throw: delay return 0.002 → 0.074), TAPE STOP (the clip's speed ratio down to a crawl in 0.9 s: brightness 0.32 → 0.10, back on release), SCRATCH (a speed wobble 0.45 ↔ 1.6), STUTTER (retrigger every sixteenth of the tempo), SKIP (the pad restarts an eighth of a bar on, its start put back on release), REVERSE (the reversed copy from the point reached, forwards again on release; needs the copy rendered: the pad's REVERSE chip or an earlier hold). All held from the PAD FX chips; no hardware modifier yet (ALT + steps is reserved for the header's LIVE FX, pending). Suite: 36 checks. 2026-10-07: phase 5 done (point 6 and point 9's second form: the wave editor shared by both samplers). WaveEditorPopup is real: REGIONS 4 / 8 / 16 (the big knob too), THRESHOLD (the machine's detectTransients : AudioFile::transients , onsets on the 10 ms peak envelope, a 2.5× rise over the 50 ms before it, over the threshold of the loudest peak, 60 ms apart; the knob re-asks when it rests), MANUAL (a tap on the wave adds a cut, a tap on a cut removes it); APPLY (or SELECT) → applyChop on the pads from pad 1 or the bank's slots from slot 1: each piece is the same file with its own trim, the source's settings. AUTO CHOP opens with 16 (pads) / 8 (slots) regions. NORMALISE and TRIM write the window to library/samples/edits/<name>-norm|trim[N].wav ( AudioFile::writeWindow , −1 dBFS) and put that on the pad / slot untrimmed. CHOP and AUTO CHOP are on SAMPLE KING's tools too (four rows beside the screen). Not done from the phase 5 text: zoom and zero-snap, beat-aligned regions from guessBPM , libzynthbox slices (ravving's pieces are trims on copies of the clip, which the 10-slot limit and the pads' own params make the simpler fit). The user's idea (2026-10-09): a full-screen page like the music player for recording the mic, a guitar or a line freely, with monitoring; the recordings kept where the samplers find them; the sampler's wave tools and the live effects reused; for the guitar, the pedals the image has, and a TUNER (automatic: string after string, each one passed on once it is in tune; manual: the string picked by hand; tunings for guitar, bass and ukulele).

Backend PitchDetector (src/backend/pitchdetector.*): plain C++, no Qt objects. YIN (de Cheveigné & Kawahara 2002: the cumulative mean normalised difference, the first dip under a threshold, parabolic interpolation) on a mono block, decimated to half rate first. Laptop-tested (tests/tst_pitchdetector.cpp: sines and plucked-string-like tones from 30 Hz to 1.3 kHz, noise, silence). Tuner (src/backend/tuner.*, published as studio.input.tuner ): ravving's own JACK client ("ravving-tuner", one input) reading the DRY input jack in use (before the effects: a fuzz would hide the pitch). The audio thread only copies into a lock-free ring; the detection runs on the GUI thread 20 times a second, and only while the tuner is shown ( active : the client is activated then and deactivated after, so it costs the graph nothing otherwise). Tunings are data (data/tunings.json): name, instrument, the open strings as MIDI notes. reference : A4 in Hz (430–450, 440 by default). AUTO: the strings in order, low to high; a string held within ±3 cents for 0.8 s counts as tuned and the next untuned one is up; after the last, ALL TUNED. A note clearly nearer another string is named ("that is the A string"). MANUAL: the string tapped is the target, and stays. Out: frequency, the nearest note, cents off the target, in tune, each string's tuned flag, how far the hold has gone (for the ring). InputRecorder : a take for the RECORDER is kept as played (no compression, no trim: the sampler's processing is for one-shot takes), written to the library's live recordings folder ( Paths::liveRecordings() ), and said with recordingReady(file) ; the sampler's takes keep going as now. LiveRecordings (the list): the files in that folder, newest first, with length; rename, delete, TRIM / NORMALISE through AudioFile::writeWindow (already there). Guitar pedals: data/input-fx.json presets marked "modes": ["guitar"] built from the guitarix LV2s on milo (fuzz, overdrive, tube drive, amp + cab) and the Calf modulation; the INPUT popup and the RECORDER list the presets for the mode in use. Page (qml/pages/RecorderPage.qml; Session.recorderView, opened from MENU) Top bar: RECORDER, the input tabs MIC · GUITAR · LINE (input.mode), ✕. Left: the input (GAIN, a long meter, the jack lights, MONITOR and its LEVEL), ● REC / ■ with the time and a level trace of the take as it goes, and the EFFECTS for the mode (the pedals on GUITAR) with their knobs. GUITAR: the TUNER in the middle (the needle and cents, the note, the strings as buttons lit as they pass, AUTO / MANUAL, the TUNING picker, A4). Right: the RECORDINGS (newest first); the one picked shows on SampleScreen with its trim, ▶ preview (studio.previewSample), TRIM / NORMALISE, CHOP (WaveEditorPopup) onto SAMPLE KING's bank or the PADS, TO SAMPLE KING / TO PADS (one slot / pad), RENAME, DELETE (double tap). Hardware: the input knobs as in INPUT (knob 1 mode, 2 monitor level, 3 gain, big knob gain), RECORD / SELECT records, ▲ ▼ the recordings, BACK leaves.

Their levels are a first pass: to set by ear with a guitar.
