Research of 2026-10-11, after the video recorder was built ( docs/video.md ). The question: could ravving stream a live session to Twitch or YouTube from the Zynthbox itself, while the user plays, and how feasible is it? Short answer: yes, feasible with what the device has , because the hard part (capturing the screen and the master's sound without dropping audio, encoding at a cost the audio graph does not feel) is done and measured; a stream adds a network sink, a stream key, a bitrate budget and a reconnect strategy. The rest of this file says how, what each platform wants, what was measured, the design, the risks and the phases.

Twitch ( developer guide , ingest list ; the Broadcasting Guidelines page itself needs JavaScript and did not load, so its numbers come from Restream , StreamYard and BlazingCDN : third-party, consistent with each other; confirm on Twitch's page before shipping): - Ingest: rtmp://<ingest-server>/app/<stream-key> ; the generic entry point is rtmp://live.twitch.tv/app/<key> ; GET https://ingest.twitch.tv/ingests lists the nearest servers ( url_template ). ?bandwidthtest=true on the URL streams without going live, for a bandwidth check in Twitch Inspector: the way to test from the device without an audience. - The stream key comes from the creator dashboard (Settings → Stream); it is a secret that anyone can stream to the channel with. - Video: H.264, CBR, a key frame every 2 s, 720p30 at about 3000 kbps (4500 for 720p60 / 1080p30), 6000 kbps the practical ceiling. Audio: AAC-LC 128–160 kbps, 44.1 or 48 kHz. - RTMPS: Twitch's pages reached did not say; ffmpeg on the device has rtmps anyway. YouTube ( Choose live encoder settings , official): - Ingest: RTMP / RTMPS (RTMPS recommended; HLS exists as an alternative). The URL and key come from YouTube Studio → Go live → Stream ( rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2/<key> , rtmps://a.rtmps.youtube.com:443/live2/<key> ). A channel must be verified and has a 24-hour wait before its first live stream. - Video: H.264 (or HEVC / AV1), CBR, key frame every 2 s ("do not exceed 4"), CABAC, up to 2 B-frames, square pixels, Rec. 709. H.264 bitrate: 720p30 minimum 3 Mbps, recommended 8; 480p30 minimum 0.4, recommended 4. Audio: AAC, 128 kbps stereo, 44.1 kHz (48 kHz for 5.1). Both accept the H.264 + AAC in FLV that ffmpeg's -f flv writes; both want a fixed key frame interval and CBR, which the recorder's -g 2×fps already does and -b:v -maxrate -bufsize adds. Neither needs 16:9: a 1280 × 800 picture is letterboxed by the player; a scale / pad to 1280 × 720 is a cosmetic choice.

ffmpeg 7.1 with the protocols rtmp rtmps rtmpt rtmpts srt rist tls https and the muxers flv , mpegts , hls , tee (one encode, several outputs: a file and the stream at once). The encoder budget ( docs/video.md , the transport playing, 0 xruns): full screen at 30 fps 48 % of a core, at 15 fps 26 %, 640 × 400 at 30 fps 31 %. A stream at 720p30 x264 veryfast CBR 3000 kbps sits in the same range (CBR costs no more than CRF); the audio graph did not feel any of them. The sound path: AudioTap 's 21-second ring and the 64-frame video queue absorb a network stall of seconds without losing a sample (the recorder's design, reused as is). Wi-Fi (milo on the 5 GHz band, −29 dBm, link 390 Mbit/s): an upload from milo to the laptop over the LAN measured 205 Mbit/s (80 MB over ssh, twice), round trip to the router under 1 ms. The LAN is no limit; the ISP's uplink is the one that matters and was not measured (a home uplink of 10 Mbit/s gives 3× headroom over 3000 kbps; ?bandwidthtest=true or a stream to OBS on the laptop measures the real thing).

Two targets, one pipeline: Straight to the platform (Twitch / YouTube): ffmpeg's -f flv rtmp(s)://…/<key> output in place of (or beside, with tee ) the recorder's Matroska. Everything else is the recorder's: the tap, -copyts with the wall clock on both inputs, x264 on two threads at nice 10, the countdown, the plate's status, RECORD / STOP by the keys (RECORD starts the stream, STOP ends it; or STREAM is a card of its own and RECORD still records locally). Encoder changes for a stream: -preset veryfast -tune zerolatency (no lookahead: a second less latency, a little less quality), -b:v 3000k -maxrate 3000k -bufsize 6000k (CBR), -g 60 -keyint_min 60 at 30 fps, -profile:v main , -c:a aac -b:a 160k -ar 48000 , -flvflags no_duration_filesize , and the output stamped from zero (no -copyts on an FLV: its timestamps are 32-bit milliseconds; the sync holds because both inputs are stamped by the same clock and ffmpeg keeps their offset). To the computer first (the user's laptop running OBS): ravving sends SRT ( -f mpegts srt://laptop:9000?mode=caller ) or RTMP to OBS (a Media Source listening on SRT, or an RTMP server such as nginx-rtmp); OBS adds a camera, overlays, chat and the platform account, and streams. This is the robust set-up for a show: the device does one cheap thing (720p over the LAN at 200 Mbit/s), the laptop does the internet and the production, and a stream key never touches the device. It also reuses the COMPUTER link's host name. The stream status comes from ffmpeg's -progress ( bitrate= , speed= , drop_frames= , out_time ): speed under 1.0× for seconds means the uplink is too slow for the bitrate; drop_frames says ffmpeg is dropping to keep up. Shown on the card and the plate as LIVE · 00:12:34 · 3.0 Mb/s, with a warning when it falls behind. A disconnect: ffmpeg exits; ravving restarts it with the same key after 2, 5, 10 s (Twitch keeps a stream alive for about 90 s of silence before ending it; YouTube similar), the tap running on, so the sound is not lost and the stream resumes where the network came back. The stream key: typed once (SETTINGS · STREAMING: PLATFORM Twitch / YouTube / Custom URL, the KEY, the QUALITY) and kept in ~/.config/ravving/streaming.conf (0600, root-only on the device, as the SSH key is); shown masked; a 40-character key on the on-screen keyboard is tedious, so also accepted from a ravving/streaming.txt on a USB stick or sent from the computer (the link works both ways over ssh). Never logged (the ffmpeg command line in the journal has it masked).

Part Verdict Why Capture + sound + encode done the recorder: 0 xruns at every tier, exact sync, a 21 s audio ring Network sink (RTMP/RTMPS/SRT) easy ffmpeg has the protocols; a flag change on the command CPU for 720p30 CBR fine ≤ 48 % of one core measured at full screen 30 fps; the Pi 5 has four Uplink depends on the ISP 3 Mbit/s steady needed; the LAN gives 200; measure with Twitch's bandwidth test Latency / drop handling moderate -progress readout + restart with backoff; the ring hides stalls up to 21 s Stream key entry and storage moderate typing is painful; USB file / computer link / a webconf page help; 0600 file A camera in the picture later a USB camera works as a source already (untested); picture-in-picture (screen + camera) is one ffmpeg overlay filter, more CPU Chat / viewers on the device out of scope needs OAuth to the platform APIs; the laptop (OBS) is the place for it Viewer-side latency normal 5–15 s on the platforms; the device cannot change that Overall: feasible in two or three days of work , most of it UI (the STREAM card, the settings, the status) and testing against a real account; the audio-first rule is already satisfied by the recorder's design. The OBS-on-the-laptop route is the one to do first: it needs no account on the device, no key, is easy to test on the LAN (OBS shows the picture), and is what a real show would use; the direct route is the same code with another URL.

Backend Streamer ( stream ), sharing the recorder's pieces: extract the ffmpeg argument builder and the tap handling of VideoRecorder into a base ( CaptureSession ), so recording and streaming are two sinks of one capture; a stream can also record locally with -f tee . Settings: platform, url, key, quality (720p30 3000k / 480p30 1500k / audio-only 160k, for a music stream on a weak uplink), reconnects. Status from -progress ; the restart loop; Issues entries for a failed connection and a slow uplink. UI : a STREAM card in the control center's top grid (LIVE · 00:12:34 · 3.0 Mb/s), SETTINGS · STREAMING (platform chips, URL/KEY fields one per row, QUALITY, a TEST button = Twitch's ?bandwidthtest=true for 20 s with the result), the plate's LIVE state, RECORD / STOP as the recorder's (the STREAM card armed: RECORD starts the stream, STOP ends it), a toast on reconnects. Tests : tools/stream-test.sh against an RTMP listener on the laptop ( ffmpeg -listen 1 -i rtmp://0.0.0.0:1935/live/test -c copy out.flv , or OBS): the stream arrives, its bitrate and key frame interval (ffprobe), the sync, audio-impact.sh while streaming (0 xruns), a forced disconnect (the listener killed) and the reconnect, the ring's dropped frames (0). A real stream to the user's Twitch or YouTube account, with the bandwidth test first, then a short unlisted stream; measure speed and drop_frames over 10 minutes. Later: a camera picture-in-picture, the sections' names as a title overlay (ffmpeg drawtext , cheap), viewer count through the platform APIs if ever wanted.

Twitch developer guide: https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/video-broadcast/ (ingest URL format, the bandwidth test, the stream key's place); ingest servers: https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/video-broadcast/reference/ Twitch encoder numbers (third-party): https://restream.io/integrations/twitch/best-live-streaming-settings-for-twitch/, https://streamyard.com/blog/how-to-optimize-streaming-software-settings-for-twitch, https://blog.blazingcdn.com/en-us/rtmp-encoder-settings-bitrate-keyframes-and-ingest-urls, https://compresto.app/blog/best-bitrate-for-twitch YouTube Live encoder settings (official): https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2853702 The device's own numbers: docs/video.md (encoder tiers, sync), this file (Wi-Fi upload).
Findings from easyrave.com's page source (fetched 2026-10-04 into ~/Downloads/theme_refs/rave/site/index.html , 1.2 MB, everything inlined).

h: What easyrave is › A commercial product
t: A commercial product. It has accounts and licences ("free = 3 songs, license = unlimited") and online saves through easyrave-api.ezamboni96.workers.dev . No licence is published for the code or the assets. No MIT/GPL header, no copyright line. That means all rights reserved by default.

h: What easyrave is › All sound comes from its own Web Audio code
t: All sound comes from its own Web Audio code. There are no third-party audio libraries (no Tone.js, no WASM synths). The only third-party code is MediaPipe, loaded from a CDN for the CAM feature.

Machine How 909 / 808 drums Synthesised. bd909 , bd808 , snare , clap , hat , tom , ride , crash : oscillators with pitch envelopes plus filtered noise and waveshapers. No samples. LinnBeats Samples : 10 WAVs ( kick snare sstick clap tamb conga chh ohh cowb ride ), embedded as base64 ( LINN_EMBED ) or fetched from linn/*.wav . No provenance given. 303 bass Oscillator → resonant biquad, with accent, slide and tie per step. Includes a genBassline generator (in key, weighted toward the root). POLY-6 chords Oscillator voices. Chords are stacked in thirds from the current scale, with per-degree "chord sets". THERE LEAD One glide voice, a 2-octave ribbon quantised to the scale, LFO vibrato. SAMPLE KING 8 slots of user audio (mic recording or dropped WAV/MP3), cutoff, bit crusher. Master An AudioWorklet glue compressor + limiter ( ERMaster ), and a crusher worklet ( ERCrush : bit-depth reduction + sample-and-hold). Extras The DROP builder (4-bar riser into an impact), NO/ONLY KICK, SING/autotune (YIN pitch + TD-PSOLA), voice → 303 pattern, WAV/MP3 export.

h: Can we borrow it? › Code: no
t: Code: no. It's unlicensed, commercial JavaScript. Copying it, translated or not, would copy its expression. Ravving reimplements behaviour. Reading what a feature does to design ours is fine; porting their functions line by line is not.

h: Can we borrow it? › Samples: no
t: Samples: no. The Linn WAVs come with no licence or provenance (they're probably LinnDrum ROM material), so we can't ship them. Drum kits need licence-clean sources: our own recordings or renders, or CC0/permissive packs.

h: Can we borrow it? › Artwork: no
t: Artwork: no. Nameplates and finishes are reference only (this rule was already set for the Rave themes). Ravving draws its own in QML.

h: Can we borrow it? › Ideas, techniques and musical facts: yes
t: Ideas, techniques and musical facts: yes. These aren't copyrightable, and we implement them ourselves: - Analog-drum synthesis recipes: a sine kick with a fast pitch drop and a long tail, noise snares and hats. These are standard techniques. DrumSynth (ZBP_SYNTH_00015) already does this kind of synthesis on the device, and its kits can be programmed to match. - Diatonic chords stacked from the scale, per-degree chord sets: music theory, already in Rave.chordName . - An in-key random bassline weighted to the root: already in BassPage.randomBassline . - The DROP structure (riser, cut, impact), kill-kick, stutter: performance ideas we build on libzynthbox (pattern performance clone, mutes, master filter). - A bit crusher (bit reduction + sample-and-hold): a textbook algorithm. Ravving still needs an implementation, because the device has no crusher among its 56 FX (see the mapping). - Pitch tracking for SING (YIN) and pitch correction (PSOLA): published algorithms with open implementations (e.g. aubio, GPL) that we could use instead.

h: Can we borrow it? › Fonts: yes
t: Fonts: yes. Oswald, IBM Plex Mono and Baloo 2 are OFL. We can bundle them if we want the exact type.

h: Can we borrow it? › Colours: yes, as reference
t: Colours: yes, as reference. Per-machine colour values are facts. Rave.machines uses them, as the Rave themes already do.

h: What it means for the engines
t: easyrave's sounds can't come with us, so ravving uses the device's engines (proposal in the ravving skill's mapping.md , still awaiting approval): - Drums: DrumSynth kits programmed after the 909/808 recipes (synthesis, licence-clean), or SamplerSynth with clean one-shot kits. - Bass: Nekobi (a TB-303 model). Chords: Obxd. Lead: Calf Monosynth. Sampler: SamplerSynth. - Crusher: to be added (an LV2, or a stage in libzynthbox). If any of easyrave's sounds or code turn out to be essential, asking its author for permission is the way to get them.

┌──────────────── QML (qml/: the Ravving module, compiled in) ────────┐ │ Main.qml: RaveHeader + StackLayout of the five pages + MENU drawer │ │ pages/: DrumsPage ChordsPage BassPage LeadPage SamplerPage │ │ components/: the shared parts every page is built from │ └───────────────▲──────────────────────────────▲──────────────────────┘ │ context properties │ Zynthbox QQC style (SVG theme) ┌───────────────┴──────── C++ app (src/) ──────┴──────────────────────┐ │ Ravving page state, hardware → HardwareEvent "ravving" │ │ Hardware the `Hardware.on…` attached property import Ravving│ │ StyleHost what the Zynthbox style needs "zynqtgui" │ │ ZynthboxBridge loads libzyncoder + libzynthbox "zynthbox" │ │ HardwareSwitches polls the buttons → MidiRouter's CUIA queue │ │ HardwareKnobs polls the 4 knobs (turns / pot positions) │ │ UnixSignals SIGTERM → LEDs off, then _exit (as zynthbox-qml) │ └───────────────▲─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ dlopen + meta-object calls (headers are not installed yet) ┌───────────────┴──────────── libraries ──────────────────────────────┐ │ libzynthbox (sequencer, sampler, mixer, MIDI router, engines) │ │ libzyncoder (buttons, knobs) · qml-style-zynthbox · KF6 Kirigami │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Rule: ravving runs no Python. When it needs something zynthbox-qml does in Python, that piece is ported to C++ under src/ , and the class doc names the Python it came from.

h: Input flow: the Hardware attached property
t: The device's keys and knobs reach QML the way the keyboard does through Keys : as events delivered to the item with active focus , bubbling to its parents until a handler accepts them. device button ─► HardwareSwitches (zyncoder poll, 20 ms) └► MidiRouter.enqueueCuiaCommand("SWITCH_STEP3_RELEASED") MIDI-mapped CUIA ─► MidiRouter ─► cuiaEvent ─► ZynthboxBridge ─► Ravving::handleCuia ─┐ device knob ─► HardwareKnobs (zynpot poll) ─► Ravving::handleKnobTurn / handleKnobMove ─┤ keyboard (dev) ─► Main.qml Shortcuts ─► ravving.simulateCuia / simulateKnob ────────────┤ ▼ HardwareEvent ─► Hardware::dispatch(window): activeFocusItem, then each parent, until one accepts it import Ravving FocusScope { Hardware.onKnob1Up: event => level += event.delta // knob 1 clockwise Hardware.onBigKnobDown: event => select(index - 1) Hardware.onKnob2Moved: event => cutoff = event.value // Z2_V5B fixed pot, 0..1 Hardware.onStepPressed: event => grid.toggle(event.index) Hardware.onUpPressed: event => { if (atTop) event.accepted = false } // bubble on } Signals: knob1Up/Down … knob3Up/Down , bigKnobUp/Down , knob1Moved … knob3Moved , generic knobTurned / knobMoved , up/down/left/right/select/back/menu/play/stop/record/metronome Pressed , stepPressed (index 0–15), numberPressed (index 0–4), and pressed for anything else. As with Keys , the specific signal goes first and the generic one gets whatever is still not accepted. A handler that runs accepts the event unless it sets event.accepted = false . Focus model: - The open page (a RavePage , i.e. a FocusScope) has the focus. ▲ at a page's top edge is left unaccepted, bubbles to Main.qml , and focuses the header's first group. - In the header, ◀ ▶ move between the KnobGroup s and ▼ / BACK return to the page. Step keys always go to the page. A number key nobody handles still switches the page (C++ fallback). - A KnobGroup (FocusScope) hands its targets to the knobs: knob n → targets[n], the big knob → targets[3] or fine steps on targets[0]. It can also hold navItems , which its navKnob (the big knob by default; knob 1 for INSTRUMENTS) steps through and SELECT activates. Targets show a KnobBadge (a tiny knob icon: the knob number, value arc, pulsing while a Z2_V5B pot waits for pick-up). - Inside a page the big knob is always the volume of the machine on screen ( RavePage.module , MachineModule.nudgeLevel() ); the fader wears the big-knob badge while it is. Groups in a page ( ParamCard , the machine strip) set ownsBigKnob: false so it passes through to the page. Popups and the header, outside the page, keep using it. - A machine's strip (role, PAN knob, VOL RaveFader ) is a KnobGroup : tap it and knob 1 pans, knob 2 sets the level; BACK or a tap in the grid give the knobs back to the rows ( StepGrid.knobsActive is off while the strip has them). - ▲ ▼ walk one vertical order per machine, owned by MachineModule : header → strip → SOUND MODIFIERS cards (only while open) → the editor → SOUND EFFECTS cards (only while open). The sections move the focus themselves ( ParamCardRow.released(dy) , coming back to the card last used with enter() ); a page calls focusUp() / focusDown() when its editor has no further to go (the drums: past the top row / the ACC row; the bass roll: past its top / bottom note row). focusUp() returns false from the strip, so ▲ bubbles to the header; ▼ from the header lands on the page's focusTop() (the strip). - RECORD on an instrument page is that machine's take (the strip's ● shows ● / count-in beat / … / ■); RECORD with the header focused, or ALT + RECORD anywhere, is the global recording (the header's ●, red RECORD LED). - The metronome is libzynthbox's (SyncTimer audibleMetronome ) with zynthbox-qml's tick/tock wavs: ZynthboxBridge::setMetronomeSounds() builds the two ClipAudioSources through the exported constructor (no meta-object factory exists) and SamplerSynth's global-sketch1 outputs are wired to the master. - An external MIDI controller plays the machine on screen (on every page; LIVE, which may be left on another machine, is the step keys' only: 2026-10-09) through the same path as the step keys, so REC records it: GM drum notes 35–59 by role ( DrumKit::roleForGmNote ), any other note cycling through the rows from C2, velocity ≥ 100 an accent. Plugging one in or out shows a Toast (easyrave's dark pill, bottom centre). Debug: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.midi.debug=true". - The key lights ( Main.qml 's ledColors ): ▲ ▼ SELECT BACK ALT MENU always light in a soft white ( navigationLight ; ALT white while held, MENU while the menu is open); ◀ ▶ light while they switch something on the open page ( RavePage.sideKeysLit : the CHORDS views with the editor focused, the drum machines, the sampler banks); PLAY dim green when stopped, bright while playing; STOP dim when stopped, lit while playing; RECORD dim red when ready, red while recording (global or a sampler take), a machine's colour during its take. - ALT + ◀ / ▶ undo and redo the pattern of the machine on screen (the toolbar's ↶ ↷). - ALT + ▲ gives the focus to the app header at once, from wherever it is (a page's rows, a section's cards, the strip): Ravving.headerRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch. - ALT + 1 opens the SONG page from anywhere, and again goes back to the page ( Ravving.songRequested , raised in C++ before any dispatch, its press swallowed too). - The header's INSTRUMENTS chips light the machine on screen only: none while the MIXER, the SONG page, the music player or the RECORDER covers the pages ( Session.pageCovered ). - AUTO: the header's AUTO arms recording ( Studio.recordAutomation ): while playing, a SOUND MODIFIERS or SOUND EFFECTS knob turned is written into its machine's pattern at the step playing ( Machine automation lanes, step → value, undoable, saved); the toolbar's AUTO plays them back (lit, "•" while there are some; a long press clears them). - SOUND EFFECTS cards (open): SELECT switches the focused card's effect on or off, BACK closes the section and the focus goes back to the editor above ( ParamCardRow.selectAndBack ). Closed, ▼ past the editor lands on the bar ( FxChain.focusBar() ): ◀ ▶ ring the chips, SELECT switches the ringed effect, ▼ opens the section on its card, ▲ / BACK go back up. A tap on the ▸ SOUND EFFECTS heading opens it on the effect last touched (the bar has no OPEN button since 2026-10-12: the heading is the one way in by touch). - Dialogs ( RavePopup : ChoicePopup, InputPopup), drop-down lists and the menu darken the page behind them ( ModalDim ); a dialog takes the keys while open and gives the focus back. Dialogs wear easyrave's keyboard-shortcuts card (gradient #1e1c24 → #131118, hairline border, radius 16, DialogHeader : spaced title, hint, ✕); the menu drawer is easyrave's settings panel (gradient #211f28 → #16141c, hairline-split sections under small captions, flat wells that light yellow, #f0c832). - MENU opens the control center ( ControlCenter in the drawer): MIXER, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MIDI, SYSTEM cards, the power row (REBOOT and POWER OFF need a second press within 3 s), OUTPUT and BRIGHTNESS sliders on knobs 2 and 1; ◀ ▶ walk the actions, SELECT runs one. - ✱ ( starPressed ) opens and closes the MIXER ( MixerPage , the StackLayout's sixth view, Main.mixerOpen ); a number key leaves it for that page. In it ◀ ▶ or step keys 1–9 pick a strip, knob 1 is its level, knob 2 its pan, the big knob fine level, SELECT mutes, ALT + SELECT solos, BACK or ✱ go back; the step LEDs show the strips (muted dim, picked white). - MODE switches LIVE on the open page's instrument (from anywhere; the MODE LED shows it). ALT is a modifier held in C++ ( Ravving.altHeld ): ALT + big knob is the master volume wherever the focus is ( masterTurned , never dispatched), badged on the MASTER dial, and ALT + knobs 1–3 go straight to Ravving.altKnobTarget (the header's FX SENDS: PHASER, ECHO, HEAVY), a KnobGroup borrowed while ALT is held (badges, frame, pick-up). - A machine's ❚❚ pauses its written pattern ( DrumMachine.paused → Sketchpad.setTrackPaused : its clip stops in PlayfieldManager and is left out of the launch at play; resuming rejoins on the next bar); it stays playable live. - LIVE (one machine at a time, Session.liveMachine ) turns the step keys into pads ( Hardware.onStepDown on the press, onStepPressed on the release): on the drums keys 1–8 play the rows and key 9 held makes accents; with REC on while playing a hit is written at the nearest step ( Machine::recordLive , timed against the measured step length), in STEP entry while stopped at the cursor ( writeAtCursor ). With the toolbar's Q off ( Machine.quantise ) the hit keeps its distance from that step as the subnote's delay (SyncTimer ticks, negative when early), so it plays back as played; the machine keeps these offsets itself ( timing in its state) and puts them back whenever its model rewrites the pattern ( syncTiming ). The LEDs show the pads (rows in the machine's colour, key 9 red, white while held) and drop the playhead ( RavePage.stepKeysArePads ). libzynthbox's own live recorder is not used: it only hears controller ports, and pads sent through SyncTimer arrive as sequencer traffic. - The toolbar's ⟲ ( Machine.loopBar ) plays only the bar on screen: the pattern's playback window moves to it ( bankOffset = that bar, patternLength = one bar) while bars keeps the real length, and paging with ‹ › moves the loop. Not saved; attach and restore put the window back.

The drums play through libzynthbox exactly the way zynthbox-qml's sketchpad does, with ravving's C++ objects standing in for the Python ones libzynthbox talks to: Class Role Stands in for / ports Studio backend root ( studio in QML): builds the machines from data/kits.json , transport (play/stop, tempo, swing, step), saves the sequence after edits; a preview clock on a desktop; the sampler's browser ( sampleFiles() : kits.json sampleFolders , folders labelled short) and hold-to-hear previews ( previewSample() / stopPreview() : a one-shot clip on SamplerSynth's global lane) sketchpad song + transport glue Machine the base of every machine: track (level, pan, effects, mute, ❚❚, kick cuts), pattern (bars, view bar following the playing bar while playing: follow , off when a bar is picked mid-play, back on when stopped; playhead, STEP cursor), presets, LIVE play/record, UNDO / REDO of the pattern ( canUndo , undo() , canRedo , redo() : every edited whose content differs is a step back, 50 deep, changes within 0.5 s of the last joining its step (a knob turned, a handle dragged); the mix, sound and effects are left out, and so are a subclass's viewKeys() such as the sampler's bank; beginEditGroup() / endEditGroup() make a take one step; a project open starts it afresh); subclasses give steps, sound and velocities; SECTIONS: sectionContent() (the pattern part less soundState() 's keys and the viewKeys() , plus ❚❚ and ONCE) and applySectionContent() (laid over the machine's own by withSection() , the history started over; an empty map empties the pattern), sectionBars() / sectionSounds() ; the samplers keep their banks' hits, not their samples ( SamplerBanks ) Its own length ( bars , m_bars ) is kept apart from what its clip plays: applyPlayLength() is the one place that sets the clip's patternLength and bankOffset , from playedBars() : one bar under ⟲ (the bar on screen), the section's span under ONCE ( once , setSpan() from the studio; the bars past its own emptied by clearRest() ), else its own; while it rests the playhead hides and a live hit is not written. new MonoMachine a mono line (one note per step) with ACCENT and SLIDE (the note lasts 1.5 steps and a legato engine glides into the next): page 3's AC 303 ( bass , DISTRHO Nekobi: accent velocity 127 vs 80, Nekobi accents above 90) and page 4's THERE LEAD ( lead , Calf Monosynth, legato + portamento); base note and velocities from kits.json; presets in scale degrees ( bass-presets.json , lead-presets.json ), RANDOM, octave; follows the header's key: a ROOT or SCALE change snaps every note to the nearest note of the new key (upwards on a tie, as easyrave's snapAll ), and the line's key is saved with it easyrave's AC 303 and THERE LEAD ChordMachine page 2's POLY-6 on TAL NoiseMaker (6 voices, Juno chorus); a custom voicing is scale degrees, or chromatic (semitones from the chord base, chart letter c ) when a note is outside the key, so a chart can carry a C7 in E♭ major; setStepNotes(step, "48,52,55,58") for scripts; live keys below 1000 are chord degrees, from 1000 on single scale degrees ( noteKey , noteKeyForNote , noteOfKey : the NOTES tab's LIVE, written one note into the step's voicing by a take or STEP entry): each step holds a voicing, a diatonic chord (a degree stacked in thirds from the scale, triad or seventh per degree by the chord set: Classic, Triads, Sevenths) or a custom set of scale degrees (built in NOTES); a run of one voicing is one held chord; everything is in scale degrees, so a key, set or octave change revoices it all. Three views: CHORDS ( setChord ), NOTES ( noteSets , toggleNote ), SLOTS (four chordSlots of 1/2/4/8 bars, armedSlot , assignSlot , cycleSlotBars , clearSlot : editing one rebuilds the steps in order). LIVE keys and the chord keys play whole chords, a keyboard note plays its degree's chord; presets chord-presets.json ("1111666633337777", "x" + VOICINGS for custom) easyrave's POLY-6 SoundPresets an LV2 plugin's factory presets read from its bundle's presets.ttl (name, category from TAL's prefix, port values); a machine's kits.json soundPresets {file, keep} gives it soundPresets / soundPreset / loadSoundPreset() : the ports are set (but keep ), the SOUND MODIFIERS take the values ( adopt() ), the name is saved, and an engine restart sends the sound again before the knobs new SoundControls a machine's SOUND MODIFIERS driving its engine's own ports, built from the machine's sound in kits.json (owned by Machine ): cards of knobs, 0..1 mapped onto min..max linearly or with "curve": "log" ; a knob with choices is a switch (snaps to i / (n − 1), ParamCard draws it as a WaveCycler ) whose choices can each set several ports (TAL's JUNO wave: waveform + pulse width + levels). Bass: WAVE · FILTER (CUTOFF RESO ENV MOD) · VOICE (DECAY ACCENT TUNE); chords: FILTER (CUTOFF RESO LFO) · SHAPE (ATTACK LENGTH GLIDE) · TONE (WAVE SAW/JUNO/SQR/TRI, SPREAD, CHORUS OFF/I/II); lead: WAVE (SAW SQR SIN TRI) · FILTER (CUTOFF RESO ENV) · VOICE (GLIDE LENGTH). Machine::setExpression() plays kits.json expressions live (the ribbon's vibrato = Calf lfo2pitch ) new JalvPlugin , JalvEngine one LV2 plugin in jalv (effects, and instruments with MIDI in); JalvEngine makes an instrument a machine's SoundEngine (a mono output feeds both sides) zynthian_engine_jalv.py DrumMachine one drum machine: kit rows, steps as subnotes of its track's PatternModel, accents, presets, per-row level/mute/solo (as velocities), level (track gain), pan (track passthrough), mute, audition, kit switching and reset new TakeRecorder a machine's REC ( studio.take ): a fresh take of what is played LIVE, counted in by the transport's first bar (stopped) or punched in at the loop's restart (playing), overdubbing loop after loop; holds the metronome on for the take easyrave's per-machine ● REC MidiInput external controllers ( studio.midiIn ; devices : the connected ones' names): notes from MidiRouter's hardware port (raw controller notes parked on unused track 9; every device's channels reset to the current track; bridge duplicates dropped), plug-in/out notices zynthbox-qml's MIDI controller handling (subset) VideoRecorder LIVE REC ( video , docs/video.md): a video of the screen (x11grab) or a USB camera (v4l2) with the master's sound, or ( mode "audio") the sound alone as a 24-bit WAV among the exports (finished with tags through Exporter::finishRecording ), encoded by ffmpeg (libx264, two threads, nice 10; Kits. data/kits.json holds every machine: drumMachines (track, Zynthian channel, engine, default kit and preset) and machines by kind ( mono : bass on track 3, lead on track 5; chords : track 4), each with its engine (type, LV2 URI, fixed controls ), its sound (SOUND MODIFIERS), presets file, defaultPreset , baseNote and velocities. Studio builds them generically and publishes the non-drum ones as studio.machines.<key> . Also the kit folder (the 40 drum-machine soundfonts in zynthian-data). Grid rows are not written by hand: DrumKit reads them out of the kit (soundfonts are not General MIDI: the 909's clap is on 50, the Linn's on 39). Tapping a machine's nameplate opens ChoicePopup with every kit; DrumMachine::loadKit() moves each hit to the new kit's note for its role (keeping accents), the engine reloads the soundfont ( SoundEngine::reconfigure ), and the choice is saved in the session ( session.json ). A double tap on the nameplate goes back to the default kit ( resetKit() ). A new engine type is one SoundEngine subclass plus a line in SoundEngine::createEngine() . Presets are factory beats (House, Techno, Electro, Breaks, Hip Hop, Groove, Empty) that replace the pattern. They are drum charts written per role ( "KICK": "X...x..." , X = an accented hit), so every preset plays on every kit. The toolbar's PRESET button shows the loaded preset (• once edited) and opens a ChoicePopup by genre; SAVE CURRENT AS NEW stores the pattern as "My Beat N" in Paths::presets()/drum-presets.json , and DELETE removes a user preset. The other machines save the same way into their own file, named by the factory file's userName ("My Bassline N", "My Progression N", "My Melody N", "My Pattern N").

Row mix. Each row's level, mute and solo are kept per role (they survive kit changes) and live in the hits' velocities: level 0.8 → velocity 100, an accent hits ×1.27 harder, and a muted or soloed-out row gets velocity −1, PatternModel's "do not play". Accents are kept by the machine and saved in the session with the row mix, never read back from velocities. The session lives in Paths::state() ( ~/.local/state/ravving ; an explicit path: libzynthbox's MidiRouter renames the application to "zynthbox-qml" while it initialises).

The pattern interface. StepGrid and PatternToolbar only draw and forward to a pattern object: rows, stepCount, steps, accents, playhead, bars, viewBar, presets, presetName, presetEdited, canSavePresets, rowLevels, rowMuted, rowSoloed, toggleStep(), toggleAccent(), clear(), loadPreset(), saveAsPreset(), removePreset(), setRowLevel(), setRowMuted(), setRowSoloed(), audition() . The studio's DrumMachine and SamplerMachine implement it; PatternState.qml implements it in memory for pages whose backend is still to come (the melodic toolbars). Not wired yet: the drums' SOUND MODIFIERS knobs, Q, the loop toggle, the sampler's LAYER / CUTOFF / BIT CRUSHER / live input effects, easyrave's SAVE CHORD (custom chords onto the chord keys), CAM and SING.

Studio machines are shown by MachinePanel (a MachineModule backed by a Machine: level, pan, ❚❚, effects, sound, REC/takes, STEP cursor, LIVE pad and keyboard bookkeeping), extended by DrumMachinePanel (step grid; pads = rows, key 9 = accent), MonoMachinePanel (mono PianoRoll with pattern: machine ; in LIVE all 16 step keys play the scale from the root upwards and ▲ ▼ shift the octave (with STEP on, playing or not, they walk the rows, each heard: previewSelection , and SELECT writes the row: writeSelection / selectionKey , shared in MachinePanel ); with showRibbon the lead's Ribbon : its notes go through the same LIVE path, a slide starts the next note before ending the last so the engine glides, drag up = vibrato) and ChordMachinePanel (the nameplate shows the loaded TAL sound's title, POLY-6 for its own; a tap opens the sound picker, a double tap rebuilds its own sound from TAL's start-up sound, the engine's controls and the default knobs; CHORDS / NOTES / SLOTS tabs: ChordRoll , a poly PianoRoll on the same steps, ChordSlots ; ◀ ▶ switch them while the editor has the focus ( moveView , viewCount ); the step keys and ▲ ▼ work on the view on screen; CHORD SET, chord keys played as pads that also fill an armed slot; LIVE follows the tab: on CHORDS / SLOTS pads 1–7 = the degrees' chords, on NOTES all 16 pads play single scale notes (note keys), ▲ ▼ the octave while LIVE (the rows with STEP on; SELECT writes the selected chord or note); ▲ ▼ = octave while LIVE) and SamplerMachinePanel ( SampleScreen with the slot's waveform and trim handles, a KnobGroup itself: a tap on it or ▲ from the grid's top row gives knob 1 to the start handle and knob 2 to the end, ▼ gives the knobs back to the rows, LOAD with hold-to-hear previews, ▶, CLEAR, REVERSE, ● REC and INPUT ( InputPopup ), PITCH; the step grid over the bank's slots; BANK A–D chips and ◀ ▶; pads 1–8 = slots, key 9 = accent; knobs 1–3 = the selected row's mute, solo, level). MachinePage is the page around any of them: it forwards the step keys, ▲ ▼, the header hand-off and an external keyboard to its panel ( BassPage , LeadPage , ChordsPage only declare their panel). All of qml/ is one QML module, Ravving , built by qt_add_qml_module into the binary (qmlcachegen bytecode, typed bindings compiled to C++) and loaded with loadFromModule("Ravving", "Main") ; Hardware and HardwareEvent join it through QML_ELEMENT . Every file imports Ravving ; there are no relative imports. For development, RAVVING_QML_DIR makes QmlSourceOverride (a URL interceptor) serve the .qml files from a source tree instead, so QML edits need only a restart. Opening it stops the transport, leaving it stops the player InstrumentChip , GroupLabel , LedDisplay header parts; a chip draws its machine's track level as a slim bar along its bottom (the mixer's colours), only while the machine sounds, from the header's meters ( studio.meters() read ten times a second; the pads' second track counts too) Machine (sound sources) soundSources / soundSource / chooseSoundSource() : kits.json sources after the machine's own engine ( sourceName ); engineConfig() is the chosen one, saved as soundSource in the state; the studio restarts the engine on a change ( Studio::restartEngine : JackWiring::removeSynth forgets the old ports, SoundEngine::stop ends its process, a new engine is started and wired with the same DRIVE insert). soundControlsApply hides the SOUND MODIFIERS on another source MachinePanel (STEP entry) ◀ ▶ in STEP entry while stopped move the entry cursor a step ( moveCursor , wrapping in the pattern) on every panel, instead of switching views or banks; keys held together join one step ( Machine::writeWithPrevious : the second key goes where the first went, the cursor advances once) MachineModule a machine panel: strip, SOUND MODIFIERS, the editor, SOUND EFFECTS. The editor keeps the height it has with both sections closed and scrolls under an open one (a Flickable; a line with dots in the accent along an edge says content continues beyond it) instead of being squashed Nameplate , FxChain , PatternToolbar machine panel parts StepGrid drum/slot rows × 16 steps (+ ACC); drums, sampler and the PAD SAMPLER's lane PianoRoll notes × 16 steps, mono (a MonoMachine: bass, lead) or poly (a ChordMachine's NOTES view: noteSets , toggleNote ), ACCENT/SLIDE lanes. Two fingers pinch to zoom (rows kept 18–56 px tall, so the range follows the scale and the height) and drag to scroll; a scroll past an octave shifts the owner's octave ( octaveScrolled ), so OCT − / + shows what is on screen. ▲ ▼ select a note row ( currentNote ; a tap or a note played live selects too) and a step key writes that note. heldNotes lights the rows played live; a held note without a row shows as an edge marker ("▲ G4" / "▼ E2") or, outside the scale, a lit line between its neighbours with its name Gestures: a one-finger drag scrolls the rows (DragHandler, the gesture locked to its first axis; past 8 semitones octaveScrolled shifts the owner's octave) or pages the bars sideways (one bar per 120 px, the content following the finger), two fingers pinch to zoom and scroll; a tap toggles a cell. A row for the section on screen: RENAME, NEW, COLOUR, LENGTH (AUTO), MOVE, ADD TO SONG. The SONG as a strip of blocks as wide as bars × repeats, a row for the block picked: MOVE, REPEATS, REMOVE. the knobs work on one row, ▲ ▼ pick INPUT or EFFECTS, ◀ ▶ the mode or the preset (+ big knob for fine gain); the input's peak meter (−60…0 dBFS, yellow from −18, red from −6, held peak, CLIP) SampleScreen the sampler slot's screen: libzynthbox's WaveFormItem (made at run time), trim handles, darkened trimmed-out parts, a take's time and meter while recording PadSamplerPanel the PAD SAMPLER (MPC-style, docs/mpc-sampler-plan.md ): PadGrid + the pad's SampleScreen, tools (LOAD, ● REC with SMART stop, CLEAR, COPY, ERASE, 16 LVL, CHOP, AUTO CHOP), Pad Play chips, the live PAD FX row, one tab card (TRIM · MIX · AMP ENV · TUNE · PLAY · FILTER · FLT ENV) on knobs 1–3, the lane (a StepGrid of the selected pad + ACC); ◀ ▶ tabs, ▲ ▼ lane → pads → strip; LIVE = the 16 step keys are the pads PadGrid a pad that sounds beams (its colour pulsing over it, the border lit: the machine's playing ); the MPC's 4 × 4 pads (13–16 top, 1–4 bottom): number, name, 16 hit dots, pad colour, mute tint, selection, held flash, latched-loop ring; APPLY / SELECT → the owner's applyChop (pieces onto the pads from pad 1, or the bank's slots from slot 1); NORMALISE / TRIM → trimToNewFile . Both machines expose the same three methods and transientsDetected RavePage page base: a FocusScope receiving the hardware Pages combine these and hold only page-specific logic: the bassline generator, the bank switching, the chord cursor. Generic controls (buttons, combo boxes, sliders, tabs) come from the Zynthbox Quick Controls style, so they follow the active SVG theme; the dials are ravving's own ( DialFace ), since the theme's SVG dial breaks up at the small sizes the machines use. easyrave-specific parts (key caps, nameplates, grids) are drawn in QML from each machine's finish in Rave.machines .

libzynthbox doesn't install headers, and its headers pull in all of JUCE. So for now ZynthboxBridge : dlopen s libzyncoder.so and calls init_zynlib() . libzynthbox needs zyncoder's MIDI router first, the same order as zynthbox-qml. dlopen s libzynthbox.so and resolves three symbols: Plugin::instance() , Plugin::initialize() and Plugin::registerTypes() . Gets the MidiRouter QML singleton and connects to cuiaEvent through the meta-object system. Both libraries are opened with RTLD_LOCAL . RTLD_GLOBAL lets libzynthbox's bundled JUCE/tracktion symbols interpose on libraries loaded later, and the app crashes in Kirigami's platform-plugin lookup. Next step for the bridge: make libzynthbox install its headers and a CMake config, then replace the bridge with a normal link.

ravving ships as a Store AppImage that bundles ravving, the data and ravving-setup ( setup/ ), the page the AppImage opens over zynthbox-qml to install ravving and pick the UI the device runs; both lean on tools/default-app.sh . See packaging.md .

What ravving relies on for each engine, where each fact comes from, and what was measured on the device. The port facts come from the engine mods' research ( ~/Coding/<engine>_mod/docs/ RESEARCH.md , decoded from each engine's own source); read the mod before changing an engine's engine.controls in data/kits.json or its MODS profile in data/engines.json . Audited 2026-10-05.

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json)
t: What a page lets the user tweak of an engine (its SOUND MODIFIERS, the MODS cards, and its expressions, such as the lead ribbon's vibrato) is the engine's , not the machine's: one profile per engine in data/engines.json , found by the engine itself ( type , and for jalv the plugin uri ; EngineProfiles ). Every source that plays an engine shows its knobs, on any machine: Profile Engine Shown for tal-noisemaker TAL-NoiseMaker (jalv) CHORDS' own synth nekobi Nekobi (jalv) BASS' own synth calf-monosynth Calf Monosynth (jalv) LEAD's own synth, BASS' 808 · Monosynth source fluidsynth FluidSynth every soundfont source (one set for all of a machine's soundfonts: its knobs are offsets to the preset's own sound) A source starts its knobs where its own engine.controls put those ports (the 808's cutoff 400 Hz shows as the CUTOFF knob at 400), so loading a source never changes its sound; without such a control a knob starts at the profile's default . The project keeps each set apart: sound (the own engine's), sourceSound (the soundfonts'), sourceSounds (each other plugin source's, by name); AUTO lanes are sound/… , source/… and sources/<source>/… .

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json) › An engine with no profile shows no MODS
t: An engine with no profile shows no MODS. A machine or a source that brings its own sound in kits.json keeps it (a special case; the profile is the rule).

h: The MODS: one profile per engine (data/engines.json) › Checked against the engines' real ports, twice
t: Checked against the engines' real ports, twice. On the laptop, tools/check-engines.py ( ctest -R engines ) checks every knob, choice, expression and kits.json control against the plugins' ports, ranges included, from tests/data/lv2-ports.json . Run tools/check-engines.py --refresh to read them again from the device's lv2info after adding an engine or upgrading plugins. On the device, when an engine starts, SoundEngine::hasControl() checks the MODS of the source playing, and a knob on a control the engine lacks is an issue in the issues centre ("BASS MODS: Calf Monosynth lacks 1 of their controls"). Adding an engine's MODS: add its profile to data/engines.json (the cards as SoundControls reads them: symbol , min , max , default 0..1, "curve": "log" , or choices for a switch), refresh the ports if it is a new plugin, run tools/check-engines.py , then hear each knob on the device ( device.sh call <machine>.activeSound setValue CARD KNOB 0..1 ).

http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi , a TB-303 clone. Research: nekobi_acid_mod . Fact What ravving does waveform : the plugin's own labels are wrong : 0 renders a square, 1 a sawtooth WAVE switch: SAW = 1, SQR = 0 decay is a rate : higher % = shorter (τ 2.3 s at 0 %, 42 ms at 100 %) DECAY runs 100 → 0, so turning it up lengthens notes accent is velocity > 90 (forced short decay, filter "wow" from resonance) plain 80, accent 127 glide is always on (τ ≈ 13 ms) when notes overlap SLIDE = the note lasts 1.5 steps cutoff 0–100 % ≈ 0–5 kHz (capped ~6.5 kHz), resonance 0–95 %, env_mod , accent , tuning ±12 CUTOFF, RESO, ENV MOD, ACCENT, TUNE as LV2 ranges volume is linear ( v/100 ); Zynthbox's jalv wrapper pins it, ravving's jalv does not volume 100 Measured: ~1 % CPU; the bass track ~0.067 RMS playing.

http://kunz.corrupt.ch/products/tal-noisemaker . Research: noizemakr_mod . Fact What ravving does every port is a bare 0..1; enums quantise as floor(v·(n−1) + 1.5) (1-based): write i/(n−1) voices 1 (6 voices), portamentomode 1 (On: chords glide too), lfo1destination 1/7 (Filter), lfo1waveform 0 (sine), transpose 0.5 (0 oct), filtertype 0 (LP 24 dB; its den is 11) osc1waveform : Saw, Pulse, Noise; osc2waveform : Saw, Pulse, Triangle, Sine, Noise WAVE: SAW, JUNO (pulse, osc1pw 0.75), SQR (pulse 0.5), TRI (osc 2) lfo1amount is bipolar and cubic: (2(v − 0.5))³ , 0.5 = none LFO knob spans 0.5 … 1 lfo1rate = (e^(0.2 + 3v·ln20) − 1) / 19 Hz 0.3 ≈ 0.9 Hz, a slow sweep envelopes are one-poles, very steep: release 67 ms at 0.3, 0.5 s at 0.45, 1 s at 0.5, 3.5 s at 0.6, 12 s near 1; attack 16 ms at 0.15, 0.77 s at 0.45 (computed with the mod's own formulas; its summary table is off) ATTACK spans 0 … 0.55 (3.6 ms … 3.2 s), LENGTH 0.15 … 0.65 (10 ms … 5.8 s) chorus1enable , chorus2enable (the Juno chorus I / II) CHORUS switch OFF / I / II detune , cutoff (log inside the engine), resonance , portamento SPREAD, CUTOFF, RESO, GLIDE volume 's curve is undocumented; measured steeper than linear (0.55 → 0.51 RMS, 0.25 → 0.068) volume 0.25 256 factory presets in the bundle's presets.ttl (78 leads, 53 basses, 34 FX, 28 drums, 26 pads, 15 arps, 13 keys, 7 chords: the name's prefix), each with its port values next to the JUCE state (the mod's research reached them only through the programs extension, which jalv does not surface) SOUND ▾ on CHORDS loads one by setting its ports ( Machine::loadSoundPreset ), keeping voices , volume , transpose ; the SOUND MODIFIERS follow it ( SoundControls::adopt ) Measured: ~1.5 % CPU holding a 4-note chord, ~6 % playing; the chords track ~0.07 RMS.

http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Monosynth . Research: calf_monosynth_mod (+ its engine-symbols.txt ). Fact What ravving does two envelopes: EG1 → cutoff ( env2cutoff , default 8000 cents), EG2 → amp ( adsr2_amp = 1) LENGTH drives adsr2_r ; adsr2_s 1 (a held note sustains); ENV is env2cutoff 0 … 4800 cents logarithmic ports: cutoff, every EG time, portamento, LFO rates CUTOFF 300 … 9000 Hz, GLIDE 1 … 400 ms, LENGTH 10 … 3000 ms with "curve": "log" o1_wave 16 waves: 0 Sawtooth, 1 Square, 3 Sine, 4 Triangle… WAVE: SAW, SQR, SIN, TRI; o12_mix 0 (osc 1 only) legato 0 Retrig, 1 Legato, 2/3 finger modes; pbend_range up to 2400 cents legato 1 (overlapping notes glide), pbend_range 1200 one LFO1 drives lfo2pitch and lfo2filter vibrato only: lfo_rate 5.5 Hz, lfo2pitch played by the ribbon (expression vibrato , 0 … 60 cents) master 0..1 (Zynthbox's wrapper pins it; ravving's jalv does not) master 0.3 Measured: ~0.5–1 % CPU; the lead track ~0.086 RMS playing, ~0.16 while the ribbon plays.

FluidSynth 2.4.4 (a process, not an LV2), one per drum machine with its kit's soundfont. Research: fluidsynth2_mod . Fact What ravving does level CCs (7, 11) and velocity attenuate as 40·log10(v/127) dB, twice the usual law row levels go through velocity (level 0.8 → velocity 100 ≈ −4 dB; accent ×1.27 → 127) reverb / chorus CCs are sends of at most 20 %; the effects' settings have no CC none sent; measured: with FluidSynth's own reverb and chorus on or off, a snare's tail is silent either way (CC 91 stays 0 and the 909 kit sends none): the drums carry no hidden reverb started like zynthbox-qml: -g 1 , synth.polyphony=64 , MMA bank select the same command line The drums' SOUND MODIFIERS are the kit's own (engines.json's kitSound , EngineProfiles::resolveKit): TONE (CUTOFF, RESO), SHAPE (ATTACK, LENGTH: the release) and PITCH (TUNE in semitones, FINE in cents), SF2 generator offsets sent as NRPNs like the soundfont sources' MODS. A kit is one soundfont on one channel, so they act on the whole kit; per drum would need a channel per row. Acoustic kits inside a General MIDI font (kits.json presetKits , the picker's ACOUSTIC group): a kit's path may name one preset of a soundfont, <file>#<bank>:<program> , and after it choose a row's key, ?CYMBAL=51&HAT=44 . FluidR3's kits sit at bank 128 (Jazz 32, Brush 40, Standard 0, Room 8) and keep the General MIDI map, so a key whose sample name says nothing ("Md Studio", its toms) takes its GM role. "Jazz · ride" and "Brush · ride" put the ride (51) on CYMBAL and the hi-hat foot (44) on HAT (shown as PEDAL); the plain "Jazz · crash" keeps the crash, for breaks. FluidSynth gets the file and the bank and program; the path with its choices is what a project saves.

libzynthbox's own sampler: no process, clips (ClipAudioSource) played in the audio thread. Facts from libzynthbox's source ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp , ClipAudioSourceSliceSettings.cpp , AudioLevels.cpp ) and measured on milo. Fact What ravving does a slice's envelope defaults to {attack 0, decay 0, sustain 1, release 0} only the release is set (8 ms, the choke's fade) every voice faded in over ~165 ms (started at gain 0, ramped 0.0001 a frame since b487712): a 0 dBFS kick peaked at 0.096 patched in libzynthbox (a voice starts at its gain; only aftertouch changes ramp), installed on milo; reported in ~/Coding/libzynthbox-bug-reports.md a one-shot retriggered on the same clip and slice stops its previous voice ( SamplerSynthVoice.cpp:392 ) the slots choke themselves as easyrave's do; no exclusivityGroup needed one-shots cannot play backwards (only loops and granular do) REVERSE plays a reversed copy of the file a track's channel_N-sampleM ports exist only while a clip is registered on that slot wired per loaded slot ( setSampleOutputs ) ClipAudioSource::play(…, velocity) : 64 is unity gain previews play at 64 on the global lane AudioLevels' track gain (a machine's VOL) runs −40…+20 dB, 0 at gainAbsolute 0.667; the lane's sends leave before it the sends are scaled by VOL's gain in ravving ( TrackEffects::setSendLevel ) Measured: a 0 dBFS kick at velocity 100 peaks 19 ms after its onset (the drum's own shape) once patched.

h: The audio input (HiFiBerry DAC+ADC Pro, PCM1863)
t: Fact What ravving does the five jacks, left to right: 1 headphones, 2–3 line outputs (speaker icon), 4–5 inputs (mic icon); jack 4 is the left channel (ADC input VINL1), jack 5 the right (a plug not fully home showed up on the other channel) MIC and GUITAR record the jack with the signal ( activeJack : picked between takes when one jack is 10 dB over the other and above −45 dBFS; mixing both added the empty input's noise, audibly), so either jack works; LINE is stereo; INPUT lights each jack's level (AudioLevels' capture meter, rewired to the real inputs); monitor on headphones in jack 1 the HiFiBerry's JACK capture ports are named like a Dummy card's, and which gets the serial suffix changes between boots found by the card each start ( InputPorts ) input noise is mostly the room around the cables: a switched-off mic on jack 4 read −52 dBFS (in bursts) with the user at the desk, −75 dBFS once they left (ravving stopped or playing alike); screen brightness, mic bias, one or two ADC inputs made no difference beyond the run-to-run spread — (a ground loop through the USB-Ethernet link to a charging laptop is the usual suspect) the ADC's input mux is ADC Left/Right Input ; ADC … Capture Source did not change what was heard the selection is left as Zynthbox sets it PGA −12…+40 dB in 0.5 dB steps ( PGA Gain Left/Right ), mic bias on/off; Zynthbox selects VINL2 + VINL1 MIC +30 dB with bias, GUITAR +10 dB (a strummed electric peaked −5 dBFS at +18), LINE 0 dB; the selection left as Zynthbox sets it the open input's noise is −69 dBFS at +30 dB a take under −50 dBFS is refused, not normalised into noise input → monitor ≈ 11–16 ms (256 frames at 48 kHz); the capture node follows the output's clock (no resampling) MONITOR through track 9's lane with its own LEVEL

Ports from lv2info on milo (2026-10-05); the chains are in the presets file. A silent mic on milo (+40 dB PGA) measured −48 dBFS of noise in bursts, mostly under 300 Hz (27–28 Hz, 162 Hz), 16 dB over the empty input: CLEAN cuts it with a 24 dB/octave high-pass and a gate. Plugin Facts the presets rely on Calf Compressor stereo; threshold is linear (0.06 ≈ −24 dBFS), ratio 1–20, attack / release ms, makeup 1–64 (×) Calf Saturator stereo; drive 0.1–10, blend −10…10, mix 0–1, pre/post high- and low-pass in Hz Calf Multi Chorus stereo; amount (wet) and dry 0–4, voices 1–8, mod_rate Hz, mod_depth ms Calf Vintage Delay stereo; timing 0 = BPM (from the bpm port), subdiv 4 with time_l / time_r 3/4 = a dotted eighth / a quarter; amount (wet) 0–4, feedback , medium 1 = tape Calf Ring Modulator stereo; mod_freq 1–20000 Hz (20–600 for a robot), mod_amount 0–1, mod_mode 0 = sine Calf Filter stereo; mode 4 = 24 dB/octave high-pass, 7 = 12 dB band-pass; freq Hz, res 0.707–32 Calf Gate stereo; threshold linear (0.01 = −40 dBFS), range the most it closes (0.03 = −30 dB), ratio , attack / release ms Dragonfly Plate stereo; dry_level and its wet level (the port is named early_level ) 0–100, decay s, predelay ms, low_cut / high_cut Hz MaPitchshift (DISTRHO) mono in , two outs; ratio 0.25–4 (0.5 = an octave down), window ms, blur ; no dry mix SwankyAmp stereo, its own cabinet ( cabonoff ); every port 0–1 ( preampdrive , powerampdrive , inputlevel , outputlevel …) A mono plugin in the chain takes both sides summed and feeds both sides of what follows ( JackWiring::setInputChain ). Measured with several presets started (a dozen jalv processes): about 1–2 % CPU each over 3 s ( top ), the busiest 5.6 %; load average 1.7–2.7 on the Pi 5's four cores.

Calf Saturator (DRIVE), Calf Crusher (CRUSH), Calf Phaser (PHASER), Dragonfly Room (REVERB), TAP Echo (DELAY) have no mods; their ports come from lv2info and were calibrated by measurement ( tools/lv2probe.sh , see debugging.md ). The beat repeat (STUTTER, LOOP) is ravving's own JACK client.

What ravving wires, how to look at it, how to measure it, and what was measured. The graph is PipeWire's, seen by libzynthbox and the engines through PipeWire's JACK library ( pw-jack ), the way zynthbox-qml runs. tools/graph-check.py (run with tools/device.sh graph … ) does the checks below in one go.

JackWiring (src/backend/jackwiring.*) asks libzynthbox's JackConnectionHandler for every link and retries until the ports exist (engines and passthroughs make their ports a moment after they are asked for). Per machine (z: its Zynthian channel, t: its sketchpad track): ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} ─MIDI─> ravving-<key>-midi:midi_00 (FluidSynth) ravving-<key>:<lv2 midi in> (jalv) ravving-<key>:output_FL/FR ──> [DRIVE insert] ──> SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-input{L,R} SynthPassthrough:Synth{z+1}-dryOut ──> TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-input TrackPassthrough lane dryOut ──> AudioLevels:Channel{t+1} ──> GlobalPlayback:input TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx1 ──> ravving-reverb ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 1) TrackPassthrough lane wetOutFx2 ──> ravving-delay ──> GlobalPlayback:input (send 2) SamplerSynth:channel_{t+1}-sample{n} ──> the track's lane (the samplers' slots) SamplerSynth:global-sketch1 ──> GlobalPlayback:input (the metronome's ticks) GlobalPlayback:dryOut ──> ravving-repeat ──> ravving-crush ──> ravving-phaser (the master inserts: LIVE FX) ──> system:playback_1/2 (or ravving-out, a loopback, when the sound goes to Bluetooth / HDMI: docs/bluetooth.md) jacks 4/5 (the HiFiBerry's capture, HardwarePorts) ──> [input inserts] ──> a track's lane (monitor) and / or AudioLevels:SystemRecorder (record); AudioLevels:SystemCapture meters the input The link PipeWire makes on its own from every new engine to the speakers is removed, as zynthbox-qml's autoconnect does, so all sound goes through its track (level, mute, FX). Clock: every JACK client (libzynthbox's nodes, jalv) runs at the graph's rate and period, 48000 / 256 on a Zynthbox. FluidSynth's audio goes through its PipeWire driver (a stream, so its node can run on its own clock): ravving tells it the graph's rate and period ( AudioGraph , read once through a throwaway JACK client) so it is not resampled.

ravving never trusts a hardware port's JACK name: pipewire-jack names a device's ports after its node's description, or system: for the default device, and two cards sharing a description take turns at the plain name and a -<serial> one from one start of PipeWire to the next. On milo the kernel's snd-dummy and the HiFiBerry are both "Built-in Audio Stereo"; on a bad start the input listened to the Dummy and was silent (2026-10-10). The device: data/wireplumber/50-ravving-hardware.conf hides the Dummy from PipeWire, so the HiFiBerry is the only "Built-in Audio Stereo", and (by its priority, 10000 against 1000) the system: device, on every start. libzynthbox and zynthbox-qml wire that name too. ravving: HardwarePorts finds a card's ports by the card. In pw-dump each port's port.alias is " : " (kits.json input.portsCard ), and its JACK name is the JACK port whose UUID carries that port's object serial (pipewire-jack makes a port's UUID as (1 << 32) | (serial + 1) ). The input ( captureOf ) and the speakers ( playbackOf , JackWiring::setSpeakers ) are found that way at start; the input again each time it is armed (the RECORDER or INPUT opening). Seeing it: pw-jack jack_lsp -U (the UUIDs) against pw-dump (the serials and aliases); the journal says ravving: input ports … and ravving: speakers … .

Tool What it shows Use pw-top -b -n 2 every node: driver (no + ) or follower, QUANT/RATE it runs at, WAIT/BUSY per cycle, W/Q B/Q (fractions of the period), ERR (xruns), format the first thing to look at; tools/graph-check.py parses it pw-dump the whole graph as JSON: nodes with props ( node.rate , node.latency , api.alsa.* ), ports, links, devices with profiles scripting; pw-dump ID for one object pw-dot + dot -Tpng the graph as a picture pw-dot -o /tmp/g.dot; dot -Tpng /tmp/g.dot > g.png (graphviz on the laptop) pw-link -l / -o / -i links by PipeWire names (the only names some nodes have: the loopback's inputs) pw-link A:out B:in , pw-link -d to remove pw-jack jack_lsp -c / -l JACK names with connections / latency ranges ravving's and libzynthbox's names pw-mon events as they happen (nodes, links, params) watching an engine start or a link appear pw-metadata -n settings 0 the defaults ( clock.quantum 1024, clock.rate ) and forced values NOT the running clock: that is the driver row in pw-top pw-cli info ID one node's params (Props: channelVolumes…) volumes, formats wpctl status / inspect / set-profile WirePlumber's view: devices, profiles, defaults the sound card's profile (below) pw-jack jack_iodelay round-trip latency through a cable from an output jack to an input jack the only true end-to-end audio latency measurement pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test MIDI round trip through a loopback (a cable between a MIDI out and in, or a2j's Midi Through) MIDI path latency and jitter pw-jack jack_bufsize / jack_cpu_load the period, the DSP load JACK sees tools/mididump.py the MIDI an engine really receives on a port silent-engine investigations tools/meter.py RMS on any ports is sound passing a link tools/graph-check.py rates/periods vs the graph, xrun deltas, linked-but-idle nodes, the ravving links the routine check

rates : every audio node's rate and period against the running driver's. A node at another rate is resampled; a node with a larger period is buffered by that much. idle : nodes with links that are not running: a link that passes no data looks like this (an engine linked while still registering, seen once with FluidSynth: re-make the link). xruns -s N : each node's ERR counter now and N seconds later. Compare idle vs playing, and before vs after a change. links ravving : what is linked, grouped by output port, to check against the map above.
(HiFiBerry DAC+ADC Pro, profile output:stereo-fallback+input:stereo-fallback , graph 48000 / 256, PipeWire 1.4.2.)

Before: every FluidSynth audio node ran at 44100 with a 1024-frame buffer (its defaults: synth.sample-rate 44100, audio.periods 16 × audio.period-size 64) inside the 48000 / 256 graph: PipeWire resampled each one, and each added 23 ms of latency; BUSY per cycle ≈ 170 µs per engine. After -r <graph rate> -o audio.period-size=<period> -o audio.periods=2 : 48000 / 512 (10.7 ms), BUSY ≈ 85 µs, no resampling. The export suite (33 checks) and the soundfont checks pass unchanged. Four FluidSynth buffering variants side by side (standalone processes linked into the master, idle, 60 s, ravving under gdb at the time, see below): PipeWire driver 2 × 256 async (+37 xruns), 4 × 256 async (+40), 2 × 256 synchronous (+39), JACK driver through pw-jack (+40); the driver itself +20. The buffering made no difference: those xruns were the graph's, not the engines'. The JACK driver would run at exactly the graph's period (no 512-frame ring), but needs pw-jack's library path and gives one client for audio and MIDI (ports l_00 / r_00 / midi_00 ); not adopted: the stream's 10.7 ms is below the jitter of anything else in the chain, and the ring is what keeps a busy engine from starving the graph. Thread priorities ( graph-check.py threads ): PipeWire's data loops run FIFO 88 (daemon) and 83 (clients: libzynthbox's, jalv's, FluidSynth's); FluidSynth's own render thread ( fluid_pipewire ) is not realtime (its audio.realtime-prio 60 covers the synth thread only), jalv's main thread is not (it has no audio work). libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread runs FIFO 99 while the transport has run; lowering it to 70 ( chrt -f -p 70 TID ) changed nothing in the xrun rate (19/min before and after), so it is not what delays the graph.

h: gdb costs 20 to 40 xruns a minute (found 2026-10-08)
t: Idle, nothing playing, the graph showed +19 xruns a minute on the sound card's driver and +34 to +40 on each FluidSynth node (the capture driver +32 and Midi-Bridge +32 when the capture node drove the graph), at a steady rhythm of one every 2 to 3 s. The cause was the development aid left on: RAVVING_GDB=1 runs ravving under gdb -batch , and gdb stops the whole process at every fork (ravving spawns lsblk , sensor reads and the like every 2 s) and every thread start or exit; libzynthbox's nodes inside ravving are then late and the driver counts a graph xrun. Without gdb ( systemctl --user unset-environment RAVVING_GDB , restart): 0 xruns in 60 s on every node , idle and playing (below). Never leave it on for a device that is used; tools/device.sh deploy now says so when it finds it set. The same applies to any debugger or profiler attached to zynthbox-qml.

The Lo-fi Say It project playing (six FluidSynth engines, the sends, the master inserts), 60 s, no gdb: 0 xruns on every node. Busy time per 5.3 ms cycle: the driver 29 µs, GlobalPlayback 66 µs, TrackPassthrough 315 µs (6 % of the period, the busiest node: every track's lane, EQ and compressor), each FluidSynth node 85 µs. The graph has room for a great deal more.

Sequenced notes: libzynthbox's SyncTimer schedules them on the JACK frame clock and ZLRouter puts each machine's on ZLRouter:Zynthian-Channel{z} , linked to the engine's MIDI input (above). tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS prints what a port carries. External keyboards: MidiRouter's hardware pass-through ( MidiInput , port 3) feeds the LIVE machine; raw notes reach no engine on their own (the current sketchpad track is parked at 9). Midi Through arrives twice, through a2j and through PipeWire's Midi-Bridge, so copies closer than 4 ms are dropped (docs/architecture.md). Bluetooth MIDI: bluez_midi.server is PipeWire's BLE MIDI node, idle unless a BLE MIDI device connects. Latency: a MIDI round trip is measured with pw-jack jack_midi_latency_test between a hardware MIDI out and in joined by a cable (or a2j 's Midi Through for the software path alone); an audio round trip with pw-jack jack_iodelay and a cable from an output jack into input jack 4 or 5. Neither has been run yet: both need the cable on the device.

The sound card's playback node is the driver ( priority.driver 10000 from /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/99-default-soundcard.conf ) while the master is linked to the jacks. With the sound routed to Bluetooth / HDMI the playback node has no links, suspends, and the card's capture node (always linked: the input meter, the sampler) becomes the clock. It is configured as a batch device ( api.alsa.period-size 1024, api.alsa.headroom 32) and runs the graph at 256 anyway. The pro-audio profile of the card (available, wpctl set-profile <card id> 4 ) would make one driver of both halves (one clock, no drift), but renames the nodes ( pro-output-0 ), which zynthbox-qml's and ravving's wiring ( system:playback_* , the OwnSink name) rely on: not tried.

ravving speaks English, Spanish and Japanese. Every text on its screen goes through KI18n , KDE's gettext layer, and the webpage (site/) is translated from catalogs of its own. The docs stay in English. Language App catalog Webpage catalog Spanish (es) po/es/ravving.po po-site/es/ravving-site.po Japanese (ja) po/ja/ravving.po po-site/ja/ravving-site.po

The domain. Localization (src/backend/localization.cpp) sets the application domain ravving right after the QGuiApplication is made, as the KI18n guide asks, and adds the build tree's locale/ folder so a build runs translated before it is installed. The installed catalogs are /usr/share/locale/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/ravving.mo (CMake's ki18n_install(po) ; the AppImage's default-app.sh install copies them too).
QML. KLocalization::setupLocalizedContext(&engine) (KF 6.8 and later) puts i18n , i18nc , i18np and i18ncp on the root context, so QML calls them bare.
SETTINGS · LANGUAGE. SYSTEM (the default) follows the device's own language; English, Español and 日本語 pick one. The choice is kept in the profile settings ( ui/language ).

Live switching. A change sets KLocalizedString::setLanguages , sends QEvent::LanguageChange to the application and calls QQmlEngine::retranslate() : every binding that calls i18n… is evaluated again, so the screen changes at once. C++ models whose rows carry display text (the video tiers, FILES, the USB page, the audio outputs) catch the LanguageChange event, as the Qt guide does for plain QObjects, and emit their NOTIFY.

h: How it works › Numbers and dates
t: Numbers and dates. C++ formats them through KI18n ( subs(value, 0, 'f', 1) ); QML uses Rave.num(value, decimals) , the locale of the language picked. Dates use QLocale of the first language KI18n uses.

Only display text is translated. A text that is stored, compared, sent or looked up stays English: the machine roles, preset and kit names, scale names, group names, the effect and knob names in data/engines.json, the menu ids, the fifo names, the CUIA names. The display is translated where it is drawn. QML: Rave.kli18nc(context, key) marks a key for extraction and returns it unchanged (the QML side of KI18n's kli18nc , as Qt's QT_TR_NOOP ). The helpers translate at draw time: Rave.group , Rave.drumRow , Rave.param , Rave.paramGroup , Rave.effect , Rave.choice , Rave.tuning , Rave.stringInstrument , Rave.inputMode . Menus dispatch by id , never by the text shown. C++: tables of display text are KLazyLocalizedString ( kli18nc ), turned into text with .toString() when read, so a language change shows at once. A message with values is a KLocalizedString template ( ki18nc(…).subs(…) ) passed on and finished where it is shown. List models carry a display role beside the key, as Qt's QAbstractListModel examples do: the key for the logic, the display text for the screen.

Data. tools/i18n-data.py writes the vocabulary of the data files (drum rows, the engines' knobs and cards, effects, scales, tunings, groups) as i18nc calls into the extraction, as KDE's rc.cpp does, under the same contexts the helpers use.

Every call is i18nc with a context saying what the text is, starting with a KDE UI marker: @action:button , @option:check , @option:radio , @label , @title:window , @title:group , @item:inlistbox , @info , @info:status , @info:placeholder . The context names the music meaning when a word has several ("SONG" the page, "SONG" the PLAY mode). All sound vocabulary shares one context, so a knob name is translated once. Names printed on the device stay English in every language: MENU, ALT, MODE, BACK, SELECT, PLAY, STOP, RECORD, X, Y. So do product and machine names (SAMPLE KING, PAD SAMPLER, POLY-6, the engines and kits), MIDI, USB, HDMI, SBC-XQ and LIVE FX. tools/check-ui.py 's text-translatable rule finds a display text that skips i18n… ; its keep list holds these.

The translations use the words musicians and producers use in each language. English Spanish Japanese DRUMS BATERÍA ドラム BASS BAJO ベース CHORDS ACORDES コード LEAD LEAD リード SAMPLER SAMPLER サンプラー PADS PADS パッド SONG CANCIÓN ソング SECTION SECCIÓN セクション PATTERN PATRÓN パターン PRESET PRESET プリセット KICK / SNARE BOMBO / CAJA キック / スネア SCALE / ROOT ESCALA / TÓNICA スケール / ルート BAR / STEP COMPÁS / PASO 小節 / ステップ LIVE REC REC EN VIVO ライブ録音 RECORDER GRABADORA レコーダー TRACK PISTA トラック SETTINGS AJUSTES 設定 knob / big knob perilla / perilla grande ノブ / 大ノブ Japanese uses katakana for the studio words (ドラム, リバーブ, スケール) and kanji for plain ones (保存, 削除, 設定). Spanish has two plural forms, Japanese one.

Spanish runs about a third longer than English. ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 % of its size; a text still too long is elided. Look at every page in Spanish after adding text.

sh tools/i18n-extract.sh # sources → po/ravving.pot and po-site/ravving-site.pot, merged into every catalog # translate what it marked: empty or fuzzy entries (Lokalize, Poedit or a text editor) python3 tools/check-translations.py # the ctest translations-current python3 tools/site-i18n.py render # po-site → site/es/ and site/ja/ check-translations.py fails when a template is stale, a catalog does not compile ( msgfmt --check ), a text is untranslated or fuzzy, a translation drops a placeholder ( %1 ) or a markup tag ( <b> , <a> ), or the rendered pages are older than their catalogs.

tools/site-i18n.py extract collects every block of text in site/index.html (a heading, a paragraph, a row's words, with their inline , and
), the alt , title and aria-label attributes, and site.js's captions and marks, into po-site/ravving-site.pot. render writes site/ /index.html and site.js with the links pointing one folder up; the language switcher in the page's top bar links the three. , and anything marked translate="no" stay as they are. The page's catalogs live in po-site/, not po/, because ki18n_install compiles every catalog in po/ into the device's install.

msginit --no-translator --no-wrap -l <lang> -i po/ravving.pot -o po/<lang>/ravving.po , and the same from po-site/ravving-site.pot into po-site/ /ravving-site.po. Translate both, following the glossary above (add a column for the new language). Add the language to the Languages table in src/backend/localization.cpp, by its own name. Add its link to the switcher in site/index.html and its hreflang alternate. Run the workflow, then look at every page in the new language on the device.

Before every release, someone who reads the language reviews what changed in each catalog since the last release: new and changed texts, and the screens they appear on. Run git diff v<last> -- po po-site , take the screenshot tour in each language, and check that ctest -R translations-current passes. A release does not ship with fuzzy or untranslated texts.

ravving's screens share one look, taken from easyrave's: machines with side rails and a face in their own finish, controls grouped on strips, work areas recessed in wells, a dark header band on top. These rules keep every new screen in it. tools/check-ui.py checks them over the QML (a laptop test, ctest -R ui-rules , and tools/static-analysis.sh ui ); tools/ui-rules.json holds the rules and their exceptions, and is where a new rule goes. The ravving-ui skill ( ~/.claude/skills/ravving-ui ) walks through building a page by them.

Use the component; never redraw it. What Component Where it is A page's body: the rails and the face in its finish Chassis every page ( MachineModule wears it for the machines) The top band of controls (row 1: transport, plate, ✕; row 2: the deck) PageHeader the dashboard ( RaveHeader ), every full-window page The recessed display in a header's first row HeaderPlate the project name, the track playing, the take A row of buttons on its grouping strip ToolStrip the pattern toolbars, the SONG rows, the player's and the RECORDER's groups A recessed panel for a work area Well the RECORDER's input, tuner, effects, the lists An action ActionButton everywhere (squared, the standard height) An action that cannot be undone (asks twice) ConfirmButton DELETE, REMOVE, CLEAR SONG, FORMAT, EJECT A state (on/off with an LED, or one of a set) Chip / StripButton modes, tabs, banks, sorts The way out CloseButton (the ✕) every dialog (DialogHeader) and every full page An empty list or view EmptyNote every list and grid A dialog's title row DialogHeader every dialog The way a file leaves the device: a SEND… button opening the destinations (USB sticks, the computer, the phone by QR code) SendPopup ( QrPopup for the phone) the FILES browser (every kind), VIDEO SAVED, the music player's tracks, the presets dialog, the sound picker

Squared ActionButton : it does something once and leaves no state. LOAD, CLEAR, SAVE, RENAME, NEW, −/+, ◀ ▶, PLAY FROM HERE, TRIM, TO PADS, the transport keys, a picker showing its current value (it opens a list). Rounded Chip / StripButton : a state you can see. An on/off toggle wears its LED (SET, STEP, LIVE, S/M, MONITOR, REPEAT); one choice out of a set wears none (BANK A–D, the views, SORT, the input tabs, KEEP TAKES IN). It stays lit while the state is on, so it always binds checked (or is checkable). Checked: chip-shows-state . ConfirmButton for what cannot be undone: the first tap arms it (AGAIN? and a countdown bar), a second one within three seconds does it. All of them at the standard size (see Button sizes). Checked: actions-are-actionbuttons (no bare QQC.Button ).

One height: Rave.controlHeight (36 px) for every button, action or state, so a row of them lines up and a finger always finds the same target on the 1280×800 touch screen. A smallest width: Rave.controlWidth (48 px, square) for a glyph (◀ ▶ − + ⟳ ✕) and Rave.actionMinWidth (88 px) for a word (LOAD, SCAN, SAVE): a short word is no smaller a target than a long one. A longer label grows past it. ActionButton applies both on its own ( minimumWidth ); a button may ask for more (the dialogs' main action, SAVE at 150, SCAN at 130 so SCANNING… does not shift the row), never for less. A row that wants bigger buttons sizes them all from one property (the SONG page's rowButtonHeight , wordButtonWidth ), never with numbers on each button. Checked: button-standard-size (no number under the standard on a button's height or width).

h: Controls in a group take the device knobs
t: Dials, switches (WaveCycler) and sliders that sit together are a KnobGroup with them as its targets : the group takes the focus (a tap on it, ◀ ▶ between groups), the device's three small knobs then drive its controls in order (the big knob, one more), and each control wears its KnobBadge (1, 2, 3) saying which knob moves it, with the pick-up diamond on the fixed-pot kit. A group shows its frame while it has the knobs. ParamCard (the MODS and SOUND EFFECTS cards) and the header's TEMPO, FX SENDS and MASTER are the model. So nothing a finger can turn is out of reach of the hardware, and the badges say which knob is which without a manual. Checked: grouped-controls-take-knobs (a file with dials, switches or sliders and no KnobGroup).

h: Rows of controls sit on bands (dialogs and pages)
t: A page's or a dialog's row of controls sits on one ToolStrip , the darker rounded band a pattern toolbar is (the preset, OCT, undo / redo on one band): one row, one continuous band , never split into a band per group. The groups in it (a GroupLabel first, then its chips) are told apart by the space between them, as the toolbar's are. In the presets and sounds dialogs (ChoicePopup): SOURCE at the left and LOAD at the right share their row's band; GROUP and SORT share theirs (the groups wrap in what SORT leaves them, SORT keeps the top right). A row of one group hugs it (SAVE PATTERN AS's KEEP, NamePopup's options under optionsLabel ). A page's toolbar rows too: the SONG page's top bar (its title, SWITCH, PLAYS), its section and song rows, the pattern toolbars. So a dialog reads in rows and groups at a glance, as a page does, and a wrapping row no longer leaves a lone chip on a line of its own. Checked: dialog-groups-on-bands (a GroupLabel in a *Popup.qml outside a ToolStrip); one band per row is the reviewer's to see.

One ✕, the CloseButton , everywhere. A dialog gets it from DialogHeader ; a full page puts it at the end of its header's first row. Checked: close-is-closebutton . A view under the header has no ✕ (the SONG page, the MIXER): the header stays on screen, and the control that opened the view closes it (the project plate, ✱), as BACK does. No CLOSE / CANCEL / DONE buttons: the ✕ and BACK already leave.
