A button that stops work under way (CANCEL an export) is an action, and a question's answers (NO / YES while pairing) are answers; both are listed as exceptions. Checked: no-close-text .

Every page wears a Chassis in its own finish. Checked: page-wears-chassis . A page that takes the whole window (MUSIC PLAYER, RECORDER) has a PageHeader like the dashboard's: row 1 its transport, a HeaderPlate saying what is on, its own toggles, the ✕; row 2 its deck of grouped controls ( ToolStrip s). The view sits under it on the Chassis . Checked: full-page-has-header . Its controls go on ToolStrip s by group, its work areas in Well s.
An empty list or view says why and what fills it, with an EmptyNote ("no recordings yet · ● REC records the input as played"), never a Text of its own. Checked: empty-says-why .

Every page has a finish of its own in Rave.qml ( Rave.machines , songFinish , playerFinish , recorderFinishes ): chassisTop , chassisBottom , rail , well , ink , dim , accent , glow , dark . A new one:

h: Palettes › Starts from a researched palette, not a guess
t: Starts from a researched palette, not a guess. Pick its family from a reference palette set (the Radix / Tailwind / Material colour scales, Adobe Color's or Coolors' tested schemes, or a brand's own): a dark chassis from the scale's 950–900 steps, its well one step darker, the rail a mid step of the same hue, the ink from the scale's 50 step, the dim from 400, the accent the family's 400–500 (or its complement for contrast), the glow a lighter step of the accent. Is readable (WCAG 2.x contrast), against both chassis colours: ink ≥ 7:1 (AAA body text), dim ≥ 4.5:1 (AA text), accent ≥ 3:1 (AA for non-text) on the chassis or the well it lights in. Checked: palette-readable (the ratios are printed when it fails). Is distinct from the pages beside it: the player is violet, the RECORDER's inputs wine, amber and teal, the SONG page a matte slate night.

h: Text is translatable, keys are not
t: Every text a screen shows goes through i18nc with a context (docs/translations.md); a key that is stored or compared stays English and is translated where it is drawn (the Rave display helpers, Rave.kli18nc to mark it). The device's printed key names and the product names stay as printed. Translations run longer (Spanish about a third): ActionButton and Chip shrink their text to fit, down to 75 %, so give words room and look at every new screen in Spanish. Checked as text-translatable : a text: given a literal string without i18n… , outside the keep list in tools/ui-rules.json.

Write it here, under its heading, with why. Add it to tools/ui-rules.json : a pattern (a regex no QML may match) or a check (a function in tools/check-ui.py , registered in CHECKS ), with the files allowed to break it and why. A known breach still to fix is allowed with "migrate": true : it shows as a warning, and the list only ever shrinks. Run python3 tools/check-ui.py --verbose ; fix what it finds or list it.

The recipes for growing ravving the way the drums and the bass were built. Read architecture.md first for the layers; this is the how-to. The code rules hold throughout: reuse a part before writing a new one, keep each class to one job, and give every public API a doc comment and every non-obvious line an inline one.

The drums and the bass share everything except what is specific to them. A new machine (CHORDS, LEAD, SAMPLER) follows the same path. Backend: a Machine subclass ( src/backend/machine.h ). It inherits the pattern, bars, presets, level/pan/pause/mute, effects, LIVE play and STEP entry. Implement: - onAttached() : write the machine's own state into its libzynthbox pattern; - refresh() : publish the bar on screen to QML (its own Q_PROPERTYs + stepsChanged ); - revoice() : rewrite every step's velocity (mute/solo/kick modes changed); - clearOwnSteps() , applyChart(chart) , chart() : its preset format (a chart is a map of strings, one character per step, so preset files stay readable); - placeHit(position, key, accented) , liveNotes(key) , liveVelocity(key, accented) : what a live key writes and plays (a list of notes: one for a row or a mono note, a whole chord for ChordMachine); - state() : everything it keeps (call Machine::state() and add to it: its steps, kit, sound…); a project file is exactly this, so it must be complete; - restoreContent(state) : take that back while running (opening a project) and write the pattern; an empty state means its defaults (the default preset, kit, sound). Call it from the constructor too, so start-up and opening share one path (MonoMachine and ChordMachine do). A missing key means "default", a present but empty one means "empty" (a cleared pattern stays cleared). Write steps through addSubnote / setSubnoteMetadata (velocity −1 = silent, duration in pattern ticks via stepTicks() ), and call markEdited() after a user change. Data: an entry in kits.json's machines ( key , kind , track , zynthianChannel , engine , sound , presets , defaultPreset , baseNote …; tracks and channels must be unused) and a presets file ( data/<machine>-presets.json , {presets: [{name, genre, chart}]} ), installed by CMakeLists.txt. A new instance of an existing kind (another mono synth) needs nothing else on the C++ side. Studio ( studio.cpp , loadKits() ): a new kind is one more kind == branch creating it; addMachine() then wires saving, ❚❚, the track lane, sends, the engine, DRIVE, SOUND MODIFIERS and expressions generically ( attachMachine() ), and it appears as studio.machines.<key> . QML: a MachinePanel subclass (see MonoMachinePanel.qml , ChordMachinePanel.qml ): the toolbar and editor as children, and the overrides MachinePanel declares: stepLeds , liveKeyDown/Up (what pads do while LIVE), stepKey , moveSelection(dy) (▲ ▼ in the editor; false at the edge), keyForNote / padForKey (what a keyboard note plays and which pad lights). Light live notes from heldKeys . QML: the page : a MachinePage declaring its panel (see pages/ChordsPage.qml ); it forwards the device and an external keyboard to it. Add the C++ files to src/backend/CMakeLists.txt and the QML files to src/CMakeLists.txt ( RAVVING_QML_FILES ), a screenshot step in src/main.cpp , and the machine to Rave.machines (finish colours: strings).

Engines are SoundEngine subclasses ( soundengine.h ): start() , reconfigure(config) , midiInputPort() , audioOutputPorts() (left, right), optional setControl(symbol, value) , and the started signal. SoundEngine::createEngine() picks one by the type of the kits.json engine object: "jalv" ( JalvEngine ): any LV2 instrument , e.g. {"type": "jalv", "uri": "http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi", "controls": {"volume": 75}} . Ports and control indexes come from lv2info (cached per URI); a mono output is sent to both sides. Nothing else is needed for a new LV2 synth. "fluidsynth" ( FluidSynthEngine ): soundfonts (the drum kits). A new kind (setBfree, sfizz, a sampler…) is one more subclass run through ConsoleProcess (libzynthbox's ProcessWrapper: restarted on a crash, startup commands, a console prompt) and one more type in createEngine() . Choose an engine by measuring it first ( debugging.md : synthprobe/analyse): velocity response, glide, CPU ( top ), level.

h: SOUND MODIFIERS: an engine's own controls
t: A machine's SOUND MODIFIERS are data: its sound in kits.json, which Machine turns into a SoundControls ( machine.sound ). Cards of knobs, each driving an engine port by its LV2 symbol, a 0..1 knob mapped onto min..max (linearly, or "curve": "log" for ports the engine treats as logarithmic), with a 0..1 default: "sound": [ { "title": "FILTER", "knobs": [ { "name": "CUTOFF", "symbol": "cutoff", "min": 300, "max": 9000, "curve": "log", "default": 0.55 } ] }, { "title": "TONE", "knobs": [ { "name": "WAVE", "default": 0, "choices": [ { "label": "SAW", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0, "osc1pw": 0.5 } }, { "label": "JUNO", "controls": { "osc1waveform": 0.5, "osc1pw": 0.75 } } ] } ] } ] A knob with choices is a switch (its value snaps to choice i of n at i / (n − 1)) and shows as a WaveCycler (SAW, SQR, TRI, SIN are drawn); each choice sets its controls (several ports; give every choice the same ports) or a value for the knob's symbol . Ports with no knob go in engine.controls . A live control a page plays (the ribbon's vibrato) is an expression : "expressions": {"vibrato": {"symbol": "lfo2pitch", "max": 60}} , played with machine.setExpression("vibrato", amount) .

h: SOUND MODIFIERS: an engine's own controls › Get the ports right from the mods
t: Get the ports right from the mods. Every engine Zynthbox ships has a mod in ~/Coding/<engine>_mod/ whose docs/RESEARCH.md decodes its ports from the engine's own source: which are logarithmic, how enums quantise (TAL: i / den , rounded, 1-based), which envelope drives what (Calf: EG1 → cutoff, EG2 → amp), what a port called volume really does. Read it before writing a machine's engine.controls and sound , and record what ravving relies on in engines.md . Studio connects the controls to the engine and sends them all whenever it (re)starts; values are saved with the machine. Read a plugin's port ranges with lv2info and check what its numbers mean in its source: an LV2 range is not always the unit its own GUI shows.

On the track lane (EQ, COMPRESSOR, SIDECHAIN, PAN): an entry in EffectChain::effects() (name, knobs, defaults, shared or per machine) and its mapping in TrackEffects::apply() onto the JackPassthrough lane's properties. An insert (DRIVE): a JalvPlugin per machine created in Studio::attachMachine() , given to TrackEffects (which maps the knobs onto its controls and starts it on first use) and to JackWiring::addSynth(…, insert) ; TrackEffects::driveSwitched → JackWiring::setInsertActive() moves it into the path only while on, so the dry sound never depends on the extra process. Calibrate its gain staging with lv2probe.sh . A send (REVERB, DELAY): one shared JalvPlugin in GlobalEffects , fed from every lane's wet outputs ( JackWiring::addSends ) and returned with addEffectReturn . On the master (LIVE FX: CRUSH, PHASER, STUTTER/LOOP): LiveFx and JackWiring::setMasterInserts , which takes any AudioInsert . Your own DSP (BeatRepeat): an AudioInsert subclass opening its own JACK client (libjack, linked through pkg-config; PipeWire's at run time). Keep the process callback lock-free: atomics from the GUI thread, buffers allocated in the constructor, no Qt calls. For musical timing, ZynthboxBridge::timerTickAtFrame(jack_frame_time()) gives the transport position sample-accurately.

Handle keys with the Hardware attached property (like Keys ); an unaccepted event bubbles to the parent. See architecture.md for the signal list. A machine's vertical order (strip → SOUND MODIFIERS → editor → SOUND EFFECTS) lives in MachineModule : pages only call focusUp() / focusDown() at their editor's edge. Knob-driven controls go in a KnobGroup (targets need value , from , to , knobStep , fineStep , knobBadge , knobPending : RaveKnob , RaveFader , WaveCycler have them). Menus: RaveComboBox (drop-downs) and ChoicePopup (grids: kits, presets) already take the arrows, the big knob, SELECT and BACK, and hand the focus back on close.

Build clean (no warnings), run the desktop screenshots (no QML warnings), deploy, check on the device (screenshot + measurement), update architecture.md and these guides, then commit as a single line authored by the user.

h: Reporting a problem to the issues center
t: Every component owns a check pass: at start, and whenever something fails or recovers, it tells the center ( src/backend/diagnostics.h ): #include "diagnostics.h" Issues::report(QStringLiteral("wiring"), QStringLiteral("sound"), QStringLiteral("warning"), QStringLiteral("Some audio connections are missing"), // the title, the user's words QStringLiteral("some ports never appeared…"), // the detail: what was seen QStringLiteral("Pick the sound again, or restart ravving."), // what to do QStringLiteral("restart")); // an action button, or "" Issues::clear(QStringLiteral("wiring")); // once it works again Rules: a stable id per problem (reporting it again updates and counts it); error when something does not work, warning when it works worse or will stop, notice for what is worth knowing (a desktop without device keys); always a suggestion the user can follow; clear it from the same place that would see it recovered. A library's stderr line can become an issue through StderrWatch 's pattern table (src/stderrwatch.cpp). tools/issues-test.sh exercises the center over the fifo.

One CMake project, its targets each with the CMakeLists.txt of their sources (the source files themselves are where they were: the split is of the CMake files only): File Owns CMakeLists.txt the project: version, C++ standard, AUTOMOC, qt_standard_project_setup , the dependencies ( find_package Qt6 / KF6BluezQt / ZLIB, pkg_check_modules jack / sndfile / taglib), RAVVING_DATA_INSTALL_DIR and RAVVING_THEME , the build options ( RAVVING_QML_AOT , RAVVING_PCH , RAVVING_TIME_TRACE , RAVVING_UNITY , RAVVING_IWYU , RAVVING_TESTS ) with ravving_build_settings(<target>) , their per-target side; the add_subdirectory calls; the generated files ( VERSION , config/plasmarc ) and the install rules of the project as a whole ( data/ , the theme, systemd and WirePlumber drop-ins, the desktop entry and icons) src/backend/CMakeLists.txt ravving_backend , the static backend library ( src/backend/* and src/zynthboxbridge.* ): its sources, its PUBLIC include directories ( src/ , so the app includes backend/xxx.h ; src/backend/ , so its files include each other bare), its PUBLIC link set (the Qt modules, JACK, sndfile, TagLib, zlib, BluezQt), the RAVVING_* compile definitions, the unity build src/CMakeLists.txt ravving , the app: src/*.cpp , the Ravving QML module over qml/ at the repository root (each file's path from there is its resource alias, so the resources stay qrc:/qt/qml/Ravving/qml/… and the module's qmldir stays at build/Ravving ), RAVVING_QML_AOT , the branding resources and the shaders, the link to ravving_backend , the binary's install rule; the binary itself stays at build/ravving setup/CMakeLists.txt ravving-setup , the AppImage's setup program ( build/setup/ravving-setup ) tests/CMakeLists.txt the laptop-side tests, built with -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON Target names, options, output paths and the install layout are those tools/device.sh , tools/build-appimage.sh , tools/static-analysis.sh and tools/build-profile.sh rely on; a new backend class goes into src/backend/CMakeLists.txt , a new QML file into src/CMakeLists.txt 's RAVVING_QML_FILES .

Folder Where What for Settings build/ laptop and device the development loop: tools/device.sh deploy , ctest RAVVING_QML_AOT=OFF , RAVVING_PCH=ON build-release/ device the Store AppImage ( tools/build-appimage.sh , configured there on each run) Release at -O2 (no debug information; binaries stripped at install), RAVVING_QML_AOT=ON , RAVVING_PCH=ON , prefix /usr Neither is ever removed by the tools: device.sh deploy syncs the source with --exclude '/build*' (so its --delete leaves both alone on the device), REMOVE RAVVING and the release check uninstall only what cmake --install put on the system, and the AppImage build clears only its staging trees ( build-release/stage , build-release/appimage ). Keeping them is what keeps builds incremental.

A clean build of 0.2.0, laptop, 4 cores, RelWithDebInfo (the device's settings), 2026-10-10: as it was RAVVING_QML_AOT=OFF + RAVVING_PCH=ON C++ compile (CPU) 829 s 499 s (precompiled Qt headers) QML compile (CPU) 740 s 156 s (bytecode only) qmlcachegen (CPU) 134 s 22 s wall clock 426 s 190 s The device (a Pi 5, 4 cores) takes about as long as the laptop for the same work. RAVVING_QML_AOT (default ON). qmlcachegen compiles each QML file's bindings into C++, which then has to be compiled: on the Pi that was 40 % of a build. OFF keeps the QML precompiled but as bytecode only ( --only-bytecode ): the bindings run in Qt's interpreter and JIT, which is fine to develop with; a release keeps ON ( build-release/ ). RAVVING_PCH (default ON): the Qt headers nearly every file includes (QObject, QString, QVariant, the containers, QDebug, QJsonDocument…) parsed once instead of in each of ~90 files. ccache is used when it is installed ( CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER ): a file compiled before with the same flags comes from its cache (after a reconfigure, switching branches). The device builds at the lowest priority ( nice -n 19 ionice -c 3 in device.sh deploy ): not faster, but a build beside the music does not take the audio's time.

h: A corrupted ninja log rebuilds everything
t: ninja: warning: premature end of file; recovering means build/.ninja_deps was cut short (a build killed mid-run, two builds at once in one folder): ninja then trusts nothing it built and plans every step on every build. ninja -C build -t recompact , then one full build, puts it right (2026-10-10: every laptop build had been doing all 336 steps). Never run two builds in one build folder; let a build finish rather than kill it.

h: Why one header edit recompiled every QML file
t: The QML module is built from the ravving target, and Qt's type registration reads the metadata of every QObject class in that target. Any change to a backend header (machine.h, studio.h…) regenerated it, and with it every QML file's compiled C++: minutes for a one-line change. Fixed by building src/backend (and zynthboxbridge ) as its own static library, ravving_backend , outside the QML module: QML reaches it through context properties ( studio , ravving …), which need no registration, and the one type it registered, Sections (for its LOOP / SONG enum), is now two numbers in Rave.qml ( Rave.sectionsLoop , Rave.sectionsSong ). Touching machine.h then: 157 s and every QML file before, 19 s and no QML after.

tools/build-profile.sh [OUT_DIR] [-- cmake options] builds ravving from clean with clang and -ftime-trace ( RAVVING_TIME_TRACE ) in analysis/build-profile/build (never build/ ), then: analysis.txt , ClangBuildAnalyzer 's report: the slowest files to parse and to compile, the most expensive headers (where they come from, how often), the costliest template sets and functions; trace.json , ninjatracing over .ninja_log : the build's timeline, one lane per job; open it in https://ui.perfetto.dev (or chrome://tracing) to see what holds the four cores up (moc's mocs_compilation.cpp , a slow file at the end, qmlcachegen's steps). The tools: clang (Arch's), ClangBuildAnalyzer and ninjatracing in ~/.local/bin (built from their git checkouts in ~/.local/src ), include-what-you-use from the AUR ( yay -S include-what-you-use ). include-what-you-use : cmake -B analysis/iwyu -DRAVVING_IWYU=ON -DRAVVING_PCH=OFF and build ravving_backend there: each file's compile prints what to add, what to remove and which includes a forward declaration would replace ( analysis/iwyu.log ). Precompiled headers off, or it reports their includes as unused everywhere. Read it with care: it knows no Qt mapping (it would swap <QVariantMap> for Qt's internal <qvariant.h> : ignore those), and it does not see moc's generated code, so it calls a header unneeded where a Q_PROPERTY exposes a pointer to that class ( machine.h 's SoundControls and TrackEffects, devicecontrols.h 's Wifi): moc needs the complete type there. The first pass (2026-10-10) found nothing else to change. Unity builds ( RAVVING_UNITY , the backend only: the app target carries qmlcachegen's and rcc's generated sources, and AUTOMOC's mocs_compilation.cpp stays out of the batches on its own) are there to measure, not on by default: many backend files define file-local constants with the same names ( MaxBars , AuditionMs …), which collide once a batch merges them. What the first profile found (laptop, clean, 182 s): parsing 154 s, optimising and code generation 180 s across 85 files; with precompiled headers only QQuickItem remains an expensive header (4 files, about 1 s each); no single hotspot: the heaviest files are the machines, the exporter and moc's mocs_compilation.cpp (about 15 s each), and the costliest template sets are Qt's containers ( QMap::insert , QList::append ) and QObject::connect .

site/ is the page ravving serves at http://<device>:8098/help/ (the shortcuts, the features and the documentation; site/README.md says how it is made and how to retake a screenshot). It is installed as it is ( install(DIRECTORY site …) , this README left out), so it must be plain static files with relative references, and its documentation pages are generated into the repository: python3 tools/build-site-docs.py # README.md, docs/*.md, data/secret/README.md → site/docs/*.html python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --list # the pages python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --plain # the script's own converter, as on a machine without python-markdown The same run writes site/docs/search.json , the index behind the SEARCH box in every docs page's sidebar (every section, its heading and text): the search runs in the browser alone, so it works on the public page and on the device's own copy without internet. --check (the site-docs-current test) compares the pages and the index with what the markdown gives. The page is public at https://ravving.github.io/: sh tools/publish-site.sh copies site/ (this README left out) into a clone of the ravving/ravving.github.io repository, commits it under the source commit and pushes; that repository's workflow deploys its own content as the Pages artifact on every push. Nothing there needs access to this repository (which may be private) and no secret is kept anywhere. Run it once site/ is committed. The rule (README, "Documentation"): the docs and the page follow every change, in the same commit; python3 tools/build-site-docs.py --check (ctest site-docs-current ) fails when the rendered pages no longer match the markdown. Run it after editing a doc and commit site/docs/ with the markdown. It uses python-markdown when it is installed (Arch python-markdown , Debian python3-markdown ) and its own small converter otherwise; PAGES in the script lists the documents, their groups and blurbs.

ravving reaches a device as an AppImage in the Store's Apps category, the way zynthbox-qml installs any app: the Store downloads the file into ~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/<author>/<name>/ , registers it with libappimage (a desktop entry in ~/.local/share/applications ), extracts it next to itself with --appimage-extract (an <md5>.AppDir ), and from then on launches that AppDir's AppRun from inside zynthbox-qml when the entry is tapped. The bundle is for the Zynthbox device only . It is built on the device, for its architecture, against the Qt, libzynthbox, zyncoder and Zynthbox QML modules the device already has, so it bundles no libraries at all: just ravving, the setup program and the data. In particular the device must have the qml-style-zynthbox package (the Zynthbox QtQuick Controls style ravving selects at startup) and the qml-module-zynthbox package it imports ( io.zynthbox.ui ), as every stock Zynthbox does; see the README's build section for the whole chain. What the AppImage starts is not ravving but ravving-setup ( setup/ ), a page over zynthbox-qml that installs ravving from the bundle and picks which UI the device runs.

The bundle carries no libraries, so what ravving needs from the device is listed in one place, data/requirements.json (installed with the data, and in the bundle), and checked twice: The setup page, before installing ( default-app.sh deps DIR [--install] [--json] , which runs check-requirements.py from the bundle): every requirement, and every library the bundle's ravving links to ( ldd 's "not found"). The page lists what is missing, the feature each costs and the Debian package that brings it, with INSTALL MISSING PACKAGES (apt-get, online). A startup requirement or library missing means ravving cannot start there: TRY IT and MAKE IT THE DEFAULT stay dimmed and the list says why. ravving, once started ( Requirements , four seconds after the first frame): the feature requirements by file and program checks only (no process, microseconds), each missing one a warning in the issues centre: "MUSIC PLAYER will not work", what it costs, the package for the device's admins. What 0.2.0 needs that a Zynthbox image may not have (all on milo; several installed by hand during development): Needed for What How it gets there everything the Qt 6 Zynthbox style ( qt6/qml/Zynthbox ) and QML module ( io.zynthbox.ui ) not packaged yet : built from qml-style-zynthbox and qml-module-zynthbox's dev/qt6-port (the Debian packages are Qt 5) everything Qt Quick Shapes, Virtual Keyboard, Kirigami, KSvg (Qt 6 QML) qml6-module-qtquick-shapes , -virtualkeyboard , qml6-module-org-kde-kirigami , -ksvg starting at all libraries ravving links to: Qt 6 Multimedia, KF6 BluezQt, TagLib 2, LAME, Vorbis, libsndfile libqt6multimedia6 , libkf6bluezqt6 , libtag2 , … ( requirements.json "libraries") MUSIC PLAYER Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend libqt6multimedia6 BLUETOOTH speakers / SEND PipeWire's Bluetooth plugin, BlueZ's obexd libspa-0.2-bluetooth , bluez-obexd (and tools/bluetooth-setup.sh 's service steps) BLUETOOTH, INPUT ravving's WirePlumber settings (A2DP endpoints, one name per sound card) in the bundle ( etc/wireplumber/… ): install puts them in /etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/ , applied from the next start synths, effects, drums jalv, lv2info, FluidSynth, the LV2 plugins and soundfonts the Zynthbox image's own packages SAMPLE KING one-shots libzynthbox's fix for notes cutting each other (exclusivity group −1) not upstream yet (~/Coding/libzynthbox-bug-reports.md): a stock libzynthbox cuts a one-shot when the next starts; not detectable from ravving Adding a feature that needs something new: add it to data/requirements.json (its files, programs, package, the feature and its effect), and to this table.

AppRun nx-apphub's launcher: exec usr/bin/ravving-setup ravving.desktop, ravving.png the entry the Store lists (Name "Ravving", the icon: a 256 × 256 PNG, .DirIcon also .DirIcon, from which libappimage makes the thumbnail zynthbox-qml's Apps grid shows; an SVG one came out blank, 0.2.0's first build) usr/bin/ravving the app usr/bin/ravving-setup the page the AppImage opens usr/share/ravving/ kits.json, engines.json, the presets, requirements.json, check-requirements.py, start.sh, default-app.sh, VERSION usr/share/applications, icons the desktop entry and icon, where they came from etc/systemd/user/ravving.service etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/50-ravving-*.conf Bluetooth, sound card names usr/bin/ravving , usr/share/ravving and the unit are exactly what cmake --install puts on the device: default-app.sh install DIR copies them from the bundle to the system paths.

Four choices, each a default-app.sh command on the bundle's own copy of the script (so the script always matches the files it installs): Choice What it runs Effect TRY IT (LAUNCH RAVVING once installed) install , then run ravving ravving now; Zynthbox at the next boot, or from ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX MAKE IT THE DEFAULT install , then ravving ravving at every boot (zynthbox-qml masked) ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN zynthbox zynthbox-qml at boot; ravving stays installed REMOVE RAVVING (press twice) zynthbox --purge the same, and ravving's program and data leave the system; projects, takes and recordings stay The cards above them (installed version, what starts at boot, what runs now) are default-app.sh status , re-read after every action. The two installing tiles read by what the device has: "Install this bundle and …" with nothing installed, "Update the installed X to this bundle's Y and …" with another version, and "ravving Y is already installed: …" with this one, in which case the install step is skipped (TRY IT then reads LAUNCH RAVVING). A tile that would change nothing is dimmed: MAKE IT THE DEFAULT while ravving already boots, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN while Zynthbox does, REMOVE while nothing is installed. The AppImage itself stays in the Store's list until it is removed there. Switching stops the UI that is running, and with it everything it started: the setup page under zynthbox-qml, or the script itself under ravving's ZYNTHBOX button. The script therefore re-runs the switching commands in a transient unit of its own ( systemd-run --user --wait ) and only then touches the services. run APP switches for the session only (the boot default stays; a masked zynthbox-qml is unmasked for the start and masked again), while ravving and zynthbox change what boots.

The builder is NX AppHub CLI ( nx-apphub-cli build ), the tool the Zynthbox kit's other apps use, driven by packaging/appimage/ravving.yml.in , modelled on the kit's vvave bundle (UriHerrera/storage, AppImages/vvave/app_arm64.yml ): deps is empty, so nothing is downloaded; the zbkit repo entry is the kit's and goes unused; our binaries get into the AppDir through the scripts/ folder next to the YAML, which nx-apphub copies into usr/bin before it looks for binarypath ; the data, desktop entry, icon and unit come from the install staging tree through prebuild-commands ; binarypath and exec are ravving-setup : nx-apphub patches that binary's RPATH (with patchelf; the paths it adds do not exist in this bundle, which is harmless) and writes the AppRun for it; runtime: go (go-appimagetool, a type-2 AppImage that --appimage-extract understands). The tool is an AppImage itself and the device has no FUSE 2, so it runs with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 , and needs ARCH set because AppRun is a script. From the laptop: tools/device.sh appimage [OUT_DIR] # default OUT_DIR ~/Coding/store-packages syncs the source, installs nx-apphub on the device if it is missing ( tools/install-nx-apphub.sh : patchelf and the Python dependencies from Debian, the CLI from its git checkout into a venv), runs tools/build-appimage.sh there and copies ravving-<version>-aarch64.AppImage back. On the device itself: cd /root/ravving && tools/build-appimage.sh dist The version is project(ravving VERSION …) in CMakeLists.txt; it names the file, fills usr/share/ravving/VERSION and shows on the setup page.

Next to the AppImage, the Store listing wants an icon and a gallery: device.sh appimage also renders ravving-icon-512.png from data/icons/ravving.svg (the icon the bundle carries: the 808 plate, the big knob lit in the drums' orange over a step row) into the same output folder; device.sh gallery [OUT_DIR] screenshots each of the five pages of the ravving that is running on the device ( ravving-1-drums.png … ravving-5-sampler.png , 1280 × 800, by the number keys) into ~/Coding/store-packages/gallery/ ; pick three for the page. Load a project worth showing first: the shots are of whatever is on screen.

Every release has its translations reviewed: what changed in po/ and po-site/ since the last release is read by someone who reads the language, the screenshot tour is taken in Spanish and Japanese, and ctest -R translations-current passes (no fuzzy or untranslated text, every placeholder kept, the translated pages rendered). docs/translations.md has the steps.

Run it after any release-worthy change (a version bump, a change to the setup page, the scripts or the unit), from the laptop: tools/appimage-test.sh # build on the device, install like the Store, walk everything tools/appimage-test.sh --no-build # the AppImage already in the device's dist/ tools/appimage-test.sh --keep # leave the entry in the device's Apps list afterwards Run it on a freshly booted device. It switches between the two UIs six times in a few minutes, and after a few walks in a row (2026-10-10, the third) zynthbox-qml hung loading its sketchpad ("Starting engine JV/Helm") and only a reboot cleared it: a Zynthbox / PipeWire wedge after many fast restarts, not ravving's. After a fresh boot the same walk passed. It builds the AppImage ( device.sh appimage ), installs it as the Store would ( tools/store-register.py install , which registers with libappimage, extracts the AppDir and points the desktop entry at its AppRun), checks the AppDir's contents, then walks the page and ravving by touch, asserting default-app.sh status after each step: TRY IT from a purged system: ravving runs, installed is the bundle's version, /usr/bin/ravving is byte for byte the bundle's binary, the boot default is untouched; ravving's POWER → ZYNTHBOX: zynthbox-qml runs; MAKE IT THE DEFAULT: ravving runs and boots, zynthbox-qml is masked; ZYNTHBOX again: zynthbox-qml runs and stays masked for boot; ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN: zynthbox-qml boots, ravving still installed; REMOVE RAVVING twice, CLOSE: nothing of ravving left, the page gone. The page is started with tools/store-launch.sh , which puts it in zynthbox-qml's own service cgroup on the device's display: the exact situation of a Store launch, so a switch that kills zynthbox-qml kills the page too, as in real use. Screenshots and the status after every step go to analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ (eyeball the page shots: dimmed tiles, messages). The user's ravving settings ( ~/.config/ravving ) and live session ( ~/.local/state/ravving ) are copied aside before the walk's purge and put back at the end, a failed step included (a walk without this wiped them, 2026-10-10). Whatever the device had before is put back at the end: a dev install by cmake --install , ravving as the boot default by default-app.sh ravving ; the Store entry is removed unless --keep . A failed assertion stops the run and prints the device's status; the device is then left mid-walk, and tools/device.sh default zynthbox or ravving brings it back by hand.

h: Testing an AppImage without the Store
t: By hand on the device, the pieces the release check uses: tools/store-register.py install dist/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage camiloh "Ravving 0.3.0" # → prints the AppDir; the entry shows in Apps at once tools/store-launch.sh "$APPDIR" # the page, as zynthbox-qml's Apps list would start it tools/store-register.py remove "~/.local/share/zynthbox/apps/camiloh/Ravving 0.3.0/ravving-0.3.0-aarch64.AppImage" ( store-register.py does what registerAppImage / unregisterAppImage in zynthbox-qml's zynthian_gui_main.py do, minus the UI.) Or in zynthbox-qml: SCREEN_MAIN_MENU ( tools/device.sh cuia ), tap Apps, tap Ravving. The page is touch only; tools/device.sh tap X Y drives it: the tiles are the four quarters of the lower half (TRY IT 337 390, MAKE IT THE DEFAULT 943 390, ZYNTHBOX AT BOOT AGAIN 337 600, REMOVE 943 600), CLOSE 1160 736. A desktop look without a device: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen RAVVING_WINDOWED=1 RAVVING_BUNDLE_DIR=<a staged bundle> \ RAVVING_SETUP_SHOT=setup.png ./build/setup/ravving-setup

A stock Zynthbox cannot start bluetooth.service and registers no A2DP endpoints ( docs/bluetooth.md ). cmake --install puts ravving's two drop-ins in place; the packages ( bluez-obexd , libspa-0.2-bluetooth , libkf6bluezqt6 ) and the service restarts are tools/bluetooth-setup.sh 's job, which the setup program should run (or the AppImage's first start), and which --check verifies afterwards.

Every tool used to drive, hear, measure and watch ravving on a Zynthbox, from the laptop. The pieces are small scripts in tools/ ; this page is the recipe book that strings them together. For the first-time set-up (SSH, the build loop) see README.md ; for what each backend piece does, docs/architecture.md ; for the sound and timing checks that were run when a feature was built, docs/debugging.md and docs/quality.md . The rule for every test: iterate with a local build ( tools/device.sh deploy ), never the AppImage; the AppImage and its release check ( docs/packaging.md ) are for minor releases.

Tool What it does tools/device.sh deploy rsync the source, build on the device, install, restart, wait until the audio is wired tools/device.sh cuia NAME… press device keys by CUIA name through the remote-control fifo ( SWITCH_NUMBER_5_RELEASED , SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED , SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED + _RELEASED , SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED = LIVE, KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN , SWITCH_ALT_PRESSED / _RELEASED , SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED ) (object names) a machine key, studio , ravving , input , take , or a dotted path into an object's properties: pads.kit , bass.sound ; any other name is a QML item's objectName ( padsModule , samplerModule , padsWaveEditor , samplerWaveEditor ): set padsModule modifiersExpanded true , call padsWaveEditor open 16 , set ravving currentPage 4 , set ravving samplerMachine 1 ; mouse is the MouseWatcher ( get mouse hasMouse ). QML items are found in the item tree (a page's items are visual children, not always QObject children), popups in the object tree. A QML function is called through the script engine, so its arguments arrive as plain numbers, booleans or text ( call chordsModule moveView 1 , call padsWaveEditor open 16 ); a C++ method gets its arguments converted to the parameter types tools/device.sh set OBJECT PROPERTY VALUE set a backend property ( set pads selectedPad 3 ); plain setters are not reachable by call , properties are tools/device.sh get OBJECT PROPERTY read a backend property ( get pads muted , get studio playing ): ravving logs it, the script reads it back tools/device.sh call OBJECT METHOD ARGS… call a backend method: a machine by its kits.json key ( pads , sampler , drums1 , bass , chords , lead ), studio , input , take , exporter , music (and music.library ), profile , drives (USB sticks: call drives eject /dev/sda1 ), usb (the USB page: call usb scan , call usb importEntry samples /media/root/EVS/x.wav , call usb exportEntry soundfonts /zynthian/…/x.sf2 ; usbPopup opens it: call controlCenter run usb ), bluetooth ( call bluetooth startDiscovery , get bluetooth devices , call bluetooth pair AA:BB:… , call bluetooth useAsOutput AA:BB:… true , call bluetooth sendFile AA:BB:… /path ), or a QML item by objectName ( window showPlayer true , window showRecorder true , exportPopup open , settingsPopup open , bluetoothPopup open , projectPicker open then projectPicker actionTriggered 4 for IMPORT (the index counts the dividers: OPEN 0, EXPORT 1, NEW 2, TEMPLATES 3, IMPORT 4, SAVE AS NEW 6), playerPage , controlCenter ); any Q_INVOKABLE or slot, arguments converted ( call pads loadSample 0 /path.wav , call pads setFlag 0 looping true , call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , call input record , call input record true for a RECORDER take; set input.effects preset OVERDRIVE ; get input.tuner frequency ; call ravving setLogRules "ravving.cuia.debug=true" turns a log category on while running: each key, who took it and the focus chain), video ( set video countdown 0 , call video start / stop / toggle , get video state / lastFile / lastInfo , set video quality high ) and computer ( call computer setup HOST USER PASSWORD 22 , check , send /path , forget ), files (the FILES browser: get files kinds , call files entries videos , call files presetFile "pattern::bass-presets.json::My Bassline 1" ; filesPopup open , filesPopup showKind presets , filesPopup openFolder BASS : the drawer's dialogs open by script only once the MENU drawer has been shown since the start, so press MENU twice first); the journal logs each call tools/device.sh tap X Y a touch at a screen pixel (the panel is 1280 × 800); a hold is xdotool mousemove X Y mousedown 1; sleep 1; xdotool mouseup 1 over ssh with DISPLAY=:0 XAUTHORITY=/root/.Xauthority tools/device.sh shot FILE.png a screenshot, copied here (crop with ImageMagick to read details) tools/device.sh animations every running animation and repeating Timer, with its item, whether it is shown, its QML file and position: what keeps the window drawing (an idle screen should draw nothing) tools/audio-impact.sh [SECONDS] [idle\|playing\|both] what the screen, polls and watchers cost the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime-thread page faults, xruns ( docs/quality.md §10); idle presses nothing, so it is safe while someone plays tools/device.sh gallery [DIR] one screenshot per page tools/device.sh log [SECONDS] ravving's journal tools/device.sh bt [ADDR] [SINCE] / bt capture [SECONDS] [FILE] why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only (tools/bt-diagnose.sh: config, endpoints, codecs, the device's journal and a tally of failures), and an HCI trace with btmon while you connect it (docs/debugging.md, docs/bluetooth.md) tools/device.sh play FILE.mid play a MIDI file into ravving as an external keyboard ( tools/midifile.py makes one) tools/device.sh default … switch between ravving and zynthbox-qml, install, purge, status tools/meter.py (on the device: tools/device.sh tools copies it to /tmp ) pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py PORT --seconds 2 : RMS, brightness and crest of a JACK port tools/record.py , tools/analyse.py , tools/repeatcheck.py record ports to numpy, analyse, check periodicity tools/soundfont.py presets · ranges · render · categorise FILE… look inside an SF2 / SF3 before making it a kits.json sound source ( categorise --json proposes the entries, a category from the name and folder: Strings, Organ, Keys, Bass, Guitar, Winds, Voices, Synth, Alien for the drones, Drums, Other; mute fonts left out): its presets (bank:program), the key and velocity ranges of its zones (a velRange 0–0 font is mute everywhere: SynStrings, LaString, MelloString, Organ on the image), and an offline render of one chord through fluidsynth with the level every quarter second tools/mididump.py PORT SECONDS (on the device, pw-jack python3 ) what an engine really receives on a JACK MIDI port: notes, controllers, program changes, bends (the clock and ticks with --clock ) tools/profile-taps.sh , tools/qml-profile.sh , tools/boot-timing.sh responsiveness, QML profiling, start-up time ( docs/quality.md ) tools/static-analysis.sh clang-tidy / clazy tools/pads-test.sh the PAD SAMPLER feature suite (below) tools/sections-test.sh SECTIONS heard: sections picked at random moments while the master records, tools/sections-test.py checks every 8th sounds once and on time, a change only on a bar line, a rest in whole bars (below) tools/bluetooth-setup.sh [--check] set a device up for Bluetooth (packages, the two drop-ins, services) and check every step ( docs/bluetooth.md ) tools/soundfont-check.sh every soundfont kits.json uses, checked on the device: exists, can sound, the preset exists, a chord comes out offline ( docs/quality.md §7) tools/drums-test.sh the DRUMS page suite (60 checks: 55 on the device, 5 timing checks on the laptop from a recording of the lane): a new project starting clean on every page, the grid (toggle, accent, undo / redo, clear, bars, view bar, cursor and STEP entry), the kit (another loaded, reset), the row mix heard (mute, solo, level, accent, the machine's mute and pause), LIVE (a pad heard, hits recorded while playing), presets (save, load, remove), every SOUND EFFECT on and off with its knobs read back and DRIVE / COMPRESSOR / EQ / PAN heard, the kit's MODS, and tools/hits-timing.py (shared with the chords suite): every 8th within 12 ms, accents louder. It works in a project of its own and puts the previous one back tools/chords-test.sh the CHORDS page suite (54 checks: 50 on the device, 4 timing checks on the laptop): the key and chord sets (names follow ROOT and the set), the CHORDS view (chords, runs, undo / redo, clear), NOTES (toggle, a step's notes, custom voicings), SLOTS (arm, fill, bars, clear, the steps rebuilt), the octave, the sound source (a soundfont, back to TAL), heard (mute, pause, LIVE keys, a hit recorded), presets, every SOUND EFFECT with EQ / PAN / DRIVE heard, and hits-timing.py on two bars of piano stabs (every 8th within 20 ms) tools/video-test.sh the video recorder suite (docs/video.md): a recording over the fifo while playing, its MP4 (streams, starts, length, frame rate), the ring's dropped frames, the graph's xruns meanwhile, RECORD / STOP by the keys, the TIMER and its cancel, VIDEO off tools/share-test.sh [FILE] the phone share (SEND… → PHONE · QR CODE) with the laptop as the phone: the newest video (or FILE) offered over the fifo, its link fetched with curl and compared with the device's file (size, md5), a Range request → 206 of the right length, HEAD, a wrong token and the root → 404, the deliveries counted, the help page at /help/ (200 text/html, its CSS, a missing file and ../ → 404, not an attachment, not counted), the library's pages (openBrowse → the index, a kind's page, a DOWNLOAD link as an attachment, a wrong kind and token → 404, closeBrowse → 404), stop → the link 404 while the help page stays; runs on the laptop (it must reach the device's address, as a phone would) tools/computer-link-test.sh the computer link end to end against the device's own sshd (a throwaway local user as the computer): set-up with the password, the key installed, Downloads found, a wrong password told apart, a file sent, the key removed → refused tools/video-voice-check.sh the voice-over mix of a video: the transport playing, tools/tone.py's 1 kHz bursts into the tap's mic ports as the voice, the file measured second by second (the music DUCK dB quieter while the tone is on, the tone LIFT dB louder); DUCK=18 LIFT=0 for other settings; the device must be idle tools/video-sync-check.sh , tools/video-encode-impact.sh , tools/video-mic-check.sh the video sync mechanism alone; the encoder tiers' cost while playing; a recording with the RECORDER's mic heard and measured tools/export-test.sh the exports and music player suite (below): a project saved, changed and reopened, a short track export (WAV, then FLAC) checked to the sample, its tags and cover, a .ravv bundle and its import, the player's queue, playback, pause, seek and stop tools/examples/lofi-say-it.sh a whole project built by script ( docs/scripting-projects.md ): the recipe for making music over the fifo tools/appimage-test.sh , tools/store-register.py , tools/store-launch.sh the Store AppImage release check ( docs/packaging.md ) Environment switches: QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true" (set with systemctl --user set-environment and a restart) logs every hardware event with whether it was accepted and the focus chain it travelled; ravving.midi.debug=true the MIDI input.

A machine's track after its effects is TrackPassthrough:Channel{track+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft (kits.json gives the track: drums 0–2, bass 3, chords 4, lead 5, SAMPLE KING 6, PAD SAMPLER 7, the input monitor 9); the master is GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft . Always compare runs (silent, playing, silent again), never read a single number: a track playing a beat is ~0.02–0.2 RMS, silence is 0.0.

sh tools/pads-test.sh runs every PAD SAMPLER backend feature as a check on the device (load, one-shot, NOTE ON, LOOP + latch + stopAll, the pattern on both tracks, erase, halve / double, MUTE, copy, a card value, a take with SMART stop when a signal is present, the samplers' exclusivity, the folders), PASS / FAIL / SKIP per line with the measured level, and exits with the number of failures. Run it after any change to the machine, the wiring, the paths or libzynthbox; it needs the reference audio in the library and a kick sample in the device's sketchpads. Add a check for every new feature.

sh tools/sections-test.sh (from the laptop) builds a test project on the device: DRUMS 1 alone, a bar of 8ths at 100 BPM, section A a kick, B a closed hat, REST with DRUMS 1 resting. It records the master while A and B are picked 24 times at random moments (0.6–2.6 s apart: some land, some are replaced before their bar), then A and REST in turn, and tools/sections-test.py checks the recordings by their onsets (a kick is dark, a hat bright): every 8th once (no gap near 600 ms, none under 200), on time (each onset within 15 ms of one grid fitted through them all), the sound changing only on an onset that begins a bar, the rests whole bars from a bar line. What was open before is opened again (saved first when it had changes). 2026-10-09 on milo: 7/7, 152 eighths, 13 changes all on bar lines, every 8th within 13.3 ms of a 299.997 ms grid. Read the timing against the grid, not gap by gap: the detector reads a kick 2.7 ms early and a hat 3.0 ms late (each ±2.6 ms), so a gap across a change carries both errors (one gap read 22.7 ms off in an earlier run while every onset was within 11 ms of the grid).

sh tools/export-test.sh runs the exports and the music player as checks on the device against whatever project is open (27 checks, all passing on milo with "Lo-fi Say It"): the profile's author fallback, a 2-bar WAV export that starts busy, plays the transport, stops it, lasts exactly 2 bars + 1 s at the project's tempo (to the sample), is 24-bit at the engine's rate, carries its tags (python3-taglib reads them back), its cover PNG and a sidecar that says the start was placed on the audio clock ( headFrom: clock ); a 1-bar FLAC; a .ravv bundle (project.json, metadata.json, cover.png, the samples; zip integrity checked by Python) imported as a new project with its sample paths rewritten; the library listing the tracks, playNow sounding on the master (meter.py), the position moving, pause, resume, seek, enqueue, stop. It removes its "Export Test" files (exports, the imported project and its samples) at the end. A track export by hand over the fifo (JSON in one argument; no | inside): ssh root@milo.local "printf '%s\n' 'call|exporter|exportAudio|{\"title\":\"My Track\",\"artist\":\"Me\",\"format\":\"flac\",\"bars\":8,\"loops\":2,\"tail\":2}' > /tmp/webconf-writes-to-this-fifo" tools/device.sh get exporter phase # preparing · recording · cutting · tagging · done tools/device.sh get exporter lastFile

A project names what it plays instead of holding it: each instrument's sound source and factory sound by name, its MODS knobs as "CARD/KNOB", a drum kit or a sample by path, automation lanes by knob. A change to data/kits.json , data/engines.json or the device's files can leave a saved project pointing at nothing, and it then opens on another sound, silently. Three checks catch it: On the laptop, every change of text: sh tools/i18n-extract.sh , translate what it marks, then ctest -R translations-current ( tools/check-translations.py : templates current, catalogs compile, nothing untranslated or fuzzy, placeholders and markup kept, the translated pages rendered). To test a language on the device: device.sh set localization language es ( ja , en , or empty for the system's), then run the page suites in it: a suite that reads a display text instead of a key fails there. On the laptop, every change: ctest -R projects runs tools/check-projects.py over data/demos against the repo's kits.json and engines.json (sources, MODS knobs, automation lanes, kit roles, sections and the song). Over the device's saved projects: tools/device.sh projects ( -v for every project) runs it on milo against the installed data and files too: kit soundfonts, samples (a take saved before the takes moved to samples/takes/ is found there, as ravving finds it), imported soundfonts, the TAL factory sounds. Run it after a data change, before a release. In ravving, each time a project opens: the machines note what they could not resolve as they restore it ( ProjectCheck , Machine::checkSaved() : nothing is read twice, nothing runs after), and the issues centre shows one warning listing it ("5AM: 2 of what it plays is missing"), cleared by the next project that resolves.

h: Recipes › A sampler pad from a script
t: A sampler pad from a script. Load, play, loop, latch, stop: sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/movie-intro-16s.wav sh tools/device.sh call pads audition 0 # one pass sh tools/device.sh call pads setFlag 0 looping true sh tools/device.sh call pads setLatched 0 true # held looping, as a long press does sh tools/device.sh call pads stopAll # what STOP does

h: Recipes › A pattern on the pads
t: A pattern on the pads. Fill pads 1–4 with a kick, snare, hat and clap from the device's library ( find /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/samples -iname "*kick*.wav" | head -1 ), then call pads loadPreset "Boom Bap" , cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED , meter the lane, cuia SWITCH_STOP_RELEASED . The step keys write the selected pad's row with LIVE off and play the pads with LIVE on ( SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED toggles it; a step key held past half a second latches its pad).

h: Recipes › A take into a pad
t: A take into a pad. With something on the input jack ( INPUT sets MIC / GUITAR / LINE): call pads setSelectedPad 2 , then call input record ; with SMART on ( studio.input.autoStop , default on) the take ends by itself half a second after the sound stops, else call input stop . The processed take lands on the pad trimmed to its last burst; the journal shows takeReady . Without a signal the take never auto-stops: that is the guard against stopping before anything was played.

The hardware walk. Switch the trace on, then cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED step by step and read which item accepted each key; ALT + ▲ must land on the header from anywhere. Key 5 opens page 5 and, pressed again, toggles between SAMPLE KING and the PAD SAMPLER; the choice survives restarts, so check the nameplate in a screenshot before sending taps at a panel (a hold on the wrong one writes a step). Reference audio for sampling tests lives in the library: /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/samples/refs/ ( movie.wav and movie-intro-16s.wav from the user's "04 - Movie", nina-free*.wav ); the originals are in ~/Coding/refs/audio/ on the laptop.

Live jam test (to run). After the snippet works alone, build a lo-fi hip hop jam around it: drums, bass, chords and lead with the sampled audio on the pads, recorded with the header's ● into recordings/ , as the thEx jam was made.

tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 checks the PipeWire / JACK graph ravving runs in (rates and periods against the driver's, linked nodes that are not running, the audio threads' priorities, xruns over a minute, the ravving links). docs/routing.md has the map of what ravving wires, the tools (pw-top, pw-dump, pw-dot, jack_iodelay…) and the measurements. tools/issues-test.sh checks the issues center end to end (reports over the fifo, order, dismiss, clear, the drawer card and the dialog).

How ravving was tested while it was built, and the tools in tools/ that do it. Everything here runs from the laptop against the device ( root@milo.local ; set DEVICE= for another). The device's root shell is zsh.

Tool Runs on What it does tools/device.sh laptop deploy, press keys (CUIA), tap, screenshot, play MIDI, read the log tools/midifile.py either write a MIDI file holding a note or a chord, to play in as a keyboard tools/meter.py device level, brightness and crest factor of any JACK ports tools/synthprobe.py device play a scripted note list straight into an engine and record it tools/analyse.py device measure a synthprobe recording: segments and a pitch track tools/lv2probe.sh device try an LV2 effect on a live signal before wiring it in tools/record.py device record JACK ports to a numpy file tools/repeatcheck.py either how exactly a recording repeats at a given length (STUTTER / LOOP) tools/default-app.sh device make ravving the device's UI, or go back to zynthbox-qml ( device.sh default … ) tools/boot-timing.sh laptop time ravving's start by phase over restarts or reboots tools/qml-profile.sh laptop record and summarise a QML profiler trace of a start tools/qml-profile-summary.py laptop read a .qtd trace: self time per type, file and event tools/static-analysis.sh laptop clang-tidy and clazy over src/ tools/bt-diagnose.sh device why a Bluetooth device does (not) connect or play, read-only ( device.sh bt [ADDR] ); device.sh bt capture records an HCI trace tools/audio-impact.sh laptop what the rest costs the sound: frames/s, CPU per thread group, realtime page faults, xruns, idle and playing The quality and performance checks (what to run when, the baselines, the traps met) are in quality.md . sh tools/device.sh tools copies the device-side ones to its /tmp . They need python3-jack and numpy there (installed on milo) and must run under pw-jack : a plain JACK client would start its own jackd.

The service comes back on its own ( Restart=always : startx leaves with 0 even when ravving dies under it, so on-failure never fired; at most 5 starts in 2 minutes). The next start tells the issues center how the run before ended ( src/backend/lastrun.h ): ravving keeps a marker, ~/.local/state/ravving/running , while it runs and removes it on a clean exit (SIGTERM, a normal return); data/start.sh writes last-exit (" ", 128 + n for signal n). A crash (signal 11, 6), a kill (9), a failure (exit 1: often the display went away) or the session ending first (no exit written: X stopped, as on 2026-10-11) each read as such, with the journalctl line to look at. Tested on milo: pkill -SEGV -x ravving → back 3 s later, the issue "ravving stopped unexpectedly" (error); systemctl --user restart ravving → nothing.

Deploy and wait. sh tools/device.sh deploy syncs the tree (not build/ ), builds, installs, restarts the service and returns once the journal says audio and MIDI wired , plus a moment for the window. Keys sent while ravving boots are lost.

Go somewhere and look. sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_NUMBER_3_RELEASED # page 3 (BASS) sh tools/device.sh cuia SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED SWITCH_ARROW_UP_RELEASED sh tools/device.sh tap 255 766 # the bass's DRIVE chip sh tools/device.sh shot /tmp/bass.png # 1280 × 800; crop with PIL to read details The CUIA names are zynthbox's: SWITCH_STEP5_PRESSED / _RELEASED (a step key held, then let go), SWITCH_MODE_RELEASED (LIVE), SWITCH_SELECT_RELEASED , SWITCH_BACK_RELEASED , KNOB0_UP … KNOB3_DOWN (knobs 1–3 and the big one). A step key with LIVE off edits the pattern on release : switch LIVE on (MODE) before using step keys as a test signal, and off again after.

Call a backend method. sh tools/device.sh call pads loadSample 0 /zynthian/…/x.wav , call pads audition 0 , call pads setFlag 0 looping true , call input record : the fifo's call|OBJECT|METHOD|ARGS… line ( src/cuiafifo.h , fields split on | so paths keep their slashes) invokes any Q_INVOKABLE or slot on a machine (by its kits.json key), studio , input or take , converting the arguments; the journal logs each call with its arguments and whether it was found.

h: Recipes › Play notes as a keyboard
t: Play notes as a keyboard. python3 tools/midifile.py /tmp/c2.mid 36 then sh tools/device.sh play /tmp/c2.mid (it goes in through Midi Through, 14:0, which ravving reads like any controller: the bass plays it when it is LIVE, or with nothing LIVE while its page is on screen). A chord: midifile.py /tmp/c.mid 40 52 67 .

Measure a sound. While a note plays ( aplaymidi -p 14:0 /tmp/c2.mid & on the device): pw-jack python3 /tmp/meter.py TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1-dryOutLeft # rms 0.0256 hf 0.001 crest 3.44 Compare runs, never single numbers: an effect off, on, off again (the last run must match the first, or something else changed). hf/rms is brightness, crest falls with saturation or compression. Ports worth knowing: Port What it carries ravving-<machine>:<out> the engine itself ( ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 ) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-dryOutLeft a machine's track after its EQ/compressor/pan (bass: Channel4) TrackPassthrough:Channel{t+1}-lane1-wetOutFx1Left / Fx2 its reverb / delay send ravving-reverb:lv2_audio_out_1 , ravving-delay:outputleft the send effects GlobalPlayback:dryOutLeft the master, before the LIVE FX inserts Measured references: the bass track ~0.026 RMS for a held C2, the drums 0.15–0.17 playing, reverb return 0.04 with a send on. A soloed machine (S) mutes the others' sends too: check the INSTRUMENTS chips before suspecting an effect.

Check the wiring. ssh root@milo.local 'pw-jack jack_lsp -c' lists every connection; follow a machine from its engine: ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 → SynthPassthrough:Synth4 → TrackPassthrough:Channel4-lane1 → AudioLevels:Channel4 → GlobalPlayback , with DRIVE on ravving-bass-drive between the engine and the synth slot. JackWiring logs audio and MIDI wired when every connection it wants exists, or some ports never appeared after 20 s.

Try an engine. Before choosing one, run it alone and probe it: pw-jack jalv -n probe http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/Nekobi & # on the device pw-jack python3 /tmp/synthprobe.py probe:lv2_events_in probe:lv2_audio_out_1 \ --notes "0.2:36:40:0.2 0.8:36:127:0.2 2.6:36:100:0.4 2.9:48:100:0.3" python3 /tmp/analyse.py --segment "plain:0.2:0.4" --segment "accent:0.8:1.0" --track "slide:2.85:3.15" That is how Nekobi's accent threshold (velocity > 90) and its ~60 ms glide on overlapping notes were found.

Try an effect. lv2probe.sh URI SOURCE MIDIFILE sym=val … runs a throw-away copy of an LV2 fed from a port and measures it, one setting per call; DRIVE's calibration (Calf Saturator: input gain, saturation, makeup) came from runs like lv2probe.sh http://calf.sourceforge.net/plugins/Saturator ravving-bass:lv2_audio_out_1 /tmp/n36.mid level_in=16 drive=5 . lv2info URI lists a plugin's ports and ranges; lv2ls | grep -i word finds plugins.

Test a time effect. Record the master after the repeat while holding a pad, then check the repeat: pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py ravving-repeat:out_l --seconds 4.5 & , hold STUTTER ( xdotool mousemove 400 113 mousedown 1; sleep 1.5; xdotool mouseup 1 ; the transport must play), then python3 /tmp/repeatcheck.py --file /tmp/record.npy --bpm 120 --length-steps 1 : ~0 live, 1.000 while held. Dragging a held pad is xdotool mousemove steps of 5 px while the button is down.

Read the saved state. /root/.local/share/ravving/project/session.json is the whole session (the same format as a project): machines (each one's steps or line , bars , kit , sound , effects , level , paused , preset …), bpm , swing , master , liveFx , globalEffects , ui . It is written 1.5 s after a change and on exit. Projects are in /zynthian/zynthian-my-data/ravving/projects/ ( .current names the open one). To check a save/open round trip: copy session.json, SAVE, NEW, open the project again, and compare the two files' machines (a python one-liner; every machine should be identical). A backup of the pre-session layout is in /root/ravving-project-backup-20261005 . From QML, give studio.uiValue() its fallback with ?? (a JS object does not convert to the C++ default), and know that a JS object passed to C++ arrives as a QJSValue ( setUiValue unwraps it, or it would save as null).

Logging. Categories are off by default: ssh root@milo.local 'systemctl --user set-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES="ravving.cuia.debug=true;ravving.midi.debug=true" && systemctl --user restart ravving' sh tools/device.sh log 30 ravving.cuia prints every key with where it landed ( accepted / unhandled ) and the focus chain; ravving.midi every external MIDI message. systemctl --user unset-environment QT_LOGGING_RULES turns them off again.

Screenshots without the device. RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=dir RAVVING_STYLE=Basic RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/ravving captures every page and a few scripted states (src/main.cpp: add a step there, and find items by objectName with findItem() ). It also shows QML warnings: a clean run prints nothing.

Check the audio input. Read both channels while someone plays or touches the plug's tip (a finger on a working input hums around −30 dBFS; an open one sits near −75): pw-jack python3 /tmp/record.py "Built-in Audio Stereo:capture_FL" --seconds 10 --save /tmp/l.npy amixer -c 3 sset "ADC Left Capture Source" "VINL1[SE]" # try the ADC's other inputs Two cards are called "Built-in Audio Stereo" (the HiFiBerry and a Dummy, always −180 dBFS), and which one gets the number suffix ( capture_FL-92 ) changes between boots : check with pw-dump (the port alias names the card) or ravving's journal line input ports . ravving finds them itself ( InputPorts ).

h: Recipes › Why a Bluetooth device does not connect or play
t: Why a Bluetooth device does not connect or play. Read-only, nothing is connected or restarted, so it is safe while someone listens: sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 # one device; no address: every known one sh tools/device.sh bt 6C:5A:B5:49:35:D8 -1d # only the last day of the journals sh tools/device.sh bt capture 60 /tmp/lg.snoop # btmon for 60 s: connect the device meanwhile btmon -r /tmp/lg.snoop | less # or open it in Wireshark The report has the adapter and main.conf , the A2DP endpoints PipeWire registered (one per codec, shared by every device), WirePlumber's Bluetooth drop-ins, the PipeWire Bluetooth objects (card, sink, codec) and ravving's loopback, then per device its record (keys hidden), its cached A2DP endpoints decoded (which codecs it takes), the bluetoothd / WirePlumber / ravving journal lines and a tally: link up, Unable to select SEP , create-socket, page-timeout, profile-unavailable, A2DP transports opened. What each failure means, and the LG-vs-Sony case it was written for, is in bluetooth.md ("One audio device at a time"). In a capture, a page that is never answered shows as Create Connection followed by Connect Complete … Page Timeout ; a link refused for lack of an endpoint shows the AVDTP Discover / Get Capabilities and then a disconnect with no Set Configuration .

zsh does not split $var into words: pass a stored argument list as ${=var} . pkill -f / pgrep -f with a pattern that also matches the ssh command line kills or finds the shell itself. jalv over ssh without pw-jack starts a real jackd and breaks the session's audio. The machine finishes in Rave.machines are colour strings : .r/.g/.b are undefined (the colour silently comes out black or transparent). Type them first: readonly property color glow: finish.glow . An Item delegate in a Layout needs implicitHeight (from its content), or the layout gives it nothing and its neighbours take the room. A property int x: other meant as "the previous value" is a binding: it may update before the change handler reads it. Set it in Component.onCompleted instead. Hardware events start at the focused item and bubble: a page that moves a selection on ▲ must first check whether the event came from its strip ( stripFocused ). A QQC ComboBox takes the focus for good when tapped: use RaveComboBox . Nekobi's output is quiet (−32 dB RMS): a saturator needs input gain to bite. After a restart the window maps a few seconds after wired ; a screenshot taken earlier is black. amixer reads a negative value as an option ( -4.5dB ): put -- before sset . A popup's QQC.Overlay.modal must be set on the popup itself: on the ApplicationWindow it does nothing with the Zynthbox style. A style-made popup (a ComboBox's list) cannot be given one: draw a ModalDim in the overlay under it. Machines' sends leave the track lane before AudioLevels' gain: a VOL that should silence the echoes has to scale the sends too.

The checks to run on ravving every so often (and before a release), what each tool is for, what the last run found, and the traps met on the way. All the tools live in tools/ ; the laptop ones need no libzynthbox (ravving builds without it), the device ones run against root@milo.local ( DEVICE= for another). When Run Look at after C++ changes tools/static-analysis.sh new lines in analysis/summary.txt against the baseline below after changes to a shell script ( tools/*.sh , data/start.sh ) tools/static-analysis.sh shell (ShellCheck, here or on the device) analysis/shellcheck.log : the scripts are kept at zero findings; a finding that is the script's intent (a remote command built on the laptop, a deliberate word split) gets a # shellcheck disable= line with the reason above it after adding a pointer handler (Tap / Drag / Pinch / Point / Wheel) to a page or the header tools/static-analysis.sh handlers zero: each binds enabled: … !Session.inputBlocked , else a drag on a dialog reaches it (§1, "Handlers under dialogs") after QML changes the screenshot tour (below) QML warnings in its output; pixel diffs against a reference tour after anything that touches startup tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 the medians against the table below before a release tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 , tools/qml-profile.sh boot to first frame; what QML creates before it after any UI, animation, poll or watcher change, and in every phase pass tools/audio-impact.sh (§10) idle 0 frames/s; playing ≈ the playhead and meter rates; 0 RT-thread faults from ravving's own code; 0 xruns

tools/static-analysis.sh # both; or `tidy` / `clazy` alone It configures a separate build folder with a compile database ( BUILD , default /tmp/ravving-analysis ; the normal build/ is never touched), generates moc and the QML type registration, then runs clang-tidy with the repo's .clang-tidy and clazy (levels 0–2 without the Qt-idiom noise listed in the script) over src/ only, in parallel. Reports go to REPORTS (default ./analysis ): clang-tidy.log , clazy.log and summary.txt , one count per check. Arch packages: clang (clang-tidy, run-clang-tidy) and clazy . A newer clang-tidy brings new checks: decide for each whether it finds something or restates the house style, and turn the latter off in .clang-tidy with a line saying why.

tools/static-analysis.sh shell runs ShellCheck 0.10 at -S style over every shell script. The first run found 42 things (the suite's $? after A && B , unquoted xrandr arguments in start.sh, a stray unused variable, A && B || C used as if-then-else); all fixed or justified in place, so the baseline is 0 . ShellCheck is on milo ( apt install shellcheck ); on a laptop without it the script sends the files there.

A sideways drag on the EXPORT or USB dialog paged the chords roll underneath (bar 1 → 4, reproduced on milo with xdotool). The modal dimmer stops items, not pointer handlers: Qt Quick still hands the press to every handler under it after the dialog's button or field took it, and BarSwipe's DragHandler then takes the drag over past its threshold. Disabling the page while a dialog is up was tried and dropped: a disabled ComboBox closes its own list at once, so the drop-downs (ROOT, SCALE, CHORD SET) stopped opening. What stays: the modal layers (dialogs, the MENU drawer, a drop-down's list) register in Session.overlays by identity (a repeated open cannot leave the page blocked), and every handler on a page or the header binds enabled: !Session.inputBlocked (five of them). tools/check-handlers.py ( static-analysis.sh handlers , also in all ) fails on a new one that does not; it found the five before the fix. Measured after: drags from the dialogs' fields, buttons, rows and blank parts, the drawer and a drop-down's list move nothing below; the page pages again after each and the focus is back on it.

h: The baseline (2026-10-05, clang-tidy / clazy on LLVM 23)
t: What is left is known and accepted; anything not in this list is new and worth reading. Check Count Why it stays bugprone-implicit-widening-of-multiplication-result 12 soundfont record offsets ( index * Size ) and the track lanes: int-sized files and lists bugprone-signed-bitwise 11 MIDI status / channel and LED colour byte masks on int ; values are 0..255 bugprone-incorrect-roundings 3 int(x + 0.5) on frame counts, which are never negative bugprone-multi-level-implicit-pointer-conversion 2 jack_free(ports) and QMetaObject's void * arguments: the C APIs' own types bugprone-inc-dec-in-conditions 1 m_editGroup > 0 && --m_editGroup == 0 : the decrement is meant to be guarded readability-redundant-nested-if 1 LiveFx: the two conditions read as two decisions clang-analyzer-cplusplus.NewDeleteLeaks 1 false: the QFutureWatcher is parented to the machine and deleteLater() s itself clazy range-loop-detach 24 loops over temporaries ( toList() , split() ) on load paths; a member list looped often would be worth fixing (DrumKit::rows() was) clazy writing-to-temporary 2 QSettings(...).setValue() : the temporary's destructor writes it clazy connect-non-signal 2 clazy cannot follow a for over signal pointers (Studio); its own message calls it a clazy bug clazy qproperty-without-notify 1 HardwareEvent::accepted: a per-event object, never bound

Machine::stepTicks() : integer division multiplier / 32 (exact only while libzynthbox's BeatSubdivisions is a multiple of 32) is now / 32.0 . The four machines are final : their constructors call their own restoreContent() , refresh() and revoice() , which is exact only while nothing derives from them. DrumKit::rows() returns a const reference: ten loops in DrumMachine iterated a copy of the kit's rows (clazy range-loop-detach). Uninitialised jack_status_t and loop counters, QJsonValue / QString loop copies in InputPorts, a const local that blocked a return move, by-value std::function , #include <QtConcurrent> (the whole module) → <QtConcurrentRun> , an unnormalised Q_ARG , mismatched parameter names, four last-use copies now moved.

main() writes the phases of a start to the journal ( src/startuptimer.h ): ravving: startup main 0 ms process up (after startx, X and the binary loading) ravving: startup application 18 ms QGuiApplication ravving: startup libzynthbox 649 ms libzynthbox's singletons and engines ravving: startup studio 2922 ms machines, effects, the session (Studio) ravving: startup qml 3681 ms Main.qml created ravving: startup first-frame … the first frame on screen ravving: startup wired … audio and MIDI connected tools/boot-timing.sh restart 5 # service restarts: CSV + medians, ms from the service starting tools/boot-timing.sh reboot 3 # reboots (ravving the default UI): also kernel boot → first frame tools/boot-timing.sh last # the last start, without restarting anything Compare medians, never single runs: the first frame moves by up to 3 s between runs because kwin starts beside ravving ( start.sh ) and the window is not shown before kwin manages it.

Median Before After (BASS restored) After (DRUMS restored) restart: service start → first frame 6709 ms 4937 ms (−26 %) 5596 ms (−17 %) restart: QML (studio → qml) 2068 ms 695 ms (−66 %) 1211 ms (−41 %) restart: qml → first frame 1178 ms 765 ms 888 ms reboot: kernel boot → first frame 17.28 s 14.67 s (−2.6 s) reboot: service start → first frame 11013 ms 9168 ms Since only the page on screen is built first, the start now depends on the page the session restores: DRUMS is the heaviest (all three drum machines' step grids, 864 KeyCaps), BASS a typical one. Before, every page was built whatever the page, so "before" holds for both. Compare runs on the same restored page ( "page" in the session.json: 0 drums … 4 sampler).

h: Before and after (milo, Raspberry Pi 5, 2026-10-05) › Restart sparingly
t: Restart sparingly. Every restart stops and starts the HiFiBerry's PCM, and after a few dozen in a session milo's RP1 audio DMA driver oopses ( dma2chan4 , a use-after-free; the device reboots itself; see the Zynthbox bug log). Prefer 3–5 runs per measurement, and take boot-timing.sh last after a start that happens anyway. Then the LV2 port cache (below) took the C++ side down too: Median Before With the cache restart: studio phase (libzynthbox → studio) 2292 ms 877 ms (−1.4 s) restart: service start → first frame 5596 ms (DRUMS) 3502 ms (LEAD) one cold boot: kernel boot → first frame 14.67 s 14.11 s What made the difference (from the QML profile, below): 1. Only the page on screen is built before the first frame (Main.qml's PageLoader ): the other four pages and the mixer are built one per 40 ms tick once the first frame is up. main.cpp restores the page before loading the QML, so the first page built is the right one. 2. KnobBadge builds its drawing on first show ( shown , not visible ): 1436 badges were created at startup, nearly all hidden. 3. The LV2 ports are cached on disk (JalvPlugin::readPorts, ~/.cache/ravving/lv2-ports.json ): lv2info ran synchronously for each of the 8 plugins built at start (70–80 ms each, 561 ms for TAL-NoiseMaker: ~1 s). Each entry carries its bundle's and binary's modification times; an installed or upgraded plugin no longer matches and is asked again. Delete the file to force a full re-read.

studio is ~0.9 s now (was 2.3 s before the LV2 port cache). The input ports' pw-dump (~0.18 s, synchronous, InputPorts) is the next piece to move off the start. The Zynthbox style's QML is compiled at every start (~200 ms "Compiling" in the profile): qml-style-zynthbox ships no qmlcachegen output. Cold boots spend ~3 s from the service starting to main (X and kwin from SD). DrumsPage builds all three drum machines although one shows (its panels Repeater): the other two could follow the PageLoader pattern, ~0.5 s off a DRUMS start. Mind the panels.count > 0 ? panels.itemAt(…) binding in DrumsPage (§3).

Every font in the library's soundfonts/ folder is read at start: its preset list becomes sources for bass, chords and lead, and its sample names a drum kit when they give three roles. The journal says what it cost: ravving: kits N ms, imported soundfonts: F fonts, S sources, M ms (also after a USB import, refreshImported ). Only the preset list ("pdta") is read, found by walking the RIFF chunk headers ( SoundFontFile::presetData ). Two of three SF3 files tried leave an odd-sized sdta chunk unpadded, which broke the first walk and fell back to reading the last 8 MB of each font. The walk now steps over an unpadded chunk too. Measured on milo with three imported fonts (Guitars Universal 1.4, FluidR3Mono_GM, jRhodes4: 43 MB, 263 sources), caches dropped before each of three restarts: the scan studio step start → wired no imported fonts 2 ms 1474 ms 5156 ms 3 fonts, 8 MB tail read 195 ms ~+300 ms 3 fonts, chunk walk 17 ms 1503 ms 5144 ms So imported fonts cost nothing measurable at start; the scan's line in the journal is the check after adding a font whose writer is new.

h: An A/B before blaming a change (2026-10-09)
t: Start → wired read 7.9–8.1 s on milo, against the 5.1 s above, after SECTIONS phase 1. The build from before the day's work (6fda638, from a git worktree , deployed, three cold starts on the same project and page) gave the same 7.85–8.0 s: the time went with the device's state, not with the code. The QML step on the DRUMS page grew from 1.2 to 3.4 s in both, which is where to look next. The rule: compare against an old build on the same day, project and page before calling a slower start a regression.

h: Deploying to measure: the mtime trap
t: rsync -a keeps the laptop's modification times. A file edited on the laptop before the device last built another tree (the baseline) arrives older than that build's objects, and ninja skips it: the binary mixes old and new objects. Changing a header's ABI that way ( DrumKit::rows() by value → by reference) crashed ravving at start in a later, partial rebuild. Sync with rsync -rlp --checksum (no times: changed files get the device's clock), or find src qml -exec touch {} + on the device before building after switching trees.

tools/qml-profile.sh NAME # ./NAME.qtd and ./NAME-summary.txt tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --type Creating --top 40 tools/qml-profile-summary.py NAME.qtd --from 2 --to 4 A systemd drop-in sets RAVVING_QML_DEBUG=10002,block : main.cpp opens the QML debug server and waits for qmlprofiler before loading any QML; the script attaches on the device, waits for startup wired , flushes the trace, then removes the drop-in and restarts ravving. The summary lists self time per event type, per file and per event: look at Creating first (how many of what were built) and the call counts (1436 calls of one component is the finding, not its 0.1 ms each). Never probe the debug port by connecting to it: the server takes the first connection as its client.

StackLayout's attached properties are not ready during creation : StackLayout.index reads −1 and isCurrentItem flips while the layout adopts its items.
