A Loader keyed on them built every page, then destroyed and built them again. Give each page its index. Asynchronous Loaders break the count / itemAt() idiom : an incubating Repeater reports its count before its items exist, and bindings like panels.count > 0 ? panels.itemAt(i) : null settle on null for good (silently: no error). The pages are therefore built synchronously, spread over ticks. A model reset rebuilds every delegate : a periodic refresh that re-sorts (the Wi-Fi scan) took the text being typed and the keyboard's layout with it. Freeze the order while a row is open (WifiNetworks::frozen, plasma-nm's DelayModelUpdatesRole). A tap on the on-screen keyboard is a press outside a popup : dialogs and the drawer must not close on outside presses while Qt.inputMethod.visible ; a button next to a text field must not take the focus ( focusPolicy: Qt.NoFocus ), or the keyboard hides.

RAVVING_STYLE=Basic QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 RAVVING_NO_ZYNTHBOX=1 \ RAVVING_DATA_DIR=$PWD/data RAVVING_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/tour/project RAVVING_SCREENSHOT_DIR=/tmp/tour/shots \ build/ravving 2>&1 | grep -v -i jack It visits every page and a few dialogs, saves PNGs and quits (main.cpp). Start from an empty project folder each time (the tour turns knobs, and the session keeps them), build the reference from the previous commit the same way, and compare with compare -metric AE ref.png new.png null: (ImageMagick). QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING matters: without a terminal Qt logs to the journal and the run looks silent. The Zynthbox style is not on the laptop, hence RAVVING_STYLE=Basic .

tools/device.sh default ravving # or on the device: /usr/share/ravving/default-app.sh ravving tools/device.sh default status tools/device.sh default zynthbox # back to stock; add --purge to uninstall ravving too default-app.sh masks zynthbox-qml in root's user units (a --user disable cannot undo its global enable in /etc/systemd/user , and updates re-enable it globally; the mask wins over both) and enables ravving. Going back unmasks and starts zynthbox-qml, disables and resets ravving, and drops the development environment ( RAVVING_GDB , RAVVING_QML_DIR ).

h: 6. The Store AppImage: the release check
t: tools/appimage-test.sh builds the AppImage on the device, installs it the way the Store does and walks every choice of the setup page and ravving's ZYNTHBOX button by touch, with an assertion on the device's state after each step. Run it after a version bump or any change to setup/ , tools/default-app.sh , data/ravving.service or packaging/ . About eight minutes; results in analysis/appimage-test-<date>/ . Details in packaging.md .

h: 7. Soundfonts and engines: when one is added
t: sh tools/soundfont-check.sh (on the device, from the laptop) takes every soundfont data/kits.json names (the drum kits, the machines' default engines, every FluidSynth sound source) and checks each: the file exists, its zones can sound (a font whose instrument zones declare a velocity range of 0–0 is mute at any velocity: SynStrings, LaString, MelloString and Organ.sf3 on the image are such, and were dropped), the preset the entry asks for (bank:program) exists in the font, and a chord rendered through fluidsynth offline on that preset (a kick, snare and hat for a kit, low notes for a bass, three seconds for pads that swell slowly) actually comes out. PASS / FAIL per font, exit status = failures; 35 of 35 pass on milo (2026-10-07). Run it after editing the sources in kits.json, after an image update (the fonts live in /zynthian/zynthian-data/soundfonts ), and before a release. Behind it, tools/soundfont.py (presets · ranges · render · categorise) looks inside one font and proposes kits.json entries for new ones ( categorise --json ), and tools/mididump.py shows what an engine's JACK MIDI port really carries, for a source that stays silent in ravving but sounds offline ( docs/testing.md ). A new engine type (a SoundEngine subclass) gets the same treatment: its sources into kits.json, the check run, and a pw-top look at its nodes' rate and quantum against the graph's (48000 / 256 on the device).

zynthbox-qml keeps pipewire-pulse off because a Qt Multimedia stream once cost latency. ravving's music player needs it (Qt's audio output on Linux is PulseAudio), so the unit wants it, and the cost was measured with pw-top -b -n 2 on milo, idle, with an MP3 playing, and with the MP3 plus the transport: the driver ( alsa_output.platform-soc… ) stays at quantum 256 / 48000 in all three, its xrun count stays put (3159 before and after), and only the player's own node runs at its larger adapted quantum (1680 frames, 48000). The graph's rate is pinned ( clock.allowed-rates = [ 48000 ] ), so a 44.1 kHz file cannot switch it either. Re-measure the same way after a PipeWire update.

h: 9. The audio graph: routing, clocks and xruns
t: When an engine, insert or route is added or changed, and in every phase pass: tools/device.sh graph all -s 60 # rates, idle-but-linked nodes, threads, xruns over 60 s, the links Expected on a Zynthbox: the driver is the sound card's playback node at 48000 / 256; every ravving-* audio node at 48000 with a period of 256 (jalv) or 512 (FluidSynth's stream, by design); no node with links that is not running; 0 xruns in 60 s, idle and with the reference project playing (run it twice, once with device.sh cuia SWITCH_PLAY_RELEASED first). Any steady xrun rate means a stall somewhere: the first thing to check is systemctl --user show-environment for RAVVING_GDB=1 (gdb costs 20–40 a minute), then graph-check.py threads for a render thread without realtime priority or one above PipeWire's data loops. What each column means, the tools behind it and the numbers measured so far are in docs/routing.md .

h: 10. What the rest costs the sound
t: The sound comes first on this device: a feature, a poll, a watcher or an animation may not cost the audio anything it can hear. ravving's audio threads run at realtime priority, so other work cannot preempt them directly; what it can do is load the CPUs and the memory bus they share, stall a cycle with a page fault on a realtime thread, or hold a lock the audio side needs. Measure it, before and after: tools/audio-impact.sh # 30 s idle, then 30 s with the transport playing tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle # only the idle window (no keys pressed: safe while someone plays) tools/device.sh animations # what keeps the window drawing, item by item audio-impact.sh prints, per state: the frames per second the window put on screen ( Ravving.framesSwapped , counted on the render thread), CPU in % of one core for the render thread, the GUI thread, ravving's realtime threads (policy FIFO / RR: the JACK clients, SyncTimer, MidiRouter…) and the rest, the page faults the realtime threads took, and the graph's xruns over the window ( graph-check.py xruns , summed over the nodes: one graph-wide dropout counts once per node). playing presses PLAY and STOP: never run it while someone plays; idle only reads. What healthy looks like (milo, Pi 5, the Lo-fi Say It project, 2026-10-08): idle playing frames/s 0 16 (the 16ths' playhead and the 10 Hz meters) render / GUI thread 0 % / 3 % 13 % / 15 % realtime threads 14 % 20 % RT page faults / 20 s 0–2 (PipeWire's own data loops) ~85, all in libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread (below) xruns 0 0

h: Found and fixed on 2026-10-10 › Hidden pages followed the playhead
t: Hidden pages followed the playhead. The five instrument pages stay built in their StackLayout, and every grid's cells bound to the step playing, so the pages not on screen re-evaluated their cells on every 16th. A grid (PianoRoll, ChordRoll, StepGrid), the samplers' play position and the SONG page's section progress now read the step only while visible . Measured, 20 s playing on the LEAD page (milo, an unsaved project): GUI thread 14 % → 9 % , render 8 % and realtime 19 % unchanged, 0 xruns.

The screen drew every vsync with nothing moving (65 frames/s idle, 39 % of a core on the render thread). Three hidden button shadows in the header each held an OpacityAnimator inside a Behavior that never finished: an Animator runs on the render thread, and on an item that is not shown it never completes, so Qt Quick keeps rendering frames for it. The Zynthbox style (qml-style-zynthbox, and the copies in qml-module-zynthbox) now uses NumberAnimation in every such Behavior . Idle went to 0 frames/s and 0 % . zynthbox-qml uses the same style: it gains the same. Playing drew every vsync too (65 frames/s, render 58 %, GUI 26 %): a 60 ms fade on the playhead wash of every step key at every 16th, on every grid including the hidden pages', an 80 ms smoothing animation on the master meter restarted at every 100 ms reading, and the samplers' playheads republished at every audio block. The playhead wash is instant, the meter has no Behavior, the playheads publish at 15 Hz ( PlayPositionMs ): 16 frames/s, render 13 %, GUI 15 % , sound unchanged (0 xruns either way). The background polls cost the audio nothing measurable : the USB poll forks lsblk every 2 s at all times (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, address and vitals poll only while the drawer is open), yet ravving's 24 realtime threads took 0 page faults over 30 s idle: Qt starts processes without copying the parent's memory into the audio threads' way. Keep it that way: a new poll is measured with this tool before it ships. The xrun warning fired on every start (the issues center): the graph rebuilds as clients and links come and go, and the engines load their sounds for seconds after registering. BeatRepeat now leaves out xruns within 3 s of a client or link change and during the first 20 s; a stall without a graph change still counts (checked by stopping ravving for 200 ms seven times: 7 dropouts reported).

An idle screen draws nothing. Before shipping UI work, tools/audio-impact.sh 20 idle must read 0 frames/s; if not, device.sh animations names the item. No Animator (Opacity/Scale/Rotation/XAnimator…) inside a Behavior : use NumberAnimation . No Behavior on something the transport changes at every step or every meter reading: those values change instantly. Anything fed by the audio side (positions, levels) is published at the rate the eye needs (15 Hz for a moving line, 10 Hz for meters), never per audio block. An infinite animation ( loops: Animation.Infinite ) runs only while its state lasts (a take waiting, a latched pad) and only while its item is shown. A poll that forks or blocks runs only while what it feeds is on screen, unless it watches for something that has to be noticed at once (a USB stick); measure it with this tool.

libzynthbox's SyncTimerThread (FIFO 99, the sequencer clock) takes ~4 minor page faults a second while playing: it touches memory that has not been mapped yet (a growing buffer or a fresh allocation) on a realtime thread. Not ravving's code; to check whether zynthbox-qml shows the same and to report upstream ( ~/Coding/libzynthbox-bug-reports.md ). The GUI thread's 15 % while playing is mostly the hidden pages following the playhead (every grid's 16 keys re-evaluate at every step); giving hidden pages no playhead would roughly halve it.

Views fed a plain list (a QVariantList from the backend, a JS array) rebuild every delegate whenever the list is set again; on the Pi a row with a Zynthbox Button costs ~1.4 ms to make (five SVG frames). The long or often-updated lists now go through KeyedListModel (src/, tests in tests/: cmake -DRAVVING_TESTS=ON build && ctest --test-dir build ): a new list is applied as the fewest row changes, matched by a key; the longest also set reuseItems . Measured with AFTER=script tools/qml-profile.sh (an interaction: the USB page's takes folder, two re-scans, the presets folders, the kit picker and a favourite toggled twice): before after Creating 212 ms, 5130 objects 135 ms, 3550 Javascript 213 ms 159 ms Binding 147 ms 96 ms USB rows made 92 42 (only the folders opened; a re-scan makes none) Buttons made 170 120 Trap met: a model whose roles were replaced by each list's fields reset itself whenever the USB page went from folders to files and back (a reset rebuilds everything): the roles only grow now, and a test keeps it so. Use KeyedListModel for any list that is long or updated often; small fixed lists (the banks, the kinds) stay plain.

h: Needs the device and the user
t: Sound stalled on Bluetooth headphones after a new drum sound (user, 2026-10-12 05:07, Sony WH-CH720N, SBC-XQ): the DRUMS 2 engine restarted twice in 13 s (a GM soundfont drum), then silence, no issue reported, no PipeWire / bluez line in either journal; picking the output again (speakers, then the headphones) brought it back. Found: with Bluetooth as the output the jacks' ALSA sink was suspended (the master was unlinked from it), so the bluez sink (priority.driver 1010) was the graph's driver, against AudioOutputs' own design (the HiFiBerry, 10000, is meant to keep the clock). A Bluetooth transport that stalls as the driver stalls the whole graph silently. Fix applied the same day: the jacks stay linked and are MUTED (wpctl set-mute) while another output plays, so they keep the clock ( AudioOutputs::setJacksMuted ). VERIFIED live the same hour by hand (wpctl set-mute 59 1 + pw-link of the master to the jacks while the headphones played): the jacks sink took the clock back (pw-top: alsa_output the driver, the input and bluez following), the input's xrun counter stopped, and the user heard the samplers' mic clean again (it had been "awful": the mic's ALSA input was the graph's driver, 248 xruns). If it stalls again: tools/device.sh graph links , pw-top -b -n 2 and the bluez node's state from pw-dump BEFORE re-routing, then consider an OUTPUT STALLED watchdog (the bluez node leaving running while the transport plays → a notice and a re-route).
